title: Ravenous Book Launch
location: Ben McNally Books
description:
[at Ben McNally Books]
Join us at Ben McNally Books, in partnership with Fernwood Publishing, to celebrate the launch of
Ravenous: A Novel
, by Sara Cooper.
Order a copy of
Ravenous
here.
About the Book
Breigh is a hot elder millennial who is obsessed with the brands she is ambassading for. Her policy is YES, and her livestreams are viral. But she’s pregnant now, and her body’s changing. It's not that she's hungry. She's definitely not depressed. She just sometimes eats boxes of makeup before passing out.
Daddy’s bought a brand-new home for Breigh and Baby, complete with a Greenguard Gold-certified, twice-imported velvet infant chaise — but is he cheating on her with a hotter, younger coworker? Breigh has to get Baby out before it ruins her. She has to create more and better content than the other Momfluencers. She has to unbox something new. She has to unbox … Baby! Baby approves of her seven-step marketing plan. Welcome to #LiveBirth.
Breigh’s increasingly unhinged life reflects her generation’s anxieties around psychological manipulation through social media platforms. Multi-award-winning author Sara Cooper presents a wild debut novel in this incisive satire of consumerism, performative femininity, and social media.
About the Author
Sara Cooper is a novelist and playwright-lyricist whose work blends dark humor, psychological insight, and sharp cultural critique. She is the author of Dead Center and Ravenous, both of which were finalist for the Tucson Festival of Books Literary Awards (2025 and 2026). Her theatre work has received awards and honours from the American Academy of Arts and Letters, American Theatre Wing, New York State Council on the Arts, National Alliance for Musical Theatre, and ASCAP. She holds an MFA from New York University’s Graduate Musical Theatre Writing Program and currently teaches at Purchase College and NYU. Learn more at saracooper.me.

🎃 Free Movie Night: [REC] — Just in Time for Halloween!

Join us Friday, October 2 at Innis Town Hall for a FREE screening of the 2007 Spanish horror classic [REC].

A television reporter and her cameraman follow a group of firefighters into an apartment building after receiving an emergency call. What starts as a routine assignment quickly turns into a terrifying nightmare when the building is sealed off—and something inside begins attacking the residents.

If you like found-footage horror, zombies, claustrophobic thrillers and movies that make you yell at the screen, this one is for you!

title: A World of One Heart – Peace and Sustainability
location: Jane Mallett Theatre,Toronto Centre for the Arts, 27 Front St E, Toronto, ON M5E 1B4, Canada
description:
✨ A Spectacular Cultural Performance Comes to Toronto for the First Time! ✨

Experience four cultural performances in Toronto from October 2–4, 2026, presented as part of the international celebration of the 60th Anniversary of Tai Ji Men Qigong Academy.

Offered as a complimentary community cultural initiative and a gift to the community, these performances blend qigong, martial arts, music, dance, and contemporary performing arts to bring timeless wisdom to life through inspiring artistic storytelling, celebrating cultural heritage while sharing the universal values of love, peace, and conscience.

Tai Ji Men’s internationally acclaimed cultural performances have been presented at renowned venues around the world, including the Sydney Opera House (Australia), Pasadena Civic Auditorium (USA), and Luckman Fine Arts Complex (USA). We are delighted to bring this inspiring cultural experience to Toronto for the very first time.

The performances are presented by Tai Ji Men (Canada), an independent Canadian non-profit organization committed to enriching communities through holistic education, cultural exchange, and well-being initiatives.

title: Killer B Cinema Presents: Srigala!
location: See-Scape,347 Keele St, Toronto, ON M6P 2K6, Canada
description:
On Friday, October 2nd, join us for the Indonesian Friday the 13th! Where summer camp is still dangerous!

Advanced tickets are $5 (plus Eventbrite service fee); tickets at the door are $8 (Space is limited, and tickets sell out fast)!

Doors open at 7:30 pm, and the movie begins at 8:00.

Ticket link: https://www.eventbrite.ca/e/killer-b-cinema-presents-srigala-tickets-1999863321028?aff=oddtdtcreator https://www.eventbrite.ca/e/killer-b-cinema-presents-srigala-tickets-1999863321028?aff=oddtdtcreator

*NO outside food or drinks; please buy food and drinks from the venue.

*All films have closed captioning.

Movie info:

It’s the month of Halloween, and what better time to see the Friday the 13th rip-off you’ve probably never seen!

Srigala is Indonesia’s wonderfully wild take on the original Friday the 13th. And if you’re wondering, “Is this a true slasher film?” Absolutely… but with a healthy pinch of Southeast Asian over-the-top cinema thrown into the mix!

Considered an obscure gem of Southeast Asian horror, Srigala is a must-see, especially if you love slashers, cult horror, and movies that aren’t afraid to get a little weird.

Srigala was directed by legendary Indonesian filmmaker Sisworo Gautama Putra, who also directed the original Satan’s Slaves!

Like Friday the 13th, the story follows a gaggle of young adults — aka future slasher victims — who make their way to a remote lakeside camp. There’s a little relaxation, a little fun…and then the chaos begins!

Info about See-Scape:

Our movies will be shown on the second floor! There are two bars available in See-Scape. The bar on the second floor is open during our event and is cash-only. Debit/Credit purchases are available on the main floor.

See-Scape also has an amazing menu. To learn more about See-Scape, please click here! www.seescapeto.com/ https://www.seescapeto.com/

See-Scape is located at 347 Keele Street (the closest intersection is Keele/Dundas) and is easily accessible via TTC. (from Keele Station or Dundas West Station)

Parking: There is a Green P parking lot beside See-Scape and a few other paid parking lots nearby.

Each month, join Lizzie Violet & Zoltan Du Lac for killer B-moves from the 1930s to the present!

Please like our Facebook page and Instagram @killerbcinema so you don’t miss an invite.

Thank you to See-Scape and their staff! They make our monthly event extra unforgettable!

We hope to see you at See-Scape.

title: Clay Tile Workshop
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Experiment with clay and craft your own unique tile in this hands-on workshop designed for both beginners and art enthusiasts.

Guided by our Museum Educators, participants will explore shaping, designing, and decorating techniques inspired by ceramic works in the Aga Khan Museum’s Collections. Learn how patterns and motifs have been used for centuries across the Islamic world, and experiment with tools and textures to bring your vision to life. You’ll leave with a one-of-a-kind creation that blends traditional inspiration with your own creativity.

title: Question Everything: Evaluating in an era of bias, spin and social polarization
description:
Part of the Think, Research, Create: Intro to Library Research Series (3 out of 4)
Not all information is created equally—and not all search tools work the same way. This interactive workshop will help you compare popular tools for information discovery from AI to academic search platforms. You’ll learn the differences between misinformation, disinformation, malinformation, AI hallucinations and deepfakes. We’ll show you practical fact-checking tools and strategies to help you figure out what’s real and what’s not. You’ll also practice evaluating sources, including academic ones, so you can choose the most reliable information for your assignments. By the end, you’ll feel more confident navigating the information jungle!

title: Fall Migration Birding in Toronto
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fall-birding-26)**

**Toronto has some hidden natural gems, and October is when it puts on its best show.**

Join our guide Pedro Hernandez of[ Outdoor Commute](https://www.instagram.com/outdoor.commute/) for a beginner-friendly birdwatching walk through the unique Tommy Thompson Park. You do not need to know a warbler from a wren, but you probably will when the day is done. This walk is built for people who are simply curious about the birds sharing our skyline.

We’ll move slowly and stop often, learning how to identify species by shape, colour, and call, how to actually use a pair of binoculars (yours to borrow for the day), and how to make sense of field guides and birding apps you can keep using long after the trip ends.

October is peak Fall migration in the city, with so many different birds to spot. Depending on conditions, we might spot warblers, sparrows, and thrushes moving through, along with waterfowl like northern shovelers and gadwalls resting on the water. Year-round residents including red-tailed hawks, black-capped chickadees, and northern cardinals tend to make an appearance too.

**Please note that binoculars are included in the cost of the adventure and that, due to the Toronto location, transportation is not offered.**

**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com

**Highlights**
**Fall Migration:** October is one of the best windows of the year to bird at the Spit, with local species and southbound migrants both moving through the park at once.
**Professional Birder:** Pedro founded the popular birding account[ Outdoor Commute](https://www.instagram.com/outdoor.commute/) and brings a genuine, patient teaching style
**Binoculars Included:** Every participant gets a pair of high-quality NOCS binoculars for the walk

**Event cost: $60+HST (for explorer members). Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fall-birding-26)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

We'll meet **outside Christie Station at 8:30 AM** and travel together in a **Kia Soul equipped with SiriusXM radio**. 🎶
We'll head to Brampton for a day of exploring, with a focus on the downtown area so we can walk between several locations.

Your $20 covers:

* 🚗 Round-trip transportation from Toronto to Brampton

Possible stops include:
**📍 Brampton Downtown Heritage Walk**
Explore Brampton's history, architecture and stories from the city's past.
**📍 Alderlea**

That gives us roughly five hours to explore, so we'll keep things moving and make the most of our time.

### 🎶 THE RIDE

Travel in a **Kia Soul with SiriusXM radio**, good conversation and hopefully some great fall weather.
The ride there and back is part of the fun!

### 👟 WHAT TO BRING

Panel discussions
Helping Children Navigate AI Safely
11:15 am-12 pm

Featuring Matthew Johnson (MediaSmarts), André Côté (The Dais), and Aarani Stoneham (AI Literacy Learners), with moderation by Jessica Wong (CBC).

2-3 pm

Flourishing in an AI Society
3:15-4:15 pm

Featuring Victória Oldemburgo de Mello (Center for Conflict and Cooperation at NYU), Jess Mitchell (OCAD University), Stephanie Jonsson (ODLAN) and Mario Vasilescu (Readocracy), with moderation by Pete Bombaci (Genwell).

Together, we'll examine the opportunities and challenges of AI to foster a more informed, inclusive and empowered digital society that protects Canadians and safeguards democracy.

title: AI for a Just World: Power, Liberation, and the People Left Behind
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, 2nd Floor
description:
How is artificial intelligence reshaping healthcare, work, and state surveillance? And what can we do about it?  In this interactive panel discussion, we present three real-world case studies. With each case study, we ask: how are communities being affected, and how are they resisting? First, we consider promises being made to the sickle cell community about the role of AI in diagnosis and cure. Second, we consider the role of AI in delivery worker exploitation.  Digital platform workers are already living the future that concerns so many of us. Third, we consider how AI is reshaping warfare and state surveillance. After each case study, we will pose small-group questions for the audience to discuss.
About our speakers: Rachel da Silveira Gorman (Professor, Graduate Program Director, Critical Disability Studies), Vanessa Ferguson (PhD Candidate, School of Health Policy & Management at York University), Emmett Lockwood (PhD Student in Critical Disability Studies at York University), and Habiba Rahman (PhD candidate in Critical Disability Studies at York University)

title: 🐟Walk:  Salmon Run at Humber River & James Gardens 🍂
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🐟 Salmon Run at Humber River & James Gardens 🍂

### An Easy Fall Walk — With a Pretty Amazing Natural Show Along the Way

Every fall, something incredible happens right here in Toronto.
Salmon make their way upstream through the **Humber River**, battling rapids and leaping through the water as they return to freshwater to spawn.
And yes — you can actually see them doing it.

Join us for a relaxed, social walk along the Humber River during salmon run season. We'll spend about 30 minutes by the river watching for salmon before continuing along the trail toward **James Gardens**.
This isn't a difficult hike. It's a chance to get outside, enjoy the fall scenery, see something you might not normally experience in the city, and spend some time with other people along the way.

✨ **Fun Fact:** Some salmon travel more than 3,000 km from the Atlantic Ocean to reach freshwater rivers like the Humber. After all that distance, they still have to battle rapids and leap over obstacles to reach their spawning grounds.
Nature really doesn't mess around.

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 🚶‍♂️ What We'll Do

We'll begin outside the station and make our way toward the Humber River.
Along the way we'll:

* Walk along the Humber River
* Stop for approximately 30 minutes to look for salmon
* Watch the salmon making their way upstream
* Continue along the river toward James Gardens
* Take a break at **James Gardens**
* Enjoy the fall scenery and take some photos
* Make our way back toward the station

The walk is approximately **90 minutes**, depending on the pace of the group and how long we spend watching the salmon.
And remember — **the salmon are wild animals.** We can't guarantee exactly how many we'll see, or how long they'll put on a show. That's part of the fun!

***

## 🍂 Why Come?

The salmon run is one of those strange little Toronto experiences that you can easily miss if you don't know when and where to look.
One minute you're walking through the city. The next, you're standing beside a river watching salmon fight their way upstream.
We'll also visit **James Gardens**, one of those beautiful green spaces that can make you forget you're still in Toronto.
Bring your camera, bring your curiosity, and come see what the Humber has to offer in the fall.

***

## ☀️ Weather & Expectations

This walk takes place outdoors in typical Toronto fall weather.
Please dress appropriately for the conditions and wear comfortable walking shoes. The trail may be damp or muddy depending on recent weather.
Bring water and a snack, and dress in layers — fall weather can change quickly.

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Location:** Right outside the station
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time: 11:00 AM**
I will only wait **5 minutes**.
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🏁 **End Point:** Back at the station

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$5 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This fee helps support the group and allows us to continue organizing events throughout Toronto.

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🥪 A snack
🧴 Sunscreen if it's sunny
📷 A camera or phone for photos

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This walk is great for:

* Anyone who wants an easy fall outing
* People who enjoy nature and wildlife
* Anyone curious about Toronto's rivers and green spaces
* People looking for a relaxed social walk
* Anyone who wants to meet new people while exploring the city
* Salmon enthusiasts — obviously. 🐟

The activity is the container. **The people you meet along the way are the real experience.**

***

📲 **REMEMBER:** You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email:
📧 **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**

**Come for the salmon.**
**Stay for the walk.**
**Leave with a new connection — and maybe a new friend.** 🍂💛

Join our Digital Expo panel discussions via livestream from anywhere. Discover how AI is shaping safety, democracy, civic participation and trust, and explore how we can build AI that advances human flourishing.
Registrants will receive an email with a Zoom meeting link within 24 hours before the program starts.
Looking to attend in person?
Learn more and register
.
Panel discussions:
Helping Children Navigate AI Safely
11:15 am-12 pm
Explore how AI is shaping children's lives and learn practical ways to support safe, responsible and informed AI use at home and in school.
Featuring Matthew Johnson (MediaSmarts), André Côté (The Dais), and Aarani Stoneham (AI Literacy Learners), with moderation by Jessica Wong (CBC).
Safeguarding Democracy in the Age of AI
1-1:45 pm
Join this keynote to examine the opportunities and risks AI presents for democracy, and the steps needed to strengthen trust, safety and civic participation.
Featuring Beatrice Wayne (Samara Centre for Democracy) and Valentine Goddard (AI Impact Alliance).
AI and Civic Engagement
2-3 pm
Learn how AI is changing the way people access information, engage with one another and participate in democracy.
Featuring Mathew Markman (Ethelo), Jonathan Coutinho (Evidence for Democracy) and Lexa Michaelides (Hypha), with moderation by Tai Huynh (The Local).
Flourishing in an AI Society
3:15-4:15 pm
Discover how communities can help guide AI development toward human flourishing, trust and democratic values.
Featuring Victória Oldemburgo de Mello (Work and Play Lab), Jess Mitchell (OCAD University), Stephanie Jonnson (ODLAN) and Mario Vasilescu (Readocracy), with moderation by Pete Bombaci (Genwell).

title: Landmarks 5: Mechanics' Institute to Reference Library via Mackenzie House!
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Toronto is a city that hides its history in plain sight. Beneath the glass towers are layers of stories — grand hotels that vanished overnight, political scandals whispered through stone corridors, theatres that once glittered under gaslight, and laneways where the city first learned how to become a metropolis.

This new Toronto History Walks tour invites the walker to slow down, and see the city differently.

Over the course of 30 carefully chosen stops, this walking tour traces the landmarks that helped shape the history of Toronto. Beginning at the site of the legendary Holland House — once one of the city’s finest mansions, and a gathering place for politicians, and businessmen, the route winds through the old heart of downtown, uncovering stories both famous and forgotten.

Some locations are grand and imposing. Others are easy to walk past without a second glance. Every stop reveals a piece of Toronto’s personality. At Osgoode Hall, visitors will stand before one of the city’s most elegant historic buildings. Nearby, the old banks and newspaper buildings of the financial district recall an era when Toronto proudly called itself “Toronto the Good,” even as corruption and backroom dealings simmered beneath the surface.

The tour also explores the vanished city — the Toronto that survives only in photographs, and memory. Walkers will discover where magnificent Victorian structures once stood before demolition crews erased entire blocks in the name of progress. Former theatres, hotels, markets, and department stores emerge again through storytelling, helping modern explorers imagine the bustle, smoke, and noise of earlier generations.

Stories of fire, disaster, celebration, and reinvention. Participants will hear how the Great Fire of 1904 transformed downtown streets, how immigrant communities reshaped neighbourhoods block by block, and how Toronto repeatedly reinvented itself through booms, depressions, wars, and waves of newcomers.

But this tour is not simply about dates and buildings. It is about people. The politicians who argued over Confederation. The hotel clerks who witnessed scandals. The newspaper editors who shaped public opinion. The shopkeepers, labourers, entertainers, and ordinary Torontonians whose lives unfolded along these same streets.

Toronto has always had hidden corners and strange tales: tunnels beneath streets, forgotten cemeteries beneath office towers, unsolved crimes, and buildings said to carry echoes of the past. Even longtime residents may find themselves surprised by what has been quietly standing before them all along. Come along and experience a very different city. A deep dive into our history.

This tour explores the history of the Mechanics' Institute and the area from Church and King Street and publishing row to the 1977 Reference Library. Our mid way stop is at Mackenzie House and the history around one of the leading events in Toronto and Canada; the Rebellion of 1837. We continue north to explore the area between Dundas Street East and Bloor Street East and the landmarks, that gave rise to the district east of Yonge Street. Hope to see you there.

This walking tour begins at the **dog fountain** at Berczy Park at the northeast **corner** of Scott Street and Wellington. We end at the Toronto Reference Library on Yonge just steps north of Bloor.

This walking tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season, and hope to see you there.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: TBG Fall Ravine Festival
description:
Enjoy a day of music, adventure, and education. Join us for the Ravine Festival, an exciting day of fun and learning set against the beautiful backdrop of the Toronto Botanical Garden and its surrounding natural spaces. Discover fascinating facts about ravines, local wildlife, and how you can contribute to the preservation of Toronto’s ravine systems. This is a fantastic opportunity for families to get hands-on with nature and environmental stewardship. 



Saturday, October 3, 202612 to 4 p.m.FREE Admission 



Generously supported by Enbridge 



Event Highlights:









12 to 4 p.m. Pick up your nature passport at the Visitor Centre to embark on a Scavenger Hunt. Discover amazing facts about ravines, meet local wildlife, enjoy hands-on nature fun, and learn how to protect Toronto’s ravine spaces. Visit each station in the Garden to complete an activity and earn a stamp! Remember, once you’ve completed your adventure, check in at the passport desk for a prize! 









12 to 4 p.m.Visit our partner pop up stations hosted by Toronto Public Library, Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, Toronto Master Gardeners, Live Green Toronto, SciXchange, Willowdale School of Music, Human Nature Projects Ontario, North York Harvest Food Bank, Glen Caradus, The Loop, Toronto Wildlife Centre, and Alan Li.  















Live music performances with Sofar Sounds. Half hour performances at 12:30 p.m., 1:30 p.m. and 2:30 p.m. 









Circus at the Garden with Artists’ Play Dance + Circus Arts. 15-minute interactive and aerial performances with “Rosie Petals” that bring magic to the earth and sky. Performances at 1:10 p.m., 2:10 p.m. and 3:10 p.m. 











Free Restore and Align Yoga session by Simpli Yoga Studio. Learn now to release tension and completely relax your body at these free 30-minute yoga sessions focused on realigning your posture so you can move through life with greater ease and less strain. Classes start at 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. No registration is required. 









10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.Immerse yourself in Essense of the Garden: Plein Air Art Exhibition + Sale, featuring over 100 original artworks from 45 talented local artists. The exhibition opens October 3 and runs until October 18. All artwork is available for purchase. 















10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Local eats at the Dandelion Cafe with light bites, hot and cold beverages and Kawartha Dairy ice cream. Special offerings include: Pulled Beef and Pulled Jack Fruit Sliders served with Brussel Sprout, Honey Crisp Slaw and House-made Mac ‘n Cheese. ** Gluten Free Buns Available  









10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.Visit the Garden Shop for garden gear, nature-inspired gifts, and home decor. 









Many Thanks to our Ravine Festival Community Partners:



Toronto Public Library, Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, SciXchange, Human Nature Project, Alan Li Artist, North York Harvest, Toronto Wildlife Centre and LiveGreen

Toronto Bruce Trail Club

![🎒](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/ta4/1/16/1f392.png) **Essential Gear:** What to pack for a safe, comfortable, and self-sufficient day on the trails.

![📆](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/tff/1/16/1f4c6.png) **Year-Round Outings:** How to join our full schedule of urban walks, car pool hikes, bus day trips, and winter ski and snowshoe coach excursions.

Through fun activities, participants will figure out a "robot's" secret rules, learn why AI sometimes makes mistakes, and design their very own "Trashbot" that learns to tell trash from treasure.
This program is designed for children ages 6-9 years.
Registration required. Please register 1 spot for each child attending the workshop.
***
About this event
Digital Expo 2026 is a dynamic day of learning, exploration and connection focused on shaping a responsible AI future for everyone.

title: A World of One Heart – Peace and Sustainability
location: Jane Mallett Theatre,Toronto Centre for the Arts, 27 Front St E, Toronto, ON M5E 1B4, Canada
description:
✨ A Spectacular Cultural Performance Comes to Toronto for the First Time! ✨

Experience four cultural performances in Toronto from October 2–4, 2026, presented as part of the international celebration of the 60th Anniversary of Tai Ji Men Qigong Academy.

Offered as a complimentary community cultural initiative and a gift to the community, these performances blend qigong, martial arts, music, dance, and contemporary performing arts to bring timeless wisdom to life through inspiring artistic storytelling, celebrating cultural heritage while sharing the universal values of love, peace, and conscience.

Tai Ji Men’s internationally acclaimed cultural performances have been presented at renowned venues around the world, including the Sydney Opera House (Australia), Pasadena Civic Auditorium (USA), and Luckman Fine Arts Complex (USA). We are delighted to bring this inspiring cultural experience to Toronto for the very first time.

The performances are presented by Tai Ji Men (Canada), an independent Canadian non-profit organization committed to enriching communities through holistic education, cultural exchange, and well-being initiatives.

title: AI and Young People: The Future of Thinking
location: North York Central Library, Room 2/3
description:
Today’s youth are the first generation growing up with AI everywhere. What does that mean for how they think, make things, and become themselves?
Join us for an open conversation about AI and youth. This panel discussion will share what young people are actually doing with AI, what worries them, and what adults keep getting wrong. Audience questions welcome. This is not a lecture about the dangers of cheating or bad choices; it's the ageless conversation about agency, creativity, and thinking for yourself, but in the age where digital intelligences are developing too.
Featuring:
Dashiel Carrera
, Incoming Assistant Professor of Arts and Machine Creativity, HKUST
Diana Maliszewski
, Teacher-Librarian, Toronto District School Board
Ronit Novak
,

title: Livestream Viewing: Japanese Canadian Monument Opening Ceremony
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
Announcement for unveiling of the Japanese Canadian Monument Registration for the livestream has closed, confirmations have been sent Please join us at the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre (JCCC) or Momiji Health Care Society (Momiji) on Saturday, October 3, 2026 at 3:30pm EST for the live streaming of the opening ceremony of the Japanese Canadian Monument that is taking place in Victoria, British Columbia. A pre-show program will begin at 3:30pm, and the opening ceremony livestream will begin at 4:00pm. Further information per livestream location is outlined below. The Japanese Canadian Monument lists the names of all Japanese Canadians uprooted in 1942 AND a second set of names of children born after uprooting and up to and including March 31, 1949, after which freedom to return to the coast was fully granted. The monument acknowledges the forced dispossession and internment of the community during World War II while celebrating their resilience and impact on the region. These names and locations engraved on the wall provide a stark illustration of a community torn apart by policies that were driven by a confluence of race, economics, and power. To set them in stone here is to ensure they are never again forgotten or marginalized. Light refreshments will be served, and a souvenir book will be gifted to all attendees. Please note that capacity will be limited based on location selected ( choice between JCCC and Momiji) . Registration are closed. For more information, please refer to https://hcmc.uvic.ca/project/monument/ . For any questions, please reach out to jccc@jccc.on.ca . Livestream Event Information at the JCCC: Thank you for joining the JCCC at the monument unveiling livestream on Saturday, October 3, 2026! Doors will open at 2:30pm EST on October 3, 2026 for sign in, and the pre-show program and livestream will begin at 3:30pm EST in Kobayashi Hall. Light refreshments will be served, and a souvenir book will be gifted to all attendees. Please note that the maximum capacity of the livestream event in Kobayashi Hall is 300 guests. Once the registration form reaches maximum capacity, a waitlist for 50 guests will be monitored. Registrants will be contacted via email in September to confirm their entrance status (enrolled or waitlist) . Further details will be communicated via email, e-blast, and social media in September. The JCCC will also be replaying the livestream throughout the evening beginning at 7:00pm EST on October 3, 2026 during Nuit Blanche, as well as during Issei Day on October 4, 2026. Registration is not required for Nuit Blanche livestream viewing on October 3, 2026. To register for Issei Day, please visit: Issei Day page . A souvenir book will also be gifted to all Issei Day attendees on October 4, 2026. We look forward to seeing you there! Livestream Event Information at Momiji Health Care Society: Momiji would like to welcome our community to watch the livestream of the monument unveiling in Victoria, BC, from the comfort of the Yone and Coby Kobayashi Auditorium at Momiji Seniors Residence. Momiji will be providing a small, boxed meal for the first 150 community members and 70 tenants registered. Once we hit capacity, a waitlist will be created, and we will be working with the JCCC to ensure that as many people as possible are able to watch the event. Since the event is overlapping with our annual bazaar, we are inviting attendees to arrive anytime from Noon to 3:00pm and support our annual bazaar before joining the livestream. Further details will be communicated by email and social media in September.

title: Paradise
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
The JCCC Gallery's fall exhibition is Paradise : a multimedia installation by Japanese Canadian artists and longtime family friends Mitchell Akiyama and Emma Nishimura that explores intergenerational inheritance. Combining print, video, and sculpture, the work reflects on their relationship to the legacy of Japanese Canadian internment experienced by their paternal grandparents. The exhibition draws on a shared childhood memory of a summer day in Northern Ontario, where the artists and their siblings built a temporary "Frog Paradise." This moment of play, shaped by a sense of safety and belonging, becomes a lens for considering how one group’s utopia can exist alongside another’s harm. The installation includes video that intercuts footage of this experience with recent visits to former internment sites in British Columbia. Bridging personal narrative and historical context, Paradise examines the forced relocation and incarceration of Japanese Canadians, tracing how this legacy continues to shape memory, displacement, and belonging across generations. Nuit Blanche at the JCCC : October 3 rd at 7pm 7pm — Artist Talk Hear from Mitchell Akiyama and Emma Nishimura as they discuss the ideas, memories, and histories behind Paradise ! 9pm — Origami Frog Workshop Join the artists for a hands-on workshop inspired by the exhibition’s "Frog Paradise." Opening Reception Please join us on October 25 th from 2 to 4pm Opening Reception

We will start off the 26/27 Koerner Hall concert season, with a performance by Vieux Farka Touré (from Mali), and opening for him is Melat Mengesha (from Ethiopia)

(And we have our eyes on other concerts during the season!)

Also we have a 15% off ticket promo!! ***Ticket link is below*--($50-$80)**

Known worldwide for his electrifying live shows, Vieux Farka Touré’s virtuosic guitar work blends Malian blues, rock, and soul. Winner of Ethiopian Idol Melat Mengesha opens the show.

Often referred to as “The Hendrix of the Sahara,” **Vieux Farka Touré** is the son of legendary Malian guitarist Ali Farka Touré, who died in 2006. His live performances are highly energized, and Vieux is known for dazzling crowds with his speed and dexterity on the guitar, as well as his palpable charisma and luminous smile, both of which captivate audiences despite any language barriers (though Vieux does speak eight languages!).

Hailing from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, now based in Toronto, \*\*Melat Mengesha’\*\*s music features contemporary, folk, and Ethio-jazz roots sounds. Two major influences in her artistic expression are the legendary Ethiopian singers Gigi (Ejigayehu Shibabaw) and Aster Aweke. A major turning point came in 2015, when Melat won the first season of Balageru (Ethiopian Idol). That breakthrough opened the door to a variety of showcases and performances, from intimate stages to large-scale concerts, allowing her to tour across her hometown and beyond.

title: Tanglefoot Reunion
location: Acoustic Harvest, 200 McIntosh Street, Scarborough
description:
The Songs, The Stories, The Spirit of Canada 
For three decades, Tanglefoot carried the spirit of Canada across stages in North America, the United Kingdom, and Europe with powerful harmonies, quick wit, rich storytelling, and songs rooted in Canadian history. Now this legendary Canadian folk ensemble returns for a special reunion concert, bringing their unmistakable energy, warmth, and humour back to the stage. 
This new chapter reunites Canadian Folk Music Award winners Steve Ritchie, Al Parrish, Sandra Swannell Young, and Rob Ritchie, joined by Rob’s son, singer and multi-instrumentalist Josh Ritchie, stepping into the place once held by the late Terry Young. It is both a celebration of legacy and a fresh passing of the torch. 
Audiences can expect fan favourites, hidden gems, stories, laughter, and the kind of heartfelt music that turns a concert into a shared memory. For longtime fans, this is a rare chance to reconnect with a beloved part of Canadian folk music. For those discovering Tanglefoot for the first time, it is an invitation into songs that feel timeless, spirited, and deeply Canadian. 
Join us at Acoustic Harvest for an evening of friendship, storytelling, and music that reminds us why live folk music still matters.

title: Bus Hike: Limehouse (Bruce Trail Day)
description:
Toronto Bruce Trail Club
oin us to celebrate Bruce Trail Day on the trail around Limehouse. For the first 5 km we will hike south from the Sixth Line to Limehouse. The route incorporates the portion of trail removed from the Fifth Line thanks to those who support the Bruce Trail. We'll also pass the seed orchard where native species are grown for the seeds to be replanted to re-naturalize other parts of the trail. Those who want a shorter hike may drop out at Limehouse where information and refreshments will be available at the Memorial Hall. The second part of the hike will be a loop through the Limehouse Conservation area featuring the limestone kilns, stone arched bridge, and a climb through the "hole in the wall". Expect some slightly rocky terrain underfoot and a few moderate hills. Hiking boots or good shoes designed for walking are a must. Those completing the full 9 km will also have a chance to drop in at the Memorial Hall to learn more about the Bruce Trail and refreshments.

You must register and prepay the bus fare on the Bruce Trail Conservancy Website (registration opens Sat Sep 20 8:00 PM (Bus Fares $25 Members/$32 Non-Members (Children under 12 $10/$14). Bus fares are non-refundable and the hike goes rain or shine.

Registration Link:
[https://hikes.brucetrail.org/event/bus-hike-bruce-trail-day-limehouse/2026-10-04/](https://hikes.brucetrail.org/event/bus-hike-bruce-trail-day-limehouse/2026-10-04/)

title: Devils Hole - US Side
description:
These Boots Are Made for Hiking
Meetup: **Niagara Gorge - US side**
Meet up point: Devil's Hole State Park Parking Area
Address: 5100 Niagara Scenic Pkwy, Niagara Falls, NY 14305, United States
GPS Coordinates: 43.13301222763603, -79.04771831578047 (or 43°07'58.8"N 79°02'51.8"W)
**Make sure you have your passport!**
We usually hike the Canadian side, so we decided we needed a different point of view!
Devil’s Hole is a semi-circular notch formed by an ancient waterfall draining a section of Glacial Lake Tonawanda. This waterfall formed as the main Falls eroded back past this point in the gorge. Lake Tonawanda eventually dried up along with its waterfall.
In the early 1700's, the raging waters so terrified the locals that it was supposed that the devil lived there. The name stuck.
**Legend and Lore of Devil’s Hole**
**Devil’s Hole Massacre:** On September 14, 1763, a British supply train of wagons was passing by Devil’s Hole when a band of Senecas ambushed the party, killing all but a few who escaped (2 or 3). The commotion was heard by soldiers stationed near the head of the Portage in Lewiston and reinforcements were sent marching up the road in formation. These troops were also attacked and basically wiped out.
source: Meetup: These Boots Are Made for Hiking

**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

New topic each week.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

title: Fall Walk: From Cabbagetown to Cherry Street 🌿 🍺
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🍂 Fall Walk: From Rosedale to Cherry Street 🌿

### A Fall Walk Through Some of Toronto's Most Interesting Neighbourhoods

Looking for a walk that gives you a little bit of everything?
We'll start in **Rosedale**, make our way through **Cabbagetown and Regent Park**, wander through the **Distillery District**, stop at **Biidaasige Park**, and finish with a well-earned meal at **Cherry Street Bar-B-Que**.
Along the way, we'll see some of the city's oldest neighbourhoods, newer communities, historic architecture, green spaces, and some pretty great views.
It's a longer walk, but the route is more about **exploring Toronto together** than trying to finish as quickly as possible.

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 🚶‍♂️ What We'll Do

We'll meet outside **Rosedale Station** and begin our walk through Rosedale Valley, following the tree-lined route toward Cabbagetown.
Along the way we'll:

* Walk through Rosedale Valley 🌳
* Explore the historic streets of Cabbagetown
* Pass through Regent Park
* Wander through the Distillery District
* Stop at Biidaasige Park
* Take in the fall scenery and city views
* Finish at **Cherry Street Bar-B-Que** 🍖

The walk includes a **long set of stairs**, so while this isn't a difficult hike, you should be comfortable walking for several hours and keeping up with the group.

***

## 🏙️ A Little Toronto History Along the Way

This walk takes us through several very different parts of Toronto.
In **Cabbagetown**, we'll pass beautifully preserved Victorian homes and streets that reflect the neighbourhood's long history, including its Irish roots.

We'll then make our way through **Regent Park**, one of Toronto's most historically significant communities, where older social housing has been joined by new housing, arts, and community spaces.
From there, we'll head into the **Distillery District**, with its cobblestone streets and historic red-brick buildings.

We'll also stop at **Biidaasige Park**, whose name means *“the sun is shining”* in Anishinaabemowin.
It's a lot of Toronto in one walk.

***

## 🍺 The Keating Channel Pub & Grill

We'll finish our walk at **The Keating Channel Pub & Grill**, right on the Keating Channel.

There's a bit of history behind this stop. The pub struggled during the massive Port Lands construction, when road closures and the relocation of the Cherry Street bridge made the area difficult to reach. With the Port Lands now transformed and **Biidaasige Park** open, people are rediscovering this part of the city — and the pub is getting a second chance.

After exploring the new park and the transformed Port Lands, we'll finish at one of the neighbourhood's old survivors: a casual waterfront pub with a patio overlooking the Keating Channel.

***

## ☀️ Weather & Expectations

This is a **long urban walk**, not a difficult hike, but you should be comfortable being on your feet for several hours.
There is a long set of stairs along the route.
Please wear comfortable walking shoes and dress appropriately for the weather.

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Location:** Outside Rosedale Station
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time:** 11:00 AM sharp
I will only wait **5 minutes**.
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🏁 **End Point:** Cherry Street Bar-B-Que

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$5 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This fee helps support the group and allows us to continue organizing events throughout Toronto.

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🥪 A snack
🧴 Sunscreen
🧥 Weather-appropriate clothing

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This walk is great for:

* People who enjoy exploring Toronto
* Anyone who likes history and architecture
* People looking for a longer social walk
* Anyone who wants to discover neighbourhoods they might not normally visit
* People who enjoy stopping for food at the end
* Anyone who wants to spend a Sunday exploring the city with other people

The destination isn't really the point.
**It's the people you meet along the way.**

You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**.

**Come for the walk.**
**Stay for the friendship.**
**And maybe stay a little longer for lunch.** 🍺🌿

The location was a well known meeting place between the indigenous and and the white traders, and the Credit River was known to them as Missinhe. In 1720, a trading post was built and the area known today as Mississauga entered recorded history!

The first building was English built in 1798 on the east bank of the river. Lieutenant Governor Simcoe had ordered some sort of rest stop for travellers, but was destroyed by fire years later!

title: Traditional Indigo Batik Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for an fun-filled workshop and introduction to the traditional practice of indigo batik!
Indigo batik is a captivating textile art form that combines the beauty of natural indigo dyeing with intricate wax-resist designs. Its origins can be traced back to ancient civilizations across various cultures and regions, including Egypt, China, India, and West Africa around 2,000 years ago.
 
The technique gained prominence in Southeast Asia, particularly in Java, Indonesia, where the intricate art form of “batik tulis” (hand-drawn batik) evolved and is now a widely recognized intangible cultural heritage.
 
Batik is also widely practiced by the Miao indigenous group in Southwest China and holds historical and cultural significance for these communities to this day. Girls would learn the art of batik from their moms starting at the age of eight or nine. Since the Miao does not have their own written language, the Miao women have had a large role to play in documenting their people’s history, stories, and emotions through their textile arts.
 
During this 3-hour workshop, you will learn about the history and traditional motifs of Miao batik, as well as a significant hands-on portion dedicated to learning the traditional wax-resist dyeing method. You will create patterns using batik tools from the Miao community, before dyeing your finished piece in natural indigo.
 
No prior knowledge is needed to take this workshop, and all materials will be provided.
 
Attendees are encouraged to think through some patterns and designs they would like to work on during the session but we will also provide additional ideas and motifs for inspiration.
 
We will provide all materials, such as natural beeswax, small electric pots, batik painting tools (“ladao”), indigo dye bath, and an iron. Additionally, each participant is provided with upcycled, practice fabrics as well as a piece of organic cotton handkerchief to create on.
 
Sunday, October 4, 1 to 4:30 p.m.
Public $120, TBG Members $115 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Lisa Shi
Lisa Shi is the co-founder of SlowMaking, a cultural platform dedicated to preserving and sharing traditional craft knowledge. She has spent years travelling, learning, and conducting field research on cultural craft traditions, exploring how material culture and techniques reveal universal threads of connection across global communities.
 
Her engagement with batik is grounded in firsthand study with both Chinese and Indonesian researchers and artisans. These cross-cultural experiences inform her global understanding of batik and its broader textile histories, influences, and techniques, shaping a teaching practice rooted in research, respect, and hands-on experimentation.
 
About SlowMaking
At SlowMaking, we inspire intercultural connections and a slow, sustainable way of life through authentic storytelling, artisanal products, and immersive experiences that centre around heritage crafts.
 
To follow along for more cultural crafts and traditions: Instagram | Youtube | Website

A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: La Société d'histoire de Toronto: HISTORITOUR - Wychwood Park et le Tollkeeper’s Cottage
location: Tollkeeper’s Cottage Museum, 750 Davenport Rd, Toronto, ON, M5R 1L4, Canada
description:
Départ : Tollkeeper’s Cottage Museum, 750 Davenport Rd (coin nord-ouest de Bathurst et de
Davenport). TTC : Métro Bathurst et autobus 7 nord jusqu’à Davenport. Stationnement sur la rue. 
Arrivée : Tollkeeper’s Cottage Museum
Guides : Isabelle Montagnier et Johanne Roberge (en français) et Marilyn Spearin (en anglais)
Wychwood Park a été fondé par Marmaduke Matthews, un peintre paysagiste qui a acheté le terrain en 1870 dans l’espoir d’y fonder une colonie d’artistes. Ce rêve ne s’est pas concrétisé, mais en 1891, avec son ami Alexander Jardine, Matthews a commencé à diviser son terrain en lotissements selon un plan bien établi. Aujourd’hui, Wychwood est une petite enclave privée sur les hauteurs de Davenport. Ses belles maisons sont un magnifique exemple du mouvement Arts and Crafts anglais. Une courte balade vous permettra de les découvrir par vous-même! 
Nous visiterons également le Tollkeeper’s Cottage, un bâtiment qui date de 1825 et est la seule structure de ce genre existant encore au Canada! Venez écouter l’histoire surprenante de son sauvetage… 
Note : Cette visite est organisée en collaboration avec le Community History Project qui offre le
volet en anglais. Une tasse de thé sera offerte aux visiteurs et visiteuses à la fin. 
Historitours 2026 – Pas nécessaire de réserver – pas de chien 
Visite guidée gratuite – La Société d’histoire de Toronto passe le chapeau à la fin 
Pour plus d’informations : imontagnier@sympatico.ca

title: Historic Cooksville - MISSISSAUGA (ONLY DATE FOR 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Cooksville was the real heart of old Toronto Township. But it started out as Harrisville after the original settler, and was a major transit hub and stagecoach line through the heart of Upper Canada. The Dundas highway linked the capital of York with the hinterland, and the western ends of the empire to the west and southwest towards today's Windsor.

Cooksville was also the home of a European Grand Duchess, I guess you will just have to take the tour to find out that answer and that fascinating story. Here's a clue she also lived on Gerrard Street in Toronto and I talk about it in my Riverdale walk. Or if you think you know drop me a line. Interesting indeed?

This is a an area that has plenty of history, but not all that well known. Let's explore Mississauga together. Plenty to learn here.

This walking tour is for all walking levels and fitness skills. Please dress for the season and bring water. And remember to bring your love of history.

This tour begins at the southeast corner of Dundas Street East and Hurontario in Mississauga. The tour returns to the start location after the walk!

The ticket price is $15.00 per person!

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Toronto Language Exchange | Practice Spanish & English (In-Person)
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
Join our **Spanish–English Language Exchange Meetup** and improve your conversation skills in a relaxed, social environment. This free event is perfect for anyone looking to practice Spanish or English while meeting new people in a cozy coffee shop setting.

### **🗣️ What You’ll Do**

* Practice Spanish and English through real conversations
* Join small groups and switch languages throughout the event
* Learn practical vocabulary and everyday expressions
* Build confidence speaking in a supportive environment

### **👥 Who Should Attend**

* Spanish learners (all levels)
* English learners (all levels)
* Native speakers who want to help others
* Anyone interested in language exchange and cultural connection

### **☕ Venue**

We meet at a local coffee shop—just grab a drink and enjoy the conversation!

### **💸 Cost**

**FREE event** (please support the venue by purchasing a drink)

### **🌟 Why Join?**

Language exchanges are one of the most effective ways to learn. You’ll improve faster by speaking with real people, hearing authentic accents, and using the language in everyday situations.
Whether you're a beginner or fluent speaker, you’ll find a welcoming community ready to practice and connect.

**👉 RSVP now and start speaking with confidence!**

location: Pegasus, 489B Church St
description: Toronto's top queer and allied comedians take the stage to raise funds for people living with HIV / AIDs! Toronto! Come out for a hilarious night of queer comedy raising money for a great cause! This show features Toronto's top 2SLGBTQIA+ comics taking the stage to raise funds for Friends for Life bike rally, supporting people living with HIV/AIDs. Doors at 8 pm, show from 8:30 - 10 pm. Right in the heart of the Village at Pegasus on Church! All welcome, including allies! Admission is free with donations gratefully accepted for the Friends for Life bike rally to support people living with HIV/AIDS. Donate here on Eventbrite or with cash in person at the event. Will it be weird if I come solo? Nope! Feel free to pop in, watch some comedy, and dip after if you aren't feeling social. If you're looking to mingle and maybe have a meet cute, feel free to introduce yourself to other audience members and / or some of the comedians - everyone is really really nice. This is all about community and supporting queer artists! Questions? Want to come out but are a lil nervous? Totally feel free to reach out to us on Instagram at @friendsofroxycomedy - its all about community! See you there? 🤠🌈 --- The venue: The show takes place in the main area of Pegasus - head up the stairs and grab a seat in the front area with the stage The performance space and washrooms are up a flight of stairs. Once inside, there is no grade change. Unfortunately there is no lift or elevator All washrooms are gender inclusive Seating is self-assigned Community: All are welcome at this event, including allies, that recognize this is a queer space where we are inclusive and respectful of one another, and where oppressive behaviour won't fly At this show we don't punch down, and isms, phobias, and aggressive crowd work will never be tolerated. The show is hosted and produced by a queer, nonbinary comedian who takes this seriously AF, and all the comedians agree to guidelines to keep the vibes cute and inclusive This show will be fun filled and full of friendly queers, and the audience and comedian can make new friends and mix and mingle afterwards. If you are flying solo, are nervous, or have any questions, feel free to DM us at @friendsofroxy We all want a sexy, healthy time! You are totally welcome to wear a mask. If you are feeling sick, please stay home! We'd be stoked if you rapid tested before the show. ‍

title: Featured Collection in York University Libraries on complexities facing people experiencing homelessness
description:
In recognition of World Homeless Day on Oct. 10, Complex Communities and York University Libraries have partnered to present a featured collection from Oct. 5 to 15 highlighting the complexities of homelessness and fostering greater awareness and understanding of the experiences of those affected. 
World Homeless Day, observed annually on Oct. 10, raises awareness of the experiences and needs of people facing homelessness, promotes local solutions, and encourages community action around the world. This featured collection highlights print and electronic materials from the library’s collections on homelessness, mental health and well-being to foster greater understanding of these critical issues and support teaching, learning, and research in these areas. We invite you to browse the book display on the first floor of Scott Library, along with our virtual display. 
In addition to the books and resources on display, this featured collection will showcase a recent Photovoice project developed by TNG Community Services. Photovoice is a qualitative research method that uses participant-generated photographs and personal narratives to transform lived experiences into actionable knowledge. TNG’s project, What Does 24 Hours Look Like When You’re Experiencing Homelessness?, reflects the organization’s commitment to addressing the stigma and discrimination faced by people experiencing homelessness and amplifying their voices through storytelling and research. 
It’s easy to assume the answer is dark and grim and that the only light at the end of the tunnel is daybreak, a hot cup of coffee, or a shower at the drop-in. Scary, stressful, lonely, dangerous: all apt words to describe the realities of being marginally or precariously housed. But they are also limiting descriptors, ones that flatten people into stereotypes and leave little room for curiosity, complexity, or empathy. 
Stigma is everywhere, and few experience it more acutely than those living outside traditional social norms. 
Over the course of three weeks, seven participants from TNG Community Services’ Urban Health and Homelessness Services drop-in used 35mm disposable cameras to document their daily lives through photography. The project invited participants to capture the mundane, the joyful, the gritty and the deeply personal; moments that assert presence, permanence, and the undeniable right to take up space. 
Photography became both an act of creativity and an act of resistance. 
A leader in the social services sector in Toronto, The Neighbourhood Group helps more than 45,000 low-income people and families in 30 locations across Toronto. With more than 1,000 staff and the support of over 900 volunteers, our free programs and services address the most pressing issues in our community: poverty, homelessness, mental health, unemployment, social isolation, substance abuse, conflict resolution, violence, youth alienation, and the settlement of newcomers.  
This project was important to me because others have interest to see what I see. I grew up in the system. I only have my daughter and my other ones don’t talk to me and everyone is scarce. That you guys to show interest in me is great. I hope others seeing these pictures will have empathy and humbleness. I’d like people to put my shoes on for 24 hours, let’s see how hard it is in each other’s lives, so we can respect one another.  – TNGCS Photovoice participant 
Our heartfelt thanks to TNG Community Services and its community for sharing this powerful Photovoice project and amplifying the voices and experiences of people facing homelessness. 
A special thank you to York University Libraries and especially to the Collections Engagement Group, for their work in bringing this featured collection to life. 
For more information about Complex Communities, reach out!  ComplexC@yorku.ca

title: Streaming Passes for the Brooklyn SciFi Film Festival
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi everybody!

[The Brooklyn SciFi Film Festival](https://brooklynscififilmfest.com/) kicks off its seventh season with over 200 independent Sci-Fi films from 34 countries streaming online for two weeks. The festival is an annual celebration of independent science fiction filmmaking, and over the years, BSFFF has highlighted hundreds of bold voices in the genre.

Grab your digital pass on Eventbrite to unlock a Netflix-style platform that you can search by category and even host virtual watch parties with friends. This year, we celebrate 60 Years of Star Trek with a series of Trek fan films, panels, and interactive events. The Sixth Borough anthology series also returns each night of the festival, dropping a new episode of hand-picked, standout science fiction films.

**[Purchase your online festival pass via Eventbrite here](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/brooklyn-scifi-film-festival-digital-pass-tickets-2000526111452?aff=ebdsshcopyurl&utm-campaign=social&utm-content=attendeeshare&utm-medium=discovery&utm-term=creator-collections&utm-share-source=creator-collections)**, your rsvp to this Meetup event is not enough. **If you're prompted for a discount code, use SIFIBookClubBSF26 for 15% off.**

Let us know some of your favorites in the comments!

If you're in the NYC area, we hope you'll join us for an in-person event, as well. Check out the lineup and join us if you can.

Cheers,
Jon & Meghan

title: De las Nubes a Aquí / From the Clouds to Here
location: Gales Gallery, 105 Accolade West Building (ACW), York University @ 89 York Blvd., Toronto
description:
Sensorium ( https://ampd.yorku.ca/sensorium/ ), AMPD ( https://ampd.yorku.ca/ ) and York International ( https://www.yorku.ca/international/ ) are thrilled to present: De las Nubes a Aquí / From the Clouds to Here.
In May 2026, 23 York University students travelled to Costa Rica to take part in the PANF 3030/5030 Global Eco-Arts Residency Course. This 10-day intensive course comprised a series of workshops, gallery tours, creative class-based exercises, community interactions, and participation in a local community festival at York University’s Las Nubes Eco-Campus and surrounding areas. Through these experiences, students were introduced to themes of environmental and community-based art, food sovereignty, site-specific art, and the ethics of community engagement.
De la Nubes a Aquí/ From the Clouds to Here highlights some of the student-created art that was inspired by this course and the Las Nubes Eco-Campus in Costa Rica.

title: Bring Your Problem: Can AI Help?
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
Do you have a recurring problem you think AI might help with? A thing you keep doing by hand that feels like it should be easier? Bring it. If you don't have one, come help your neighbours with theirs.
In this interactive class, you'll learn a simple seven-step way to think about problems: what's annoying you, what you've tried, what AI could actually do, and where it would fail. We'll gather real problems from the room, sort them into groups, and map out what's worth solving with AI, and what's better solved without it. We'll also talk honestly about what an AI fix costs: your money, your time, and sometimes your private information. The problems AI could help with most are often the most personal, and the most personal ones are worth the most care.
This program takes place during
Digital Inclusion Week 2026
.
Registration is required and will start September 9, 2026 at 9:00 AM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

title: Doug Johnstone (DNRC Herzberg)
location: MP1318A
description:
Title: The Variability of Deeply Embedded Protostars: Past, Present, and Future

Abstract: Using the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) we have monitored eight nearby low-mass star-forming regions in the Gould
Belt at submillimetre wavelengths for almost a decade to search for and quantify the time dependent brightness
variability of the resident deeply embedded protostars. Secular variability is common among these protostars; greater
than 25% of the sample show measurable long-term brightness changes and 10% show burst behaviour lasting from months 
to years. We interpret this secular variability as reflecting changes in the mass accretion rate from the disk to the
protostar, as predicted by theoretical models of (proto)stellar assembly. For a subset of our sample we have
contemporaneous mid-IR light-curves which allow additional constraints on the conditions responsible for the brightness
variations, confirming that the submillimetre variability is driven by changes in the dust temperature profile of the
envelope. Furthermore, we have combined, for one source, single dish and interferometric sub-mm monitoring, which
has allowed us to unambiguously recover a time lag in the variability at larger angular scales and use the results to
confirm the envelope structure surrounding the embedded protostar.
Host: Shantanu Basu

title: Postcards of Reconnection: A Craft Workshop
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St).
description:
Postcards of Reconnection
Sometimes reconnecting starts in solitude, not small talk. In this quiet, reflective craft workshop, you’ll design and illustrate a postcard for someone you've been meaning to reach: a friend, a family member, or anyone lingering in your thoughts. Take it home, add a stamp when you're ready and pop it into the mail, taking the first step towards an important reconnection.
This interactive pre-show is followed by
From Solitude To Connetion ft. Robert Coplan,
which starts at 7pm in the North York Central Library Concourse.
You can register for that event
here
, but please note if you wish to attend the postcard workshop you need to register separately
on this page
.
***
Spend an evening rethinking time alone in a room full of other people
, as
we exp
lore the
theme
of
“good solitude” and how alone time makes togetherness possible
.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the
featured event
. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. Sign up for the workshop or try out one of the engagement activities available, including the Conversation Station: The Calming Corner, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger around the topic of solitude.
The
C
alming
Corner
| 5:30 – 6:30 pm & 8:00 – 9:00 pm
The Calming Corner offers a calmer, low-sensory space with small seating pods of two or three, prompt cards on solitude and recharge habits, and no pressure to mingle beyond your comfort zone. It's built on Coplan's own research that meaningful connection doesn't require constant stimulation, just the right amount of space to think before you speak.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: Introduction to Entrepreneurship: Is This for Me, and Where Do I Start?
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, 1st fl
description:
This program is part of the Toronto Reference Library's
Entrepreneur in Residence
(EIR) service.
Most people don't hesitate because their idea is bad. They hesitate because they think entrepreneurship is intimidating. This opening session challenges this assumption by using real Canadian statistics and introducing the Business Model Canvas, both of which can help you capture how a business creates value, reaches customers, and generates capital. By the end of this session, you will be given a chance to start filling in your own Business Model Canvas and a chance to network with other participants.
The program includes a short networking component, providing participants with an opportunity to connect with other entrepreneurs.
Registration recommended. Drop-ins welcome until room capacity is reached.
To apply for one-on-one consultations with our resident entrepreneur, Ryan, please fill out the in-take form available at
tpl.ca/eir
. We begin accepting in-take forms on September 28, 2026 until available slots are filled.

title: From Solitude To Connection ft. Robert Coplan
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
Spend an evening rethinking time alone in a room full of other people as we explore the theme of “good solitude” and how alone time makes togetherness possible.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the featured event. Grab a drink or snack at the bar.
Sign up for the Postcards of Re-Connections Workshop
(see below for registration) or try out one of the engagement activities available, including the
Conversation
Station:
The
C
alming
Corner
, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger around the topic of solitude.
****
Join us at the North York Central Library Concourse for
Being Alone Together
with psychologist and author Robert Coplan
in conversation with Alanna Mitchell
.
Together, we’ll take apart the assumption that solitude and connection pull in opposite directions, examine the difference between chosen alone time and painful disconnection, and talk about how much of each we actually need. Expect to leave with a clearer sense of your own limits, and a few practical ways to protect the quiet that makes company possible.
What does "good" solitude actually look like, and how is it different from the isolation so many people are struggling with? How do extraverts and introverts experience alone time differently, and what do we get wrong about both? And in a culture that treats constant availability as a virtue, what would it mean to reclaim solitude as a skill worth practicing — not an escape from community, but a foundation for building it?
Coplan, a Carleton University psychologist and one of the world's leading researchers on solitude, draws on psychology, neuroscience, literature and sociology in The Joy of Solitude: How to Reconnect with Yourself in an Overconnected World. He distinguishes loneliness from solitude, introduces "aloneliness" — the real distress of not having enough time to yourself — and shows that even fifteen minutes alone a day can stabilize mood, spark creativity and recharge our capacity for connection.
Come for a thoughtful conversation about the surprising role alone time plays in helping us feel closer to others.
Q&A to follow. Books available for purchase.

The Calming Corner offers a calmer, low-sensory space with small seating pods of two or three, prompt cards on solitude and recharge habits, and no pressure to mingle beyond your comfort zone. It's built on Coplan's own research that meaningful connection doesn't require constant stimulation, just the right amount of space to think before you speak.

Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Beyond Chatbots: Build Your First Production Agent with Microsoft Foundry
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
AI agents are rapidly moving beyond simple conversational experiences. In this session, we will build the foundation of a production-ready agent using Microsoft Foundry Agent Service, Microsoft Agent Framework, and Azure application services.

Starting from a practical enterprise operations scenario, we will define the agent’s responsibilities, instructions, tools, conversation state, and structured outputs. We will then connect the agent to a Foundry model, add a typed function tool, stream responses to a web application, and examine the architectural differences between a model call, an assistant, an agent, and an agent workflow.

The session will also explore hosting options, including Foundry hosted agents and custom agent applications deployed to Azure Container Apps. Along the way, we will discuss identity, configuration, state management, failure boundaries, and the design decisions that separate a useful prototype from an application that can evolve toward production.

By the end of the session, attendees will understand the core components of a Microsoft Foundry agent application and will have a reusable starting point for building their own agentic solutions. Key topics: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service Microsoft Agent Framework Agent instructions and tool contracts Conversation state and streaming responses Structured outputs Hosted agents and Azure Container Apps Production-oriented agent architecture

title: Understanding and Preventing Burnout
description:
Burnout syndrome, more commonly referred to as burnout, can affect anyone regardless of gender, age, and level of professional responsibility. Today, more than ever, we can better understand this insidious phenomenon that causes so much individual and collective imbalance. To promote both employee and company well-being, this workshop highlights the causes and factors of burnout, identifies its physical, psychological, and behavioural symptoms, and develops strategies to address it.
Key Learning Outcomes:
– Define work-related stress and understand its impact on individuals and workplace dynamics.
– Learn what burnout is, including its phases, causes, and symptoms.
– Discover strategies to prevent and recover from burnout and promote a healthier work environment.
– Explore various stress management techniques, such as time management, relaxation methods, and visualization exercises.
