title: Recovery College: YU & Balance Week 2 | Finding self-compassion and dealing with growing pains
location: Online (Zoom)
description:
Growth does not always mean having everything figured out.
This week’s session of YU & Balance is about giving yourself room to explore your interests, set goals that feel meaningful and recognize that responsibilities and personal ambitions can exist together. Students will be able to take a closer look at where they are now and where they would like to go, while also considering the role self-compassion plays when plans change, mistakes happen or progress feels slow. What would you pursue if you gave yourself permission to try? And what would it look like to support yourself along the way instead of criticizing every setback?
This session is part of a 6-week Recovery College series. For each session attended, participants will receive $5 on their YU-card. To receive the gift card, you must attend the full session (approximately 45–60 minutes). Unfortunately, we’re not able to provide gift cards for partial attendance. Gift cards will be emailed after the session to the same email address used to register and join the session.
Space is limited, and registration is offered on a first-come, first-served basis. title: What Can the University Be?
location: 519 Kaneff Tower
description:
A Conversation on Academic Freedom, Freedom of Expression, and the Future of Higher Education
Universities are being asked to do many things at once: defend free inquiry, navigate competing convictions, support community well-being, and demonstrate public value. Join us for a timely discussion on the role of the university as a public institution and the conditions that make meaningful dialogue across difference possible.
Keynote Address
Shannon Dea, Professor of Philosophy, Saint Mary’s University
“The Sheeran Effect? Institutional Neutrality, Scholarly Commitment, and the Academic Mission”
Respondent
Paul Axelrod, Professor Emeritus, Faculty of Education, York University
Drawing on their rich scholarship and depth of expertise, speakers will situate current tensions and opportunities around academic freedom, freedom of expression, academic community, care, and civility.
Join the Conversation
Join us for an engaging dialogue exploring the university as a vital public institution and the conditions needed for intellectual openness, productive disagreement, and meaningful exchange across differences while sustaining communities of learning.

Date: October 6, 2026 
Time: 2:30PM-4PM 
Location: 519 Kaneff Tower

Registration Link

What to Expect

Discover Veeva: Learn about Veeva’s mission as a Public Benefit Corporation, the Engineering Development Program (EDP), and upcoming entry-level opportunities.

title: Murder Mystery Double Book Launch
location: Ben McNally Books
description:
[at Ben McNally Books]
Join us at Ben McNally Books, as we celebrate the launches of two murder mysteries:
A Killing Cold
by Alice Fitzpatrick, and
Murder by Nordic Design
by A.L. Jensen
About the Books:
A Killing Cold
THE THIRD BOOK IN THE MEREDITH ISLAND MYSTERIES
It’s Christmas on Meredith Island, and Kate Galway is looking forward to spending some mother-daughter time with her barrister daughter, Alex.  But Kate is forced to adjust her plans when Alex arrives accompanied by her father, Detective Chief Inspector James Hewitt, Kate’s ex-husband.  The island’s matriarch, Sophie Sutherland, is eager to reunite with her old beau, Teddy Bartell, who shows up with an entourage of relations, including his son, the son’s abrasive second wife, and her twin brother.
Everyone joins in the Christmas celebrations at the pub, but the party comes to an abrupt end when someone ingests a lethal dose of cyanide.  A winter storm has shut down access to the mainland, trapping the killer on the island.  With no forensics and minimal support from the mainland police, James, Kate, and Alex must rely on old-fashioned detective work to track down the murderer before they strike again.
Murder by Nordic Design
A Hygge House Nordic Cozy Mystery 

​
Lakewood’s Fall Fair is fast approaching, but when Minna finds a dead body, can she catch a killer before the town’s biggest event becomes its deadliest?


Hygge House kicks into high gear for Lakewood’s most popular annual event. Minna Halonen and her best friend and business partner Christie Andersson prepare for the onslaught of tourists while James’s crew works to finish their new sauna in time.
As part of the fair’s planning committee, Elsi buzzes around town, while Sofia’s social media side hustle is turning into a real job.

​

On the day of the Fall Fair, Minna invites her guests to christen the newly built sauna, only to be stunned when she discovers the corpse of a carpenter. A fair’s opening has never been so foul.
Murder by Nordic Design
is the third book in the delightful Hygge House Mystery series—where murder meets Nordic comfort in a rustic northern town.

title: Author Talk with Briony Penn: The Seabird Trials
description:
Award-winning writer, naturalist and environmental activist,
Briony Penn
, will discuss her new book,
Seabird Trials: How A Scientist Took Big Oil to Court and Won
. At a time when scientists are increasingly questioned and silenced, Penn will share stories of resilience and restoration both by the seabirds themselves after one of the deadliest oil spills in the Pacific, and by those entrusted with their protection.
Penn will be in conversation with
Louise Blight
, author of
Where the Earth Meets the Sky
:
a Story of Penguins, People, and Place in Antarctica.
Learn how oil spills and climate change have impacted even the wildest, most remote corners of the earth by the industries that benefit, and the extraordinary lengths people who love the natural world will go to protect it—against all odds.
Presented as part of Women's History Month and Science Literacy Week, and as part of TPL's environmental program series,
Our Fragile Planet
, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.

title: Does Canada Need a National Portrait Gallery?
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Join four leading voices to imagine what could be one of Canada’s most significant cultural institutions yet to be built.
Canadians are experiencing a renewed sense of who we are and why it matters to be us – is now the time to respond to decades of demand for a National Portrait Gallery?
While the majority of countries include portraits of their 'great and good' in their history museums, art galleries, archives and monuments; some countries have chosen a more democratic path – creating stand-alone National Institutions in their capital cities that celebrate not only the political and military greats, but also the change-makers in every walk of life, age, ethnicity and talent. Canada has no institutional equivalent – is this a quiet statement about our national character and preference for practical leadership over hero-worship, or a decentralized sense of identity that resists a single national narrative? Or is it simply an overlooked institutional gap that deserves to be filled?
Acclaimed UK-based architect Jamie Fobert, celebrated Indigenous curator and historian Tim Johnson, and writer and activist Sarah Lazarovic join moderator Gail Lord for a wide-ranging conversation about what such an institution could mean for the country.
Together they’ll examine the case for a National Portrait Gallery: what it might contain, how it could meaningfully include and center Indigenous voices and communities, where it might be located, and how it could be funded and supported – including whether the political will currently exists to make it a reality. The panel will also consider what a distinctly Canadian portrait gallery might look like in contrast to its counterparts in the United States, United Kingdom, and Australia, and what unique story it could tell about the nation and its people.
Q&A to follow.
About this event’s guests:

Sarah Lazarovic

title: Susan Stryker's Toronto BOOK LAUNCH for Changing Gender
location: Glad Day (32 Lisgar), 32 Lisgar
description: In a very rare Toronto appearance, legendary trans trailblazer SUSAN STRYKER will join us at Glad Day to launch her new book. It's the TORONTO BOOK LAUNCH for Susan Stryker's CHANGING GENDER Schedule: 7pm - Doors 7:30pm - Introduction by Sheila Cavanagh 7:40pm - Presentation on the Legacy of Susan Stryker by Toby Anne Finlay 7:50pm - Interview with Susan Stryker and Sheila Cavanagh 8:30pm - Questions and Answers with the Audience 9:00pm - Book Signing and Social RSVP This event is FREE to attend. We strongly encourage you to RSVP to attend, which helps us with our planning. This event is made possible, in part, by a SSHRC research grant held by Dr. Sheila Cavanagh at York University. Changing Gender is a provocative, genre-bending call to reconsider the story we tell about gender itself. With the far right weaponizing the rhetoric of anti-gender ideology and increasingly targeting the lives of transgender people, one question becomes ever more urgent and contested: What are we even talking about when we talk about gender? Where did the concept itself come from, and where might it go? In Changing Gender, the leading trans scholar Susan Stryker invites readers to join her lifelong quest to uncover what gender means and does. She traces the concept’s roots in grammar and shows how it has been transformed into a battleground in the culture wars. From the origins of “Yankee Doodle” to acid trips in Joshua Tree National Park, from nineteenth-century phrenology to present-day anti-trans conspiracy theorists, Stryker finds surprising places to tap into the origins, idiosyncrasies, and generative possibilities of the gender concept. Along the way, she weaves in stories drawn from her lifetime as a pathbreaking historian, filmmaker, activist, and founding figure of transgender studies. Poignant and deeply researched, lyrical and authoritative, Changing Gender exposes the limiting assumptions about gender that span the political spectrum and imagines what life might look like if some of those limitations were lifted. Ultimately, Stryker argues, to change gender is to change what it means to be human—and to change reality itself. Published by Farrar, Straus and Giroux. Susan Stryker’s historical research, theoretical writings, media-making, activism, and academic field-building activities have helped shape the conversation on trans issues since the early 1990s. Susan retired from the University of Arizona as Professor of Gender and Women's Studies in 2020, and currently holds a distinguished visiting appointment at Stanford University's Michelle Clayman Institute for Gender Research. Related forthcoming Special Issues of Australian Feminist Studies: one on Susan Stryker’s legacy and a second on trans studies more broadly ‍

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions.
Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle.

title: Author Talk with Dr. Kirsten Johnson on Humanitarienne: A Doctor’s Stories from the Conflict Zone
description:
As a physician and public health specialist,
Dr. Kirsten Johnson
has led missions in conflict zones, disaster-stricken regions and underserved communities. In her book,
Humanitarienne
: A Doctor's Stories from the Conflict Zone
, she traces how a strict childhood marked by trauma pushed her to seek independence early.
Join this 1-hour presentation where Johnson shares her story as a global health expert working in some of the world's most volatile places and how she pushed back on inequities embedded in humanitarian systems. If you're drawn to international work, social justice, or the ways in which people are shaped by—and in turn shape the world around them, this presentation will inspire you.
Johnson will be in conversation with Cindy Schwartz, a Professional Goal-Centric  Coach certified through Concordia University.
Presented as part of Women's History Month.

title: Oct 7 - Building Composable Vision Workflows in FiftyOne
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
This workshop explores the [FiftyOne](https://docs.voxel51.com/index.html) plugin framework to build custom computer vision applications. You’ll learn to extend the FiftyOne App with Python based panels and server side operators, as well as integrate external tools for labeling, vector search, and model inference into your dataset views.

**Date, Time and Location**

Oct 7, 2026
9 AM - 10 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/building-composable-vision-workflows-in-fiftyone-october-7-2026)**

You’ll also automate repetitive tasks by writing custom workflows executing within the FiftyOne environment. Attendees will learn to transform FiftyOne from a visualization tool into a central hub for your vision stack.

What you'll learn:

* **Build Python plugins.** Define plugin manifests and directory structures to register custom functionality within the FiftyOne ecosystem.
* **Develop server side operators.** Write functions to execute model inference, data cleaning, or metadata updates from the App interface.
* **Build interactive panels.** Create custom UI dashboards using to visualize model metrics or specialized dataset distributions.
* **Manage operator execution contexts.** Pass data between the App front end and your backend to build dynamic user workflows.
* **Implement delegated execution.** Configure background workers to handle long running data processing tasks without blocking the user interface.
* **Build labeling integrations.** Streamline the flow of data between FiftyOne and annotation platforms through custom triggers and ingestion scripts.
* **Extend vector database support.** Program custom connectors for external vector stores to enable semantic search across large sample datasets.
* **Package and share plugins.** Distribute your extensions internally and externally

title: Sociology Indigenous Lecture Series: The Worst Trickster Story Ever Told: Understanding American Law Through an Indigenous Lens
location: 802 South Ross Building @ 4700 Keele Street, Toronto ON, M3J 1P3
description:
Join us as guest speaker professor Keith Richotte Jr. examines how the U.S. doctrine of plenary power—granting sweeping authority over Native American nations—came to be understood as constitutional, despite its origins in deeply flawed and outdated assumptions. Through a distinctive blend of legal analysis and Native history, Richotte, Jr. explores when and why this transformation occurred, and what it reveals about constitutional interpretation today. Centring Indigenous perspectives and the tradition of trickster stories, the talk invites audiences to rethink this history and imagine a more just, equitable and constitutional future.

title: AI Dialogues: On Creative Industries
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space
description:
The creative industries are being disrupted at a scale and speed unlike anything they've encountered before. Artificial intelligence can now generate images, write scripts, compose music, and simulate voices. What's at stake goes far beyond technology. It cuts to the heart of authorship, labour, ownership, and the value we place on human expression.
In this program, two voices at the intersection of AI and the creative industry join us for a discussion about what this moment makes possible and the challenges and risks it presents.
Our speakers:
Ana Serrano is President and Vice-Chancellor of OCAD University, co-founder of DemocracyXChange, and an award-winning leader in digital media and cultural innovation. She previously founded the CFC Media Lab and IDEABOOST at the Canadian Film Centre and has helped shape national conversations on democracy, technology, and culture.
Ryan Patterson is the creative director at Queen One Studios, an AI-native studio working in film/tv, ads and education. With over a decade of video production experience in advertising and communications, he has been featured in Variety and Deadline, spoken at the Toronto International Film Festival and Adobe MAX, and was named a Top 100 AI Creative on LinkedIn.
Moderated by author, scholar and researcher Paolo Granata (University of Toronto), these two leading voices bring the full tension of this moment into focus, not to resolve it, but to help us think more clearly and critically about it. After their dialogue, the conversation moves into the room. You'll be invited to discuss in small groups, then join an open exchange with both speakers. No conclusion is required.
This AI Dialogues program is presented in collaboration with the Provocation Ideas Festival.
*********
About the AI Dialogues
Artificial intelligence is reshaping nearly every dimension of human life, how we work, how we govern, how we heal, how we connect. And yet, for all its momentum, the conversation around AI is fragmented: hype on one side, fear on the other, and very little space in between for genuine, grounded exchange. The AI Dialogues is a series that creates that space.
Each program brings together two voices - experts, practitioners, and thinkers who have earned their perspectives through experience - to explore a single topic through the lens of AI's promise and its challenges. Then opens the floor, inviting audiences into small group discussion before bringing every voice into a shared dialogue.
The goal is not consensus. It is clarity - the kind that only comes from sitting with complexity, listening across disagreement, challenging our assumptions, and resisting the urge to resolve what isn't yet resolved.
AI will shape the future. How we think and talk about it will shape it even more.

Womp 3D is a free, browser-based tool that allows users to create and export 3D models quick and easy. title: We Need To Talk About AI: AI for the Non-Technical

description:
Curious about Artificial Intelligence (AI)?
Join us to learn about and discuss aspects of this technological innovation.
This workshop series explores AI's real impacts on jobs, privacy, the environment, and our communities, while discussing how we can shape it responsibly. Each themed 90-minute session allows for small group discussion, practical takeaways and honest conversation about AI without the hype.
Oct 7 - AI for the Non-Technical
In this session, we tackle the
"Elephant in the Room"
—addressing ethics, hallucinations, and the fear of replacement to foster a responsible
"AI for Good"
mindset. We demystify the technology by viewing AI as an
"intern with a PhD in everything"
—a tool that masters five specific superpowers, such as personalization at scale and rapid research, while leaving the irreplaceable domain of empathy, intuition, and creativity to you.
Oct 14 - How Do We Shape AI?
AI is already reshaping how we work, protect our privacy, and participate in society—yet most of us never get a seat at the table in deciding how it's built or used. This session creates that space. Equal parts presentation and conversation,

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Leader Dialogue: From Tension to Teamwork (for people managers)
description:
Tension and conflict are a normal part of working relationships—especially during change, high workload, or moments of unclear expectations. What matters most is not avoiding conflict, but how managers recognize it early, respond productively, and use it to strengthen trust and performance. This interactive 90 minute session helps people managers build confidence and capability in navigating tension and everyday conflict. Managers will practice practical tools for addressing misunderstandings, surfacing differing perspectives, and resetting strained relationships—before issues escalate or harden. Through discussion, reflection, and real world scenarios, participants will leave better equipped to move teams from friction to forward progress.
Key Learning Outcomes:
– Reframe tension in times of change as a typical and workable dynamic, and differentiate healthy tension from unresolved conflict or relationship breakdown.
– Identify personal and team conflict patterns by noticing early signs of tension, common triggers, and default responses, and understanding how these patterns show up during periods of change.
– Apply practical conversation tools to address tensions respectfully—surfacing concerns, naming impact, inviting perspective, and leading reset conversations that maintain shared expectations without blame or escalation.
Organized by Organizational Effectiveness and Well-Being, Human Resources

Audience: York University People Managers and HR professionals

title: Reliable Multi-Agent Systems: Orchestration, State, and Human Approval
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
Adding more agents does not automatically create a better system. Multi-agent solutions need clear responsibilities, controlled execution, recoverable state, and carefully designed decision boundaries.

In this session, we will extend the agent built in Episode 1 into a coordinated incident-management workflow. Specialist agents will handle triage, knowledge retrieval, impact assessment, and remediation planning. We will use Microsoft Agent Framework to demonstrate sequential, concurrent, and handoff orchestration patterns, and discuss where each pattern is appropriate.

The workflow will introduce typed state, checkpointing, failure recovery, and human-in-the-loop approval before any sensitive remediation action can continue. We will also separate deterministic application logic from agentic reasoning, showing which decisions should be handled by an AI agent and which should remain enforced by conventional code.

Attendees will see how a multi-agent workflow behaves when interrupted, how it resumes from saved state, and how human approval can be incorporated without losing execution context.

By the end of the session, attendees will be able to design controlled multi-agent workflows that combine AI judgment with reliable business-process execution. Key topics: Multi-agent orchestration patterns Sequential, concurrent, and handoff workflows Typed workflow state Checkpointing and recovery Human-in-the-loop approvals Agentic versus deterministic steps Failure handling and idempotency.

This session is a part of a series, learn more here! [https://aka.ms/ProBadgeSeries-TY](https://aka.ms/ProBadgeSeries-TY)

title: Oct 8 - MCP, Agents and Skills Meetup Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on MCP, agents and skills.

**Date, Time and Location**

Oct 08, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/mcp-agents-skills-meetup-october-8-2026)**

**Designing Multi‑Agent Systems: Sequential, Parallel, and Beyond with ADK**

Multi‑agent systems are powerful but choosing the wrong interaction pattern can quickly lead to fragile, slow, or expensive AI systems.
In this talk, we explore the core multi‑agent design patterns enabled by ADK, including sequential, parallel, and more advanced coordination models. Rather than focusing on tools alone, we’ll look at how to think architecturally about agent collaboration.

You’ll learn:

* When sequential agents are the right choice and when they become a bottleneck
* How parallel agents improve speed and coverage (and the trade‑offs they introduce)
* Common failure modes in poorly designed agent interactions
* Practical criteria for choosing the right pattern based on task, latency, and reliability

By the end of the session, you’ll have a clear mental model for designing multi‑agent systems that are intentional, scalable, and production‑ready.

*About the Speaker*

[Dr Roushanak Rahmat](https://www.linkedin.com/in/roushanakrahmat/) is an Enterprise AI Architect, Google Developer Expert (AI & Cloud), and recognized among the Top 100 Women in Tech (2025). With a PhD in Artificial Intelligence and over 15 years of experience, she specializes in designing and delivering enterprise-scale Generative AI, Agentic AI, and Deep Learning solutions that transform industries including healthcare, finance, energy, and public services.

**Privacy by Deployment: Architecting Agent-Driven Localization Workflows for Regulated Environments**

Most enterprise AI today is private by promise - a DPA, a SOC 2 report, or a contract clause that says, "we won't train on your data". For a regulated buyer, these are remedies after a breach, not controls that prevent or contain one. For organizations in healthcare, finance, defense, and government, privacy often requires stronger guarantees: data residency, customer-controlled execution, and, in some cases, operation within air-gapped environments.

This session demonstrates how agentic AI can automate a localization workflow while operating within these constraints. Using a real-world localization pipeline as an example, we will show how agentic systems can coordinate translation, review, quality assurance, and content preparation tasks while incorporating human checkpoints for approval and oversight.

We will also walk through the architectural patterns that enable these workflows to run inside customer-controlled and air-gapped environments without transferring sensitive content outside the customer boundary. The session includes a live product demonstration.

Key Takeaways

* Architectural patterns for deploying agentic AI in air-gapped and customer-controlled environments
* How agentic systems can automate localization workflows while preserving critical human review and approval processes
* Practical considerations for operating agentic workflows in regulated environments with auditability and governance requirements

*About the Speaker*

[Shruti Joshi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/28shruti) is building an AI powered secure localization stack for regulated industries such as healthcare, legal, finance that cannot send their content to a typical hosted SaaS. She brings 12+ years of engineering and architecture experience to the question this talk addresses: how do you make an agentic AI system deployable inside a regulated perimeter.

**MCP Is the Interface; Skills Are the Operating Discipline**

This talk shows how MCP and Agent Skills work together in practical agent systems. MCP gives agents a standard interface to tools, data, and workflows; skills encode the operating discipline that makes those connections reliable. Using a sanitized field-operations ledger as the case study, the talk walks through source intake, normalized state, uncertainty labels, role prompts, QA gates, and share-safe status drafting.

*About the Speaker*

[Chuck Hernandez](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chuck-hernandez/) is an AI engineering and client-delivery leader with 10+ years across software, data platforms, and enterprise implementation, including 3+ years shipping production GenAI systems.

**Agentic engineering is about good guidance.**

Garbage Inn. Is garbage out? This is true. For many input and output processes. In biological life and in computer systems, and equally true when working with LLM’s. The better the prompt, the better the context, the better the focus, And the better the contextual awareness, the better the quality of the output the LLM’s generates.
This is the governance, art and practice of what we like to call agentic engineering, something I've been practicing over the last year.

*About the Speaker*

[Dimitri Geelen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dimitrigeelen/) builds things that don't need him once they're done. Frameworks, transitions, agentic systems — the measure of success is always the same: does it hold up when he leaves the room? He understands not just how to deploy, but what it takes for a new service to survive and scale inside a complex enterprise.

title: Vincent Lao (University of Montana)
location: CITA Bridge
description:
Title: Nonlinear Dynamical Tides in Highly Eccentric Binaries: Application to Repeating TDEs and Hot Jupiters

Abstract: Dynamical tides exhibit chaotic growth within highly eccentric binaries (>~0.9) to reach a significant energy comparable to the binding energy. As a result, the critical separation for mass transfer, known as the Roche limit, can be significantly modified from the classical results based on equilibrium tides. Using an affine approximation, we analytically derive the nonlinear tidal coupling coefficients up to the four-mode perturbation level and apply them into the tidal evolution of a binary. This allows us to explore the onset of tidal disruption from first-principles hydrodynamical calculations. In this talk, I will discuss the implementation of this framework in two distinct systems: (1) repeating tidal disruption events (TDEs) near massive black holes, (2) high-eccentricity migration of Hot Jupiters. In (1), we propose a new mechanism to generate repeating bursts from a massive black hole-star binary at irregular time intervals via accumulation of tidal energy across multiple orbits, which we call “diffusive-tide disruptions”, in contrast to the common “prompt disruption” scenario where the disruption occurs at every pericenter passage. The mechanism offers a natural explanation of the burst time fluctuations in J0651 that previous models struggle to reproduce. In (2), we study the tidal evolution of a migrating gaseous planet, focusing on the suppression of tidal energy growth, hence mass loss, due to nonlinear damping. We show that it opens up the high eccentricity region of the parameter space for a planet to complete the migration to become a Hot Jupiter without being tidally disrupted. The mechanism can potentially resolve the issue of underpredicting the formation rate of Hot Jupiters in earlier work.

Open to all
Host: Norman Murray

title: Key Ingredients for Child and Family Well-Being
description:
Family life can be rewarding – but it can also be challenging, particularly when work, school, and other demands compete for our time and attention. Join Dr. Heather Prime, a child psychologist, and Gillian Shoychet, a clinical-developmental doctoral student, from the York University Psychology Clinic for an engaging, research-informed session exploring the key ingredients for fostering family and child well-being. We will discuss how family stress can affect relationships and what helps parents work effectively as a team. We will also explore skills for supporting children’s emotional and behavioural well-being, including emotion coaching and other evidence-informed parenting strategies. The session will conclude by highlighting some of the family-focused supports available through the York University Psychology Clinic.

title: Ralph Pudritz (McMaster University)
location: MP1318A
description:
Title: Reading Between the Rings: Protoplanetary Dust Rings as Probes and Sites of Planet Formation

Abstract: The dust rings in protoplanetary disks are generally thought to be formed within the pressure bumps that are created by forming planets that reside in the resulting gaps.  Hence, ring properties should reflect the planet’s mass.  At the same time, ALMA observations have shown that these rings harbor many tens of Earth masses of dust.  Do rings also give rise to planet formation?  In this talk I present recent work on both aspects of this intriguing question.  Using 2D hydro (FARGO) simulations of planet-disk interaction, we show that the ring’s dust mass, peak location, and width correlate with planet mass.  In particular, the standoff distance between the ring peak and the planet’s orbital radius depends on the Hill radius of the planet – and hence its mass.  We apply these results to predict the masses of planets in well observed disk systems – PDS 70 and WISPIT2.   I then turn to our work on dust agglomeration and concentration in generalized Gaussian pressure bumps characterized by an amplitude and width (A,w). We  address the question of what conditions are necessary and sufficient to trigger planetesimal and planet formation to be in such pressure bumps by sufficient dust concentrations.  We use the DustPy dust- gas evolution code coupled to the N-body SyMBAp to explore two different disk models characterized by the Stokes number (the aerodynamic size of a grain) at which grains fragment by collisions, across a wide range of values of (A,w).  We find that the amplitude A is the primary factor governing both the mass of the single most massive planet and the total planetary mass assembled within the first generation formed in the primary pressure bump.  Finally, we explore the conditions by which planets formed in the primary bump can excite gaps and pressure bumps at larger radii sufficient to host 2nd and 3rd generation planets.
Host: Shantanu Basu

title: ROTMAN Author Talk:  Power of Situations
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
We attend various ROTMAN events each year. Author Talks. Book Releases. Visiting Professors.

### **Agenda:**

5:00 pm - Check-in opens + light refreshments
5:30 pm - Author presentation and moderated Q&A
6:30 pm - Meet-and-greet with author + book signing

### **Book Synopsis:**

**From the #1 bestselling author of *Grit,* a new book that reveals the hidden power of situations—and how you can shape them to bring out your best.**

Angela Duckworth, PhD, is the bestselling author of *Grit* and the founder and CEO of Character Lab. A 2013 MacArthur Fellow, she is a professor of psychology at the University of Pennsylvania.

**In Angela Duckworth’s first book, she showed that a common denominator of successful strivers is a blend of passion and perseverance she dubbed “grit.**”

Ticket link is below. $22-$45

This second book springs from her deepening realization that grit, while necessary, is sometimes not sufficient. How you situate yourself to meet a challenge can be crucial.
Duckworth’s in-depth research reveals the enormous influence wielded by the objects within arm’s reach, your peers and mentors, and even your zip code. Though you’re often told to make the best of your situation, it is far, far better to make your situation better first.

**In *Situated*, you’ll discover:**

* Why your personality changes, sometimes dramatically, from one situation to another—and how you can harness that shift
* The secret to conquering temptation *without* willpower
* Why taking the less effortful path can feel like cheating but often solves a stubborn problem
* How the company you keep shapes the person you become
* The most effective ways to help others succeed

***TICKET Link here-***-

https://www.rotman.utoronto.ca/news-events-and-ideas/public-events/events-listings/2026/october-2026/oct-8---angela-duckworth/

title: Peek Inside an AI Assistant: How It Thinks and Works
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
You've asked an AI chatbot questions. But there's another kind of AI that doesn't just answer: it acts.
In this demo-driven talk, we'll look deeply at always-on personal AI assistants. The assistant can read your files, use your apps, and remember what you've told it, growing more useful over time. The same powers that let it help you can hurt you if something goes wrong. We'll also open up what happens inside: the hidden instructions, the tools it uses, what it remembers and forgets.
Then we'll look at the AI assistant that helped develop this workshop, and how we shaped our workflow together, and why.

Augustus Durham, Assistant Professor of English at the University of Toronto and author of Stay Black and Die: On Melancholy and Genius, for an evening of Black literature, scholarship and conversation.

In Inhabitants of the Deep, Howard undertakes a Black ecocritical study of the “deep”, encompassing oceans, rivers, lakes and the notion of depth itself, and its place within African American literature and expressive culture. Drawing on figures ranging from Olaudah Equiano and Herman Melville to Otis Redding and August Wilson, Howard traces Black relationships to water, ecology and the histories of the Middle Passage, ultimately considering the deep as a site not only of displacement and exclusion, but of Black ecological life.

Join Howard and Durham for a thought-provoking conversation exploring Black literature, history, culture and intellectual life.

Thursday, October 8, 2026 | 6:00–8:00 p.m.
Blackhurst Cultural Centre | 777–779 Bathurst Street, Toronto

Admission is free. Registration is required.

title: Paper Trail: Writing and Walking by Sarah Ellis
location: Lillian H. Smith, Lower Level-Auditorium
description:
Photo credit: Thelonius Mthombeni
Join award-winning author, teacher and librarian Sarah Ellis for the upcoming 38th Annual Helen E. Stubbs Memorial Lecture at our Osborne Collection of Early Children’s Books.
The word that best describes Sarah's career in writing is "meander." In this presentation she will tell stories about her work and her wanders, including the pleasures of flaneuring, both on the page and on her feet, the winding journey from grade four essay to substack via a long detour in children's fiction, her beloved companions of the road, the importance of good socks and good colleagues, the inevitable, scary and productive experience of getting lost, and the odd tendency of humans to walk counterclockwise when left to wander freely (true fact!). Come prepared for detours.
Sarah Ellis is the award-winning author of over twenty-five books for children and young adults. In 2013 she was awarded the B.C. Lieutenant Governor’s Award for Literary Excellence. She is a three-time Canadian nominee for the prestigious Astrid Lindgren Memorial Award. Having retired as a children’s librarian and then retired from college teaching she is now writing and reading fulltime in the rain in Vancouver, sharing her bookish thoughts online at "Wild Reading" on substack. Her latest book for children is As Glenn as Can Be illustrated by Nancy Vo, published by Groundwood Books and she has a recent adult memoir, My Year in Fairyland: Grief, MAID and a Lifetime of Reading published by Stonehewer Books.

title: 🌙🍂 Fall Evening Walk: High Park & Ghost Stories 👻
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🌙🍂 **Fall Evening Walk: High Park & Ghost Stories** 👻

### Fall Colours, Spooky Stories & A Different Way to Spend Your Evening

Looking for something a little different to do after work?

Join us for an **evening walk through High Park**, where we'll enjoy the fall colours while stopping along the way for some of the park's stranger, spookier, and downright weird stories.
High Park has a long history of ghost stories and local legends.

From stories connected to the **War of 1812** — yes, *that* War of 1812 — to tales of mysterious deaths and people who may not have completely left the park behind, there's plenty of history to make an ordinary fall walk a little more interesting.
But don't worry.

**This isn't a terrifying ghost hunt.** 👻

Think **fall colours, creepy stories, a little history, a few laughs, and just enough spooky atmosphere to make you look over your shoulder once or twice.**

It's a relaxed way to get outside after work, explore one of Toronto's most beautiful parks, and experience High Park as the daylight starts to disappear. 🍂🌙

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 👻 What We'll Do

We'll walk through **High Park**, stopping at different locations along the way while I share stories connected to the park's history and ghostly legends.
Along the way we'll:

* Explore some of High Park's most interesting locations
* Hear stories of ghosts, legends, and strange events 👻
* Learn a little about the park's history
* Take photos and enjoy the scenery 📸
* Have some Halloween fun along the way 🎃

We'll keep a steady walking pace, with regular stops for storytelling.
The walk will remain **outside throughout** — there is no entry into buildings.

***

## 🎃 Halloween Day — So Let's Have Some Fun

This isn't meant to be a serious paranormal investigation.

Some stories are creepy. Some are strange. Some might make you wonder whether there's actually something going on.
And some are just a good excuse to tell a spooky story while walking through the fall leaves.

**You don't have to believe in ghosts.**
You just have to enjoy a good story.

***

## 🍁 Fall Weather & Expectations

This is an outdoor walk, so please dress appropriately for the weather.
High Park can be cool and damp in late October, so bring a warm jacket and wear comfortable walking shoes.
We'll be walking at a steady pace, with stops along the way for stories and photos.

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Location:** High Park sign on the west side at Bloor Street West & High Park Avenue
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time:** **6:30pm sharp**
I will only wait **5 minutes.**
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🚶 **Pace:** Steady walking pace
🏁 **End Point:** Back where we started

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$10 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This is a **curated, guided storytelling experience**, rather than one of our regular group walks. The route, stories, and history have been researched and developed specifically for this experience.

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🧥 Warm fall jacket or layers
📸 Camera or phone
🎃 Halloween spirit
And if you want to wear a costume...
**I'm certainly not going to stop you.** 👻

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This is great for:

* People who love Halloween 🎃
* Anyone who enjoys ghost stories
* Fall-colour enthusiasts 🍂
* History buffs
* People looking for something different to do on Halloween Day
* Anyone who enjoys a good story and a few laughs
* People who want to meet new people while exploring Toronto

You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**

**Come for the fall colours.** 🍂
**Stay for the ghost stories.** 👻
**Leave with a new connection — if the ghosts don't get you first.** 🎃

title: Becoming an Illustrator
description:
Join us for an online special career series with the
2026 Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence
, Elly MacKay! In this series, Elly will share insights into building a career in children’s book illustration, covering topics such as the journey to working as an illustrator, an overview of classic children’s books, portfolios, and colour. Details about each session follow:
Thursday, October 8, 7pm:
Becoming an Illustrator
Elly MacKay shares her early and current work, her career path, and her process for creating miniature 3D worlds. Her talk also covers developing your style, illustration trends, and how to stand out.
Thursday, October 15, 7pm: Looking at Picture Books
Elly MacKay gives an overview of famous picture books, the various styles, what works, and how they’ve changed over the years. She looks at cover design, structure, page turns, and how visual storytelling and words work together.
Thursday, October 22, 7pm: From Portfolio to Book
Elly MacKay discusses portfolios and what to include, as well as working with agents and publishers. She also looks at what goes into creating your first picture book.
Thursday, October 29, 7pm: Colour and Atmosphere
Elly MacKay considers colour in picture books—how it can be used to strengthen a message, or to alter the mood. She looks at how illustrators have used colour in unconventional ways in their books.
Workshops will be recorded and available for replay through Zoom until October 31, 2026.
About Elly MacKay
Elly MacKay is a children’s book author and illustrator and a paper artist. She studied printmaking and illustration at NSCAD University in Halifax and University of Canterbury in Christchurch. Elly creates miniature worlds with drawing, painting and cutting, and photographs them for illustrations in children’s books. She has more than 20 books published in Canada and the US, including The Enchanted Symphony by Julie Andrews and Emma Walton Hamilton, I Am a Meadow Mermaid and The Secret Fawn by Kallie George. Elly is both author and illustrator of Frostfire, In the Clouds and Red Sky at Night and others. She lives with her family in Owen Sound, Ontario.

program honours the memory of illustrator Joanne Fitzgerald (1956-2011), and is a joint program of IBBY Canada, Toronto Public Library, and the Young Family.

title: Tafelmusik at the Garden: Voices of the Violin
description:
Voices of the Violin explores the astonishing range of the unaccompanied violin across more than three centuries. Stripped of accompaniment, a single instrument becomes many: storyteller, dancer, orator, and virtuoso by turns. The program moves from the concise, improvisatory gestures of 17th- and 18th-century preludes and dances—by Corbett, Purcell, Lonati, Telemann, Vitali, Jacquet de La Guerre, and Vilsmaÿr—to the monumental unaccompanied works of Biber and Bach, before Andrew Balfour carries that same solitary voice into the present day. Across four centuries, the question remains constant: how can four strings speak with so many voices?

About Tafelmusik
Every now and then a group of musicians comes along and changes the way we think about music. For over four decades, Tafelmusik has been synonymous worldwide with dynamic, engaging, and soulful performances informed by scholarship, passion and artistic excellence. 
Performing on instruments and in styles appropriate to the era, Tafelmusik has performed in more than 350 cities in 32 countries. Its extensive discography on the Sony, CBC Records, Analekta and Tafelmusik Media labels have garnered ten JUNOs and numerous international recording prizes. From a vibrant home season in Toronto, to international tours, award-winning recordings, innovative collaborations, and inspiring education programs, Tafelmusik is a musical powerhouse with a reputation for thrilling and delighting audiences. www.tafelmusik.org

title: After the Island: Caribbean Canadian Ceramics
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
After the Island: Caribbean Canadian Ceramics                                                                           
        
    




	

	

	


			
Events
	









	

    
        
             
                
                    

October 9, 2026 – April 25, 2027
Exhibition Hall. Third Floor
Included with admission. Free for Gardiner Members



                
                    
    



    
         
    




	


  Get Tickets



  Become a Member






    
         
    






    
        
             
                
                    The Gardiner Museum, Black Artists’ Networks in Dialogue (BAND), and the Museum of the African Diaspora (MoAD) present a landmark curatorial partnership exploring contemporary ceramic practices rooted in Caribbean histories, memory, and cultural transformation. 
Presented across two exhibitions and two cities—Toronto and San Francisco—this collaboration brings together artists whose work examines migration, ornament, labour, ancestry, and the enduring impact of Caribbean cultural traditions across generations and geographies. 
At the Gardiner Museum, After the Island: Caribbean Canadian Ceramics considers how artists of the Caribbean diaspora are embracing the medium of ceramics to explore themes of knowledge transfer and the liberatory potential of the clandestine. Through existing and new work by Caribbean Canadian artists PJ Anderson, Eddy Firmin, Manuel Mathieu, and Sharon Norwood, the exhibition approaches questions of identity, belonging, memory, and cultural continuity through the language of clay. 
At MoAD, After the Island: Ornament and Ceramic Practice in the Jamaican Diaspora focuses on artists whose practices engage Jamaica as memory, inheritance, orientation, and cultural touchstone. The exhibition examines how ornament functions as a carrier of history, labour, ancestral knowledge, and relation across time and distance. 
Together, After the Island: Caribbean Canadian Ceramics and After the Island: Ornament and Ceramic Practice in the Jamaican Diaspora offer a timely exploration of migration, memory, and cultural continuity, demonstrating how artists working with clay continue to create new forms of relation between past and present, homeland and diaspora, history and imagination. 
Throughout both presentations, vessels, decorative forms, sculptural installations, and ceramic surfaces become sites where histories are preserved, challenged, reimagined, and carried forward. 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    NOTICE: Scented Exhibition 
Some artworks in this exhibition include scent. If you are sensitive to odors, please be advised.

title: Navigating the Healthcare System: Know Your Options. Know Your Rights.
description:
Not sure where to go when you need medical care? Wondering whether to visit a walk-in clinic, urgent care, the emergency department, or whether a pharmacist or virtual care provider can help?
Join the YFS Wellness Centre and Nurse Decoded for an interactive workshop designed to help students confidently navigate Ontario’s healthcare system and access the right care at the right time.
Topics include:
Understanding your healthcare options (family physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, pharmacists, virtual care, walk-in clinics, urgent care, and emergency departments)
Knowing your rights as a patient and how to advocate for yourself
Accessing mental health services and crisis supports
Understanding what happens during a mental health crisis, including common processes under Ontario’s Mental Health Act
When and how to seek a second opinion or access alternative healthcare services
Practical tips to help you navigate the healthcare system with confidence
Whether you’re new to Ontario, living away from home for the first time, or simply want to better understand how to access healthcare, this session will provide practical, real-world information that every student can use.

title: Ghost Stories of Toronto: Victorian Spirits
description:
The Victorian age is famously associated with ghost stories, and Victorian Toronto is certainly no exception. For the second talk in this series, author Adam Bunch will explore some of our city's spookiest supernatural tales from the late 1800s, an era that provides us with stories of haunted mansions, secret societies, and the spirits said to roam the halls of some of our finest public buildings.
About this event's guest:
Adam Bunch
Read More:
The Toronto Book of Love
The Toronto Book of the Dead
About this series:
You can learn a lot about Toronto through its ghost stories. Whether you believe in the supernatural or not, the tales we tell about spirits and spectres illuminate the true history of the city. They're often tied to dramatic stories of death and disaster, to fascinating historic sites, and to pivotal moments that helped shape our communities. In this series of talks by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore Toronto's past through tales of ghosts, séances and hauntings. Whether it's phantom horses from the War of 1812, the strange prime minister who believed in the occult, or the ghost who was arrested by the Toronto Police Morality Squad, these supernatural stories have a lot to teach us about the history of the place we call home.

title: Healthcare Careers Decoded: Is This the Right Program for Me?
description:
Not sure if you’re in the right program? Wondering what careers are actually available in healthcare beyond the ones you hear about most? Thinking about transferring programs, pursuing graduate studies, or exploring a different direction?
Join the YFS Wellness Centre and Nurse Decoded for an honest and interactive conversation exploring the many pathways into healthcare and how to determine which profession may be the right fit for you.
The session will feature healthcare professionals from a variety of disciplines sharing their personal journeys, career realities, and lessons learned, followed by an open audience discussion where no question is off limits.
Topics include:
What different healthcare professionals actually do
Career pathways, educational requirements, and opportunities for growth
Transferable skills and how one degree can lead to many different careers
Changing directions, returning to school, and career pivots
Common misconceptions about healthcare professions
Advice for students questioning whether they’re in the right program
Live audience Q&A with healthcare professionals
Whether you’re considering nursing, rehabilitation, mental health, medicine, allied health, public health, or simply exploring your options, this session is designed to help you make more informed decisions about your future with confidence.

title: Prompt Engineering con Copilot: construye prompts que realmente funcionen
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
¿Utilizas Copilot pero no siempre obtienes los resultados que esperas?

En esta sesión práctica aprenderemos a dejar de improvisar prompts y construiremos juntos un framework sencillo para crear instrucciones más claras, efectivas y reutilizables con Microsoft Copilot.

Trabajaremos con seis elementos: contexto, objetivo, información, restricciones, resultado esperado y criterios de evaluación. A través de ejemplos y demostraciones en vivo, transformaremos prompts simples en instrucciones estructuradas que los participantes podrán reutilizar y adaptar a situaciones reales.

El objetivo no es memorizar “el prompt perfecto”, sino aprender una metodología que permita diseñar, probar y mejorar nuestros propios prompts.

                    Join us for an evening of art and conversation in celebration of the opening of After the Island: Caribbean Canadian Ceramics. The panel will feature exhibiting artists PJ Anderson, Eddy Firmin, Manuel Mathieu, and Sharon Norwood, moderated by Joséphine Denis, Co-Director and Director of Curatorial Initiatives at the Black Artists’ Networks in Dialogue (BAND) and Dr. Sequoia Miller, Chief Curator and Deputy Director at the Gardiner Museum.

                    About the Artists
                    
                
                
                    PJ Anderson
                    
                
                
                    PJ Anderson is Jamaican Canadian /  Red River Métis Artist from Thompson, Manitoba, Canada. She is a recent MFA Graduate from the University of Manitoba and currently serves as Director of Programming 2024-2027 for the National Council on Education for the Ceramic Arts (NCECA). Anderson’s practice references everyday weaponizations and the systems that reinforce them. deconstructing threat narratives and highlighting the control of visceral fear. 
                            
            
        
    



    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    
                    
                
                
                    Eddy Firmin
                    
                
                
                    Born in Guadeloupe, Eddy Firmin is an artist-researcher, lecturer, curator and teacher who lives and works between Montreal and Halifax. He holds a PhD in Art Studies and Practices from the Université du Québec à Montréal and a Master’s degree from the École supérieure d’art et de design du Havre-Rouen (France). Firmin’s practice questions the transcultural logics of his identity and issues of power, while also seeking to decolonize the imagination in art. 
                            
            
        
    



    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    
                    
                
                
                    Manuel Mathieu
                    
                
                
                    Manuel Mathieu is a Haitian multidisciplinary artist based in Montreal working across painting, ceramics, olfaction, film, and installation. He holds an MFA from Goldsmiths, University of London. His practice investigates historical violence, erasure, and spiritual legacy through embodied relationships to memory, land, and the natural world. Mathieu’s artistic journey is deeply intertwined with his community. He has initiated and participated in various social and educational projects that use art as a tool for dialogue, care, and transmission, particularly with youth and underrepresented communities. 
 
                            
            
        
    



    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    
                    
                
                
                    Sharon Norwood
                    
                
                
                    Sharon Norwood is a Jamaican-born interdisciplinary artist whose practice spans ceramics, drawing, found objects, and installation. She holds a BFA from the University of South Florida and an MFA in Studio Art from Florida State University. Through material exploration and process-based experimentation, her work engages with race, labour, identity, and historical narratives, often examining how systems of power shape cultural memory and ways of seeing. A recurring motif in her practice is the curly line, which functions both as a formal gesture and a conceptual reference to Afro-textured hair and the Black body.

  * After you register & pay, you will be prompted to input your team name
  * Ensure everyone on your team signs up with the same team name, and you will be sat together
  * Reserving your ticket secures you a reservation at The Rec Room


How to register for the Community Table or attend solo:

  * If you are looking to meet new people and join a new team, please put "Community" under the team name prompt
  * You will be sat at our Community Table, where other individuals or smaller groups signed up happy to meet new people!
  * You can sign up for a community table with a friend or two, or solo!


Trivia details:

  * Questions include name the song, singer, finish the lyric, and more!
  * Team size is recommended 1-6 people. If you'd like to play with a larger team, 2 points per additional player over 6 will be deducted from your score, to a max of 8 people.
  * Top 3 teams win a $100 Rec Room giftcard!


Meet your host: Quizmaster Jess!

She's been hosting themed trivia nights for 7 years in Toronto and is such a vibe. Follow her on instagram: @quizmasterjess https://www.instagram.com/quizmasterjess/ .


SEE YOU THERE!

title: 🎬Movie: Other Mommy  -  Food & Drinks after the movie 🍿!
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
🎬 Let’s Go to the Movies (and Actually Talk… or Not)

Whether you're a film nerd, popcorn enthusiast, or just looking for a chill night out with interesting people — this one's for you.

We’re heading out to see a movie together, then grabbing food or drinks after. If the film's great (or terrible), we’ll probably talk about it forever. If it’s just okay, we’ll talk about it for 10 minutes and move on to everything else — books, dating apps, weird dreams, how Toronto keeps getting more expensive, etc.

The vibe is relaxed, friendly, and not too serious. No film degree needed. No icebreakers. No pressure to “perform.” Just come enjoy the film, connect with some thoughtful people, and see where the night goes Click here to watch trailer!

🎞️ **Movie Title + Trailer:**[ \[Click here to watch trailer!\]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pPxrX9ukWBY)

📖 **📖 Plot Summary:** A terrifying, supernatural trip into the darkening world of a young girl as her family, and their home, are haunted by a sinister entity that is determined to take up residence inside her. But first, it needs to persuade her to let it in …

title: Indigenous Beading Workshop: Flat Stitch Ojibway Flower
description:
Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026
Time: 11:00 am – 2:00 pm ( Doors 10:45 am)
Location: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St. W.
Tickets: $65 General
Age Restriction: 16+ 
Join us for a day of creativity, connection, and cultural learning in this hands-on Indigenous beading workshop led by Natalie Ortiz. Participants will learn how to create beautiful Beaded Flat Stitch Ojibway Flowers while exploring the rich traditions and teachings behind this intricate art form.  
Guided step-by-step by Natalie, guests will be introduced to foundational beading techniques and design practices rooted in Indigenous traditions. Whether you are completely new to beading or looking to deepen your skills, this welcoming workshop offers an opportunity to slow down, learn through making, and create a meaningful handmade piece to take home. 
Recommended for participants 16+. Includes instruction, materials, and access to all current exhibitions.  
BUY YOUR TICKETS  
ABOUT NATALIE ORTIZ: 
 
Natalie Ortiz is a Toronto-based Indigenous artist. Her work focuses on handmade jewelry, moccasins, and leatherwork. Natalie is Anishinaabe of Wauzhushk Onigum Nation and of Peruvian decent. Her art carries deep meaning connected to her roots, reflecting the traditions and teachings passed down through generations. She learned beading and moccasin-making through traditional teachings. She has been making moccasins for five years, and every pair is crafted with intention, meant to be worn and appreciated by anyone who connects with them. Follow Natalie on social media for moccasins and leatherwork at @natymocs. Her jewelry can be found on Oliva’s Jewelry and @olivasjewelry. 
 
 
 
 
 
Please review our Terms and Conditions in advance and check in with Visitor Services upon arrival. Questions? Email us info@batashoemuseum.ca anytime.

title: 🍁 Fall Walk: Finch Recreational Trail & Park Adventure! 🌾🚶‍♂️ (16KM)
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🍁 Fall Walk: Finch Recreational Trail & Park Adventure! 🌾

### An Easy, Flat Fall Walk Through Toronto's Green Spaces

Looking for an easy way to enjoy the fall colours without tackling a difficult hike?
Join us for a relaxed walk from **Pioneer Village Station to Finch Station**, travelling through Black Creek Parkland and along the **Finch Recreational Trail**.

This is one of our members' favourite walks for a reason. The route is mostly flat and takes us through open fields, wooded areas, and quiet green spaces that feel surprisingly far removed from the city.

We'll take our time, enjoy the changing leaves, stop for a break by **Dufferin Creek**, and spend the day walking and getting to know each other.

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 🚶‍♂️ What We'll Do

We'll start outside **Pioneer Village Station** and make our way through Black Creek Parkland before joining the Finch Recreational Trail.
Along the way we'll:

* Walk through Black Creek Parkland 🌳
* Follow the Finch Recreational Trail
* Enjoy the fall colours and changing scenery 🍂
* Stop for a break near Dufferin Creek
* Have some time for conversation and photos
* Continue along the trail toward Finch Station

This is a **long but easy, mostly flat walk**. There are no major hills or difficult terrain, but you'll want comfortable shoes and enough energy for the full route.

***

## 🍂 Fall Is the Best Time to Do This Walk

There's something particularly nice about this trail in the fall. The air is cooler, the leaves are changing, and the open stretches of the trail give you plenty of room to slow down and enjoy the season.
It's a good walk if you want to get outside without feeling like you're climbing a mountain.
And as always, **the activity is the container. The people you meet along the way are the real experience.**

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Location:** Outside Pioneer Village Station, at the corner of Steeles Avenue West and Northwest Gate (East Side), in front of the York University sign.
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time:** 11:00 AM sharp
I will only wait **5 minutes**.
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🏁 **End Point:** Finch Station

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$5 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This fee helps support the group and allows us to continue organizing events throughout Toronto.

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🥪 A snack or light lunch
🧥 A fall jacket or sweater

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This walk is great for:

* Anyone who enjoys fall scenery
* People looking for an easy, flat trail
* Anyone who wants to get back into walking
* People who enjoy exploring Toronto's green spaces
* Anyone looking for a relaxed social outing
* People who want to meet new people while getting some fresh air

You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**.

**Come for the fall colours.**
**Stay for the friendship.** 🍁💛

title: History of Aviation 3: The Ghost of Flight 401? (LECTURE ON THE GO)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2026. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join us and learn about the world and keep active and warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life. **This is part three of the Aviation series that will debut in August 2026 with the Lecture on the disaster at Tenerife**!

The "Lecture on the Go" Series is open to members who have purchased the YEARLY MEMBERSHIP PASS, it's free for those members. If you wish to attend a lecture and you are not a yearly pass member then the price **per** lecture is $20.00.

In this third part of *History of Aviation: Was there really a ghost of fight 401? Lecture on the Go* series, we explore one of the most extraordinary stories in modern aviation history. A true story that morphed into a decades long investigation, and put a spotlight on the airline industry itself. The events surrounding Eastern Airlines Flight 401 is fascinating, and sounds a bit like a modern horror story, but it's true. I can't wait to find out your take on this modern ghost story.

Eastern Air Lines Flight 401 is one of the most famous and influential aviation disasters in history. The flight crashed late at night on December 29, 1972, while approaching Miami, Florida, after departing from New York’s JFK Airport. The aircraft was a new Lockheed L-1011 TriStar, one of the most technologically advanced airliners of its kind.

The accident happened during the final stages of landing. The crew became distracted by a malfunctioning landing gear indicator light in the cockpit. While they focused on the small bulb issue, the aircraft descended without the pilots fully realizing it. The autopilot had been unintentionally disconnected, and the plane drifted lower and lower into the dark Florida Everglades.

At 11:42 p.m., Flight 401 crashed into the Everglades about 18 miles northwest of Miami Airport. The impact destroyed much of the aircraft across the swampy terrain. Of the 176 people on board, 101 died, including the captain and first officer, while 75 survived. Rescue operations were difficult because of the remote location, darkness, mud, and water.

The tragedy became historically important because it demonstrated a major danger in aviation known as “crew distraction.” The aircraft itself was functioning, but the crew lost awareness of altitude while concentrating on a relatively minor problem. The crash helped push airlines and regulators toward improved cockpit procedures. Many aviation historians consider Flight 401 a turning point in how airlines train pilots.

The accident also became famous in popular culture because of stories surrounding “Ghosts of Flight 401.” According to airline legends from the 1970s, some Eastern employees claimed to see apparitions of Captain Bob Loft and Flight Engineer Don Repo aboard other Eastern aircraft after parts from the crashed plane were reused. While there is no evidence supporting these claims, the stories became widely known through books, documentaries, and movies.

description:
Global events - from pandemics, war, and foodborne illnesses - have threatened farmers' livelihoods, created supermarket shortages, and revealed to consumers that our food system is broken. In the face of these threats to our well-being and food security, what can we do as a community to strengthen our local food system?

Nancy Matsumoto
, author of
Reaping What She Sows
: How Women Are Rebuilding Our Broken Food System
, who will introduce her book and highlight Toronto women changemakers building up local and regional supply chains to combat the destructive effects of Big Food.
Paul DeCampo
, representative of Karma Co-op Grocery Store will moderate the discussion, which will include the following guest panelists:
Jenn Pfenning
from Pfennings Organic Farm
Nurith Jungreis
from Sunflower Kitchen
Sabrina Banh
from Fisherfolk
Together, they will discuss the importance of a resilient, transparent, climate-friendly local and regional food system—for our health, the health of workers, animals and communities, and the future of our planet. Attendees will be inspired to learn how they can also help create positive food system change and contribute to our regional food security.
Presented in celebration of Women's History Month, as part of Small Business Month, and as part of TPL's environmental program series,

, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.

Nancy Matsumoto
, an award-winning freelance writer and editor who writes about agroecology, food sovereignty, food, drink, and Japanese American culture and history.

title: 🇨🇦Japanese and English Language Exchange  (Page for everyone)
description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は5頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

***Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events***

*Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate*

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List:
Members can join the waiting-list even if an event is full. When a spot becomes available, we will move you to the going-list.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

@tjex.ca

Feel free to follow us!
