description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
🎬 Let’s Go to the Movies (and Actually Talk… or Not)

Whether you're a film nerd, popcorn enthusiast, or just looking for a chill night out with interesting people — this one's for you.

We’re heading out to see a movie together, then grabbing food or drinks after. If the film's great (or terrible), we’ll probably talk about it forever. If it’s just okay, we’ll talk about it for 10 minutes and move on to everything else — books, dating apps, weird dreams, how Toronto keeps getting more expensive, etc.

The vibe is relaxed, friendly, and not too serious. No film degree needed. No icebreakers. No pressure to “perform.” Just come enjoy the film, connect with some thoughtful people, and see where the night goes Click here to watch trailer!

🎞️ **Movie Title + Trailer:** [\[Click here to watch trailer!\]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gM4LkaXwGuY)

📖 **📖 Plot Summary:** A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

***

### 🗓️ **Event Details**

📍 **Meetup Time:** 6:00 PM (Final time + theatre announced Tuesday of event week)
🎬 **Movie Start Time:** TBA
⏱️ **Runtime:** TBA
📌 **Meetup Spot:** To be confirmed (based on theatre)
🎟️ **Cost:**

* **$11.50** for *CineClub* members
* **$16.00** regular admission
👉 You are responsible for buying your own ticket.

**🪑 Reserved Seating:**
You must buy your ticket *before* signing up. You'll be asked where you're sitting so we can all sit together! However, members are welcome to sit anywhere that works for them.
🎫 Buy your ticket here: [https://www.cineplex.com](https://www.cineplex.com)
📍🪑 **Where I will be sitting:**

🍿 **After the Movie:**
Yes, we’re heading out after! It’s not just a movie night — it’s a social night. Let's talk, laugh, and dissect every plot twist.

***

### ✅ **Before You Sign Up**

* Please **buy your ticket first** — seating is limited!
* When signing up, let us know your **seat number** so we can try to group everyone together.
* You can still sign up or just **show up on the day** if you’re not sure you can make it — we’re flexible!

📲 **Join Our WhatsApp Group:**[ Click here to join](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)
🎟️ **Join Cineplex’s CineClub for discounts**: [https://www.cineplex.com/cineclub](https://www.cineplex.com/cineclub)
🎁 **Get your SCENE Card** for free movies and points: [https://www.scene.ca](https://www.scene.ca)

***

### 🎥 **A Quick Word About Movie Etiquette**

We love a great film experience. Please:

* Turn off your phone
* Don’t talk during the movie
* Be respectful of others

Repeat offenders will be removed from the group — we take our cinema seriously (but with snacks).

***

### 👥 **About the Group**

This event is open to everyone — single, not single, shy, social, new in town or a long-time local. We're a group for people who love movies *and* making real connections. We also do walks, hikes, restaurants, arts & culture — come be part of it!

title: Fast Friends: Meet New People, Make Connections & Play 50+ Board Games | 25–45
description:
Toronto 20's to 50's Singles Social (4000+)
Looking for a better way to spend a Saturday evening in Toronto than sitting at home wondering how to expand your social circle?

Fast Friends gives you an easy starting point. Instead of walking into a busy pub and hoping you happen to meet the right people, our host creates the structure — guiding conversations and rotations so you can meet a variety of people naturally, even if you arrive on your own.

And this time, we’re back at Stout Irish Pub — a relaxed Toronto pub where the socialising can continue long after the hosted rounds finish, with drinks, food and 50+ board games to choose from. 🎲🍻

🎟️ Book Early & Save: [https://toronto10thoct.eventbrite.co.uk](https://toronto10thoct.eventbrite.co.uk)

You can pay securely online with any debit or credit card through PayPal — no PayPal account required.
*Advance tickets are cheaper and help us plan the right space and group size for a comfortable evening.*

Early Bird: CAD $10 \| Regular: CAD $15 \| At the Door: CAD $20 cash

🤝 The Evening
7:00 PM — Welcome & Settle In
Meet your host, Kristabelle, grab a drink and get comfortable.
Whether you've just moved to Toronto or have been here for years, this is a chance to step out of your usual routine and meet some different people.
Coming alone? That's completely fine — most guests do.

7:30–8:30 PM — Fast Friends
Forget the usual “How do I start talking to someone?” moment.
Our host guides a series of short conversations and rotations, giving you the chance to meet different people throughout the evening. You don't need to plan what happens next — just show up, join the conversation and see who you connect with.

✨ Themed Connection Rounds
We'll mix things up with interactive prompts and themed conversation challenges that help uncover common interests and unexpected connections.
From travel and food to music, books, hobbies and weekend adventures, these rounds are designed to get you talking about something more interesting than small talk.

🎲 8:30 PM onwards — 50+ Board Games & Socialising
This is where Stout really adds something special.
Once the hosted rounds finish, you don't have to call it a night. Stout has 50+ board games available, giving you an easy way to continue socialising with the people you've just met.
Pick a game, join a group, grab another drink, or simply keep chatting. You can make the evening as relaxed and spontaneous as you like.

❤️ Why Come Along?
✔️ Meet 20+ new people in one evening
✔️ Guided conversations make it easier to connect
✔️ Interactive themed rounds to spark better conversations
✔️ 50+ board games at Stout 🎲
✔️ Relaxed Irish pub atmosphere
✔️ Reserved space for our group
✔️ Members from our Toronto Meetup communities may also join
✔️ Most guests come solo
✔️ Designed for ladies and gents aged 25–45
✔️ Friendship-focused — not a dating event

📍 Why Stout Irish Pub?
Located at 221 Carlton Street, Stout is an easy-to-reach Toronto pub with a relaxed atmosphere, drinks, food and one of the best extras for a social event — a huge selection of 50+ board games.
So you can start the evening with structured conversations and finish it however you want: playing, chatting, laughing or getting to know someone you clicked with.

👥 Who Is It For?
You don't need to be new to Toronto, part of an existing group or know anyone attending.
If your social circle could use some fresh faces — whether you're new in town or simply ready to meet people outside your usual routine — you're welcome.

Come by yourself, bring a friend, or do both.

🌍 About Fast Friends
For over 10 years, Fast Friends has been creating opportunities for people to connect through professionally hosted social events in 30+ cities worldwide.

Our goal is simple: make meeting people easier and give you a reason to actually start the conversation.
Come solo. We'll guide the experience. You make the connections. ❤️

title: Poems of Consumption by H. Sinno
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
H.Sinno’s acclaimed performance, Poems of Consumption , reimagines consumer culture through music, poetry, and immersive visuals.

Part concert, part multimedia performance, and part poetic meditation, Poems of Consumption explores the emotional contradictions of modern life through songs built from an unexpected source: Amazon customer reviews transformed into poetry. Partially inspired by Mark Fisher’s Capitalist Realism , Poems of Consumption is a song cycle covering themes like ennui, surveillance capitalism, heartbreak, boycotts, and orientalism, with compositions that juxtapose harsh electronica with the whimsy of a string quartet.

Originally commissioned by London’s Barbican Centre and Shubbak Festival, the production has been praised for its fearless artistic vision and emotional honesty, bringing together experimental music, theatre, and literature into a deeply personal live experience.

description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: 🍂🌳 Fall Walk: Gus Harris Trail 🌳🍂
description:
Try New Things in Toronto!
# 🍂🌳 Fall Walk: Gus Harris Trail 🌳🍂

### A Hidden Ravine, Easy Walking & Great Conversation

Sometimes the best parts of Toronto are the ones most people drive right past.

Join us for a relaxed fall walk along the **Gus Harris Trail**, a quiet ravine trail that follows **Taylor-Massey Creek** through Scarborough and East York.

This isn't a challenging hike. It's an easy, mostly flat walk through one of Toronto's quieter green spaces, with plenty of time to enjoy the changing leaves, get some fresh air, and meet other people along the way.

We'll follow the creek, walk beneath the trees, and take our time enjoying the fall scenery.
The goal isn't to race to the end of the trail. **It's to get outside, have some good conversations, and enjoy the company.**

✨ **Fun Fact:** Taylor-Massey Creek takes its name from two prominent Toronto families. The Taylor family was associated with the Don Valley Brick Works, now home to Evergreen Brick Works.

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 🚶‍♂️ What We'll Do

We'll spend about **two hours** walking along the trail, taking our time, chatting, and getting to know one another.
This is a **social walk, not a race.**

The route has very few hills, making it a comfortable walk for most people with a reasonable level of fitness.
We'll finish back where we started.

***

## 🍁 Fall Weather & Expectations

This walk takes place outdoors in typical Toronto fall weather.
Please dress appropriately for the conditions and wear comfortable walking shoes. The trail may be damp or muddy depending on recent weather.
Bring water and a snack, and dress in layers if the temperature is changing throughout the day.

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Location:** Outside Victoria Park Subway Station, by Victoria Park Road.
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time: 11:00 AM sharp**
I will only wait **5 minutes.**
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🏁 **End Point:** Victoria Park Subway Station

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$5 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This fee helps support the group and allows us to continue organizing events throughout Toronto.

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🥪 A snack
🧥 A fall jacket or sweater
🦟 Bug spray if needed

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This walk is great for:

* Anyone who enjoys fall scenery 🍂
* People looking for an easy trail
* Anyone who wants to get outside and get moving
* People who enjoy exploring Toronto's hidden green spaces
* Anyone looking for a relaxed social outing
* People who want to meet new people and make friends

You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**.

**Come for the trail.**
**Stay for the conversation.**
**Leave with a new connection — and maybe a new friend.** 🍂💛

The only authorized cemeteries within York were Anglican or Roman Catholic. Citizens who did not belong to either church had no choice but to find burial arrangements outside York.

The General Burying Ground received Royal Assent in 1826 and land that came to be known as Potters Field was acquired and started operation soon afterwards. Over time, additional cemetery lands were added and in 1873, a new cemetery available to all citizens was established. The new cemetery was situated on the farm land of the Cawthra family near Yonge Street.

This walk is for all fitness levels. Please dress for the weather. This walk will begin and end outside the Yorkminster Park Baptist Church at 1585 Yonge Street just north of Heath Street.

description: We’re U-Hauling back to the beach for the final time this year on SUNDAY, October 11th 🔥🪵✨ Ferries stop heading to Hanlan’s on October 14th, so we’re closing off the season. Join us to watch the sunset, enjoy a bonfire made by our strong lesbian hands, and connect with the community. This is an even chiller vibe than our usual gatherings, so feel free to bring your poetry, guitars and anything else you’d like to share. 🌭We will have free marshmallows, smore supplies and hotdogs (including vegan and halal options!) 🌬️ It gets cold on the island after dark, so we highly suggest bringing a sweater and a blanket! ⛴️ We’re handing out 50 free ferry tickets at the Jack Layton Ferry Terminal. Catch the 5:15PM! The last ferry back to the city is at 10:30. Pack up by 10 to make sure you don’t get stranded! 🔥 Please practice fire safety. If you want to build your own, make sure you know what you’re doing and you bring your own wood! Removing wood from the island can seriously harm the ecosystem. 👯 The fun doesn’t have to end because the fire’s put out! Link in bio for the OFFICIAL Lez Bonfire afterparty tickets. Code BIPOC for 15% off. Thank you to @c1foundation, @citypoolwarrior and everyone who has donated in the past. Community effort keeps this gathering alive! Lez Beach is first and foremost a grassroots gathering to combat rising levels of harassment and exclusion towards lesbians in queer spaces. Hanlan’s Point Beach is a public, clothing optional space and we cannot control who can and who cannot enter the space during Lez Beach. If you have concerns about the crowd, please come sit with us at the entrance to the event! We keep each other safe. If you’ve never attended before, take a look at our FAQ posts! This is a gathering to encourage safety and reclaim space for sapphics in the queer community. There is zero tolerance for racism, transphobia, fatphobia or misogyny. If you do not connect to the sapphic experience, we ask you to reconsider the space you’re entering. Poster art + graphics by @azaydrea ‍

description:
“Love is Life.” Few films have captured the poetry of love, memory and relationships quite like Kabhi Kabhie.

The Aga Khan Museum is proud to partner with Classic Legends Indian Films Festival (CLIFF) — a celebration of Indian cinema, bringing together timeless classics, acclaimed contemporary films, distinguished filmmakers, and engaging conversations. The festival honours India’s rich cinematic legacy while creating a global platform for screenings, retrospectives, cultural exchange, and dialogue between cinema, literature, and the performing arts.

As the concluding screening of Romantic Ravivaar at CLIFF 2026, Kabhi Kabhie offers audiences a chance to experience a landmark of Hindi romantic cinema once again – on the big screen, with its poetry, music and timeless story of love across generations.

title: La Société d'histoire de Toronto: HISTORITOUR - Facettes de High Park
description:
Départ : Départ au coin sud-ouest des rues Bloor ouest et Parkside (à quelques pas vers le sud-ouest de la station de métro Keele) 
Arrivée : Fin à l’entrée principale du parc sur Bloor (près de la station High Park) 
Guides : Isabelle Montagnier et Paul Overy 
Si vous habitez à Toronto, vous connaissez sans doute High Park et vous avez peut-être visité son petit zoo et sa très belle allée de cerisiers Sakura. Mais saviez-vous que ce site magnifique recèle des trésors cachés comme une savane de chênes noirs, une rivière souterraine, un théâtre shakespearien en plein air, un terrain de jeu pour les enfants et ses beaux jardins bordant l’étang Grenadier, parmi d’autres endroits remarquables? 
Venez en apprendre davantage sur l’histoire fascinante de ce lieu, depuis l’intendance autochtone et la création du parc par un don de terrain, en arpentant les pistes vallonnées des lieux en compagnie de vos guides, Paul Overy, guide à propos de l’écologie et des cours d’eau perdus et d’Isabelle Montagnier, résidente de longue date du quartier. 
Attention, cette visite comprend plusieurs petits raidillons et nous sortirons des sentiers battus! Laissez donc votre vélo (et votre chien) à la maison et habillez-vous en fonction de la météo (très variable à cette époque de l’année). Nous vous recommandons aussi de porter de bons souliers avec semelles antidérapantes et des pantalons longs en raison du risque de tics. À noter : le stationnement d’autos dans le parc est interdit en fin de semaine et jours fériés. 
  
Pas besoin de réserver – Visite guidée gratuite
La Société d’histoire de Toronto passe le chapeau à la fin.

description: Eunice Keitan is a Malaysian-Canadian Neo-Soul loop artist who channels the complex feeling of navigating two worlds, fusing the smoothness of Neo-Soul with evocative, ancestral Asian soundscapes. Part live-looping innovator, part ensemble leader, she builds lush, deep, and layered narratives - songs that are emotionally candid about identity and belonging. title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

Graduate Studies is where the next generation of careers and ideas are born. Come explore!
Thinking about your next chapter? Whether you’re exploring a career change or pursuing a new passion, there’s no better place to take that step than right here at York. York’s Master of Financial Accountability (MFAc) is the only program of its kind in the world. The MFAc is a way to accelerate your entry into senior management, assurance, and oversight functions. Creatively redefine the boundaries of environmental research. Adopting an interdisciplinary lens for your PhD in Environmental Studies, you will create a unique Program Plan, to be guided by your supervisory committee. title: Agents That Take Action: Secure Enterprise Integration with Azure
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
An enterprise agent becomes genuinely useful when it can act on business systems. It also becomes significantly more dangerous if those integrations are not governed correctly.

In this session, we will connect our Microsoft Foundry agent to real enterprise capabilities using Azure API Management, Azure Logic Apps, Azure Functions, Azure Service Bus, OpenAPI tools, and Model Context Protocol servers.

The agent will create an incident ticket, initiate an approval workflow, invoke a protected business API, submit a long-running remediation command, and report the final result back to the user. Rather than allowing the model direct access to backend systems, we will introduce a governed integration layer with typed tool contracts, authentication, authorization, rate limiting, schema validation, retries, and centralized logging.

We will also compare the roles of OpenAPI tools, MCP servers, Logic Apps actions, Azure Functions, and asynchronous messaging. Managed identities and Microsoft Entra ID will be used to eliminate embedded API keys and apply least-privilege access across the solution.

By the end of the session, attendees will understand how to give agents meaningful enterprise capabilities without bypassing security, integration governance, or operational controls. Key topics: Microsoft Foundry tools OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol Azure API Management as an AI gateway Azure Logic Apps agent actions Azure Functions Azure Service Bus Managed identity and Microsoft Entra ID Secure and asynchronous tool execution.

title: Python Essentials 1 and 2 Learning Circle
location: York Woods
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Tuesday afternoons from September 22 to December 8, 2-3:30pm. title: AI for School: Responsible Success for Teens
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
AI can help with schoolwork. So why does it feel like walking a tightrope? How do you use it for learning without fooling yourself?
In this youth-focused class, you'll learn to use AI as a tutor, quiz partner, and explainer, not an answer machine. You'll practice the tutor loop using provided examples: starting with what your interests are, what you want to learn, how you like to learn, and what you already understand. We'll also cover academic policies around AI and when AI is the wrong tool entirely.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start September 9, 2026 at 9:00 AM.

description:

title: Google AI Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization.

Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.

title: Parade: Queer Acts of Love & Resistance
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
The queer resistance that changed Canada—and the rights we can’t take for granted.

A new monthly series in partnership with Hot Docs, bringing visionary documentary filmmaking from around the world to Toronto’s East End.

Parade: Queer Acts of Love & Resistance captures a wide range of pivotal moments that sparked Canada’s 2SLGBTQI+ movement and its progress, and honours the activists and elders whose resistance led to the rights we have today. Rarely seen archival footage and first-person accounts bring the viewer to the frontlines of the decades-long struggle.

From police raids to early drag shows, community organizing to addresses to the House of Commons—the complex history of the country’s diverse communities is brought to life. Key milestones illustrate the power of taking resistance into the streets and underscore how easily the rights we’ve fought for can be revoked, making this essential viewing for all Canadians. Unflinching, bold, enraging, hopeful: Parade is a vital new chapter in the queer film canon.

More information can be found here: https://soulpepper.ca/parade-queer-acts-of-love-resistance/ https://soulpepper.ca/parade-queer-acts-of-love-resistance/ .

title: Saying Hello to Connecting ft. Nicholas Epley and Gillian Sandstrom
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
This evening will explore the “the liking gap” – how strangers would like us more than we think if we tried to connect.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the featured event. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. This evening's workshop will be announced shortly so stay tuned for that. Try out one of the engagement activities available, including this event's
Conversation Station: The
Bus Stop Challenge
, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger in the most ordinary of small-talk settings.
*****
Join us
in the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon
for
Saying Hello to
Reconnecting
,
with psychologists and authors Nicholas Epley and Gillian Sandstrom
in conversation with
Paul Bloom
.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
Why do we walk past dozens of strangers a day, headphones in, eyes down, when a two-minute conversation could brighten both of our afternoons? At this event we'll find out what's actually stopping us and then test it. You'll learn what the research says about how strangers respond to being approached, why our predictions are so consistently wrong, and how to start the kind of small, low-stakes conversation that adds up to a bigger life. Then you'll get a chance to have one.
Why do so many of us underestimate the power of a simple "hello"? What is the "liking gap," and how does it keep us from connecting with people who would genuinely enjoy meeting us? And in an age of texting, remote work and screen-mediated relationships, what do we lose when we avoid the small, unscripted moments that once wove strangers into our daily lives?
Nicholas Epley, a University of Chicago psychologist, has spent his career studying this gap. In A Little More Social: How Small Choices Create Unexpected Happiness, Health, and Connection, he argues that connection is a choice we make based on expectations of how others will respond — expectations that skew far too pessimistic. Gillian Sandstrom, Professor in the Psychology of Kindness at the University of Sussex, takes it further in Once Upon a Stranger: The Science of How "Small" Talk Can Add Up to a Big Life, tracing her own path from self-described introvert to leading researcher on talking to strangers.
Come ready to say hello.
About this event’s guests:
Dr. Gillian Sandstrom
Dr. Nicholas Epley
Dr. Paul Bloom
Read More:
Once Upon A Stranger
A Little More Social
The Sweet Spot
***
Connection Workshop (to be announced soon) |
5:30 - 6:30 pm (TBC)
The
Bus Stop Challenge
| 5:30 – 6:30 pm & 8:00 – 9:00 pm
Set up like a familiar TTC platform or bus shelter, this station drops you into the most ordinary of small-talk settings. Draw a prompt card with a simple mission (ask a stranger's opinion, compliment something, trade a recommendation) and see how fast a short, unscripted exchange can turn a stranger into a familiar face. It's the “liking gap”, live and in action.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: OPTIONS – Emotional Intelligence: The Human Side of Technical Leadership
description:
Wednesday, October 14 | 10 – 1:30PM |GB202 | Register in Advance
Engineering and technical environments require strong analytical thinking, problem-solving and technical expertise. But success—particularly when working with others—also depends on how we handle stress, communicate, manage disagreements and respond to different people.
In this interactive three-hour workshop, participants will explore four areas of emotional intelligence: self-awareness, self-management, social awareness and relationship management. We’ll look at questions such as: What happens when I’m stressed or frustrated? How do I know when I’m getting triggered? How can I pause before reacting? How do I recognize what someone else may be experiencing? And how can I handle a difficult conversation without making things worse? 
Using practical examples, reflection and discussion, participants will explore how emotional intelligence can help with teamwork, conflict, communication, trust and working under pressure—in graduate school, research teams and future workplaces. Participants will leave with practical strategies they can use right away to manage their own reactions, work more effectively with others and handle challenging situations.
Participants will receive a certificate of completion upon completion. 
Coffee, Tea, Light Snacks, and Lunch will be catered. 
Facilitator Bio 
Annie Simpson M. Ed. specializes in emotionally intelligent leadership and high-trust teams. She is an experienced facilitator, trainer, and executive coach with 20 years of experience in leadership development education. At the University of Toronto, Annie helped grow the Troost Institute for Leadership Education in Engineering (ILead) where she managed a talented team and developed programs and courses for students and corporate professionals. More recently, at Western University, she designed and led multi-day professional development programs for faculty and staff who led teams. As the founder of Annie Simpson Consulting, Annie designs training programs and team retreats for various clients in the Technology, Higher-Education, Social and Community Services, and Financial sectors.

title: Engineering leadership: Navigating a changing world
location: Online
description:
Engineering has always addressed challenges by advancing technology. But success now depends not only on technical expertise but also on the ability to connect people, foster collaboration and drive innovation across complex environments.  
What does it take to lead as an engineer in an era defined by AI, global collaboration and rapid change?
Join Professor Emily Moore for an engaging discussion on how engineering careers are evolving and how leaders can adapt to meet new challenges. Drawing on her research into engineering career paths, teamwork and organizational dynamics, Professor Moore will share practical insights on developing the skills that matter for long-term success. Discover how engineers can strengthen their leadership capabilities, navigate change with confidence and amplify their impact in a world where the human side of engineering has never been more important.  
Join us on October 14, 2026 at our monthly Skule™ Lunch & Learn.  
By registering for the Skule™ Lunch & Learn event, you could potentially earn Continuing Professional Development (CPD) credits. CPDs are essential for professional engineers and limited license holders to renew their licenses annually through the PEO PEAK Program. If you’re wondering whether this event offering qualifies you for CPD credits, click here to learn more. 
About the speaker
Professor Emily Moore was appointed Director of Troost Institute for Leadership Education in Engineering (ILead) in October 2018, after more than twenty years in industry. Emily started her career at the Xerox Research Centre of Canada scaling up new materials and processes from the lab to manufacturing. In her 11 years at Xerox, Emily learned a great deal about leading teams and developing new products, becoming a manager and Principal Engineer. Emily then spent 10 years at Hatch, a global engineering firm serving the mining, energy and infrastructure sectors. Emily led international teams to develop new product and service offerings and to deliver major projects, first as the Director of Technology Development and then as Managing Director, Water. Emily was also the inaugural chair of Hatch’s Global Diversity and Inclusion efforts. Emily holds a bachelor’s degree in engineering chemistry from Queen’s University and completed a doctorate in physical chemistry from Oxford University as a Rhodes Scholar. In 2016 Emily was recognized as one of 100 Global Inspirational Women in Mining and received the SCI Canada Kalev Pugi Award.

title: Oct 14 - Advances in AI at SDSU
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from AI researchers at San Diego State University.

**Date, Time Location**

Oct 14, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/advances-in-ai-at-sdsu-october-14-2026)**

**Agent as Policy for Robotic Manipulation**

This talk will introduces how a general-purpose agent can directly drive a physical robot throughout task execution without any task-specific or environment-specific training. We introduce Agent as Policy (AGP), which places task planning and execution under the agent’s control.

*About the Speaker*

[Xiaobai Liu](https://www.linkedin.com/in/xiaobai-liu-33598336/) is a Professor of Computer Science at San Diego State University (SDSU), where he directs the Machine Vision and Perception Lab. Prior to joining SDSU in 2015, he conducted research and taught at UCLA.

**Grounding Multimodal Open-World Learning for Physical AI**

Physical AI systems such as robots, unmanned vehicles, and embodied agents must perceive and reason about a world that is dynamic, unstructured, and rarely matches their training distribution. Yet most multimodal models remain brittle when confronted with novel objects, unseen conditions, and a messy unstructured environment.

This talk develops how grounding perception across modalities and environments can make open-world learning more robust for physically situated systems. Drawing on our recent work, I will highlight the core challenges of multimodal open-world learning including out-of-distribution detection, distribution shift generalization, and cascaded semantic grounding and point toward multimodal systems that stay reliable when deployed in the unpredictable open world.

*About the Speakers*

[Salimeh Sekeh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/salimeh-sekeh-65473344/) is an Associate Professor of Computer Science at San Diego State University (SDSU), where she directs the Sekeh Laboratory. Her recognition includes an NSF CAREER Award and a Cisco research gift (both 2022), and the Maine College of Engineering and Computing Early Career Research Award (2023), along with multiple industry and federal research awards.

[Mary Wisell ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mary-isabelle-wisell/)is a second-year PhD student in the Sekeh Lab and leads the lab's work on environment-aware OOD detection and cascaded failure analysis for multimodal intelligence with several publications in top-tier Machine Learning and computer vision conferences.

**Model-Free, Position-Free Signal Source Seeking Using Unmanned Maritime Systems**

Long-range signal source detection in open-world environments presents a significant challenge, mainly due to the detrimental effects of the environment on signals propagation paths and presence of extraneous signal sources. While distributed static sensing systems are often employed, achieving scalability and comprehensive coverage across expansive areas is cost-prohibitive.

One affordable solution involves using low-cost autonomous unmanned vehicles (AUVs) that can leverage their mobility and actively explore the environment using extremum seeking control (ESC) algorithms. This talk presents novel ESC approaches to steer AUVs to sources of interest in an a priori unknown, highly non-convex map.

*About the Speaker*

[Zahra Nili Ahmadabadi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zahra-nili-ahmadabadi-phd-29113171) is Associate Professor with the Mechanical Engineering Department at San Diego State University (SDSU). She is a recipient of the ASME rising star award and ARO Early career award.

description:

From 12–2 PM, witness the cast of Partita prepare to take the stage in HEAR THE DANCE: Signature Programme 3. This open rehearsal of Justin Peck’s sneaker ballet invites you to get closer to the artists as they move through technically challenging choreography that celebrates the joy of being together. 
The rehearsal features recent graduates of Toronto Metropolitan University and students from the National Ballet School. 
Justin Peck is a three-time Tony Award-winning director, choreographer, filmmaker, and dancer based in New York City. He is the Resident Choreographer of the New York City Ballet and only the second person in the institution’s 75-year history to hold this title. 
He has created more than 50 stage and theatre works presented around the world, including at Lincoln Center, the Palais Garnier, Sydney Opera House, Brooklyn Academy of Music, and Broadway. His creations have been performed by companies including the Paris Opera Ballet, Australian Ballet, Dresden Semperoper Ballet, Hong Kong Ballet, Boston Ballet, Juilliard, The National Ballet of Canada, Miami City Ballet, Pacific Northwest Ballet, LA Dance Project, Dutch National Ballet, the School of American Ballet, Joffrey Ballet, and Houston Ballet.

Are you thinking of pursuing your graduate education in Public & International Affairs ( https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/2SBlvZkXTYOlpwH-FuVp8w )? We invite you to attend our program session!
The two-year Masters in Public and International Affairs prepares Canada’s future leaders for today’s global challenges. It has three distinguishing features. First, it is bilingual, students being required to take one-third of their courses and do their assignments in them in Canada’s other official language. Second, it seeks to fuse together theory and practical knowledge. Instructors are both academics and practitioners. Students learn to write briefing notes and memos to senior government officials.
They do a paid supervised internship with a government department, an international agency, or a non-governmental organization. Those students who wish to pursue an academic career have the opportunity to do a major research paper in their final year. Third, it is multidisciplinary and integrative: students are exposed in their courses to different methodological approaches and skills. The second-year Capstone Seminar is designed to bring together these diverse aptitudes in a dynamic learning environment.
As its name suggests, the MPIA has a strong international component. It encourages second-year students to go on a one-term exchange or to opt for the double Masters degree the MPIA has with the Université de Strasbourg in France. Our programme boasts a very high success rate in placing its graduates in enriching jobs in the federal or provincial civil service, as well as in international organizations or local bodies
To learn more about other sessions being offered during our Experience Grad York week, visit yorku.ca/gradstudies/egy ( http://Experience Grad York week, visit yorku.ca/gradstudies/egy ).
Still have questions? Contact us at fgsapply@yorku.ca ( mailto:fgsapply@yorku.ca ).

title: Open Studio: Esie Mensah’s ZAYO
location: Union, 65 Front Street West, Toronto, ON, Canada
description:
With Open Studio, Union and Fall for Dance North invite you into the daily life of a dancer. If you’re passing through Union Station’s West Wing, pause for a moment or stay for an hour and experience the artists at work. 
From 4–7 PM, experience Toronto-based dancer and choreographer Esie Mensah in process as she rehearses ZAYO with her company of dancers. 
ZAYO is an Afrofusion dance-theatre production shaped by Esie Mensah’s lived experiences. Conceived over eight years, the work explores the courage needed to follow one’s calling and ancestral purpose. The piece follows a young woman discovering her power as she exists between worlds, guided by her Ancestors toward her chosen destiny. 
Esie Mensah is an award-winning choreographer, director, dancer, educator, and TEDx speaker whose work spans dance, theatre, opera, and film/TV. She has worked with Rihanna, Drake, Nelly Furtado, Kenny Ortega, and clients including Canada’s Got Talent, Holt Renfrew, Deloitte, and the Toronto Raptors. 
Her work has toured nationally and internationally. Theatre credits include choreography for Soulpepper, Obsidian, Shaw Festival, and Stratford Festival, as well as directing Serving Elizabeth at Theatre Aquarius. She choreographed Scott Joplin’s opera Treemonisha: A Musical Reimagining and was an Artist in Residence at Fall for Dance North in October 2025. 
Co-presented by Union and Fall for Dance North.

title: Trust, Participation and Democracy: What Canadians Are Saying
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space
description:
Trust in democratic institutions is being challenged in Canada and around the world. While many Canadians still believe in democratic values, more people are worried about political divisions, lower trust in governments and public institutions, false information, and whether political systems are meeting people's needs.
Using the latest public opinion polls, election research, and public engagement data, this panel will explore how Canadians feel about democracy today. Are concerns about democracy shared by many Canadians, or are they more common in certain groups? What is causing changes in political trust and participation? And what can governments, community organizations, educators, and local communities do to help strengthen democracy and encourage people to get involved in the future?
Featuring
Andrew Parkin
, Executive Director,
Environics Institute
Sarah Morra,
Chair, Vote 16 Canada and Research Assistant,
The Samara Centre for Democracy
Joanna Massie,
Postdoctoral Fellow in Political Science,
McMaster University
Moderator:
Shawn Micallef
, Toronto Star columnist & University of Toronto civics instructor
Toronto's municipal election takes place on October 26, 2026. Check out the
KnowYourVote.TO
website and the
Celebrate Democracy
page to learn more about the upcoming election, access important voter resources, and discover activities and interactive library programs for all ages happening at a branch near you.
This initiative is made possible by donations to the Toronto Public Library Foundation and is generously supported by the McConnell Foundation.

title: Tutankhamun: The Sensational Discovery - Part 1
location: North York Central Library, Room 1 (2nd floor)
description:
This year marks an important anniversary in the history of Egyptology. On November 4th, 2026, it will be 104 years since Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon discovered the intact tomb of King Tutankhamun in 1922 - a discovery that continues to capture the public imagination.
Nearly a year after the complete collection went on display at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Cairo on November 1, 2025, Sherine ElSebaie will take audiences back to the moment of its discovery. Following the footsteps of the excavators, she will recount the story leading to the discovery of the tomb and explore the remarkable objects found in its first two chambers during the initial excavation in 1922.
Sherine ElSebaie is an Egyptologist who began her academic journey with a B.Sc. in Egypt, completed a Master’s degree in Egyptology at the University of Toronto. She then engaged in advanced doctoral studies, further deepening her expertise in the field. She specializes in ancient Egyptian art and religion, with particular interests in the history of archeology, tourism, and cultural heritage.
Registration is encouraged but not required.

title: Vibe Coding: Make Your Own Interactive Story with AI

description:

You'll design the branches, describe the rules in plain language, test for the tricky edge cases (what if the player picks the weird option?), and end up with a single file you can share with anyone. title: Short Book Club
location: Parliament Street, Main Floor Program Room
description:
Are you interested in joining a book club but are short on time?  Then join our Short Book Club, where we read titles that are 250 pages or less. Meetings are held on the second Wednesday of each month.
Our October book is
Crying in H Mart
by Michelle Zauner
Summary: Zauner, of indie band Japanese Breakfast, presents a memoir about growing up Korean-American, losing her mother, and forging her own identity. She tells of growing up the only Asian-American kid at her school in Eugene, Oregon; of struggling with her mother's high expectations of her; of a painful adolescence; of treasured months spent in her grandmother's tiny apartment in Seoul, where she and her mother would bond over heaping plates of food. As she grew up, her Koreanness began to feel ever more distant, even as she found the life she wanted to live. Her mother's diagnosis of terminal pancreatic cancer when Michelle was twenty-five forced a reckoning with her identity and brought her to reclaim the gifts of taste, language, and history her mother had given her.

mindset. We demystify the technology by viewing AI as an

Oct 14 - How Do We Shape AI?
AI is already reshaping how we work, protect our privacy, and participate in society—yet most of us never get a seat at the table in deciding how it's built or used. This session creates that space. Equal parts presentation and conversation,

title: Historical Society of Ottawa - Lest We Forget? An exploration of the Valour and Unequal Treatment of Algonquin who have served in Canada’s Armed Forces
location: online
description:
Guest Speaker
Lynn Gehl Ph.D, Anishinaabe Algonquin Advocate, Academic, Author & Artist 
Wendy Jocko Sgt. CD (Ret’d),  Former Chief of the Algonquins of Pikwakanagan First Nation. Canadian Forces Veteran 
Details 
Wendy Jocko’s uncle and four great uncles served in WWI and her father and five uncles served in WWII. Wendy served for 23 years, including tours of duty in Bosnia and Croatia.
Wendy’s son served in the 1st Battalion of the Royal Canadian Regiment. 
In Lynn Gehl’s book “Joseph Gagnon: An Algonquin World War I Veteran”, she recounts the story of her great-grandfather who, in exchange for his wartime service and sacrifices, found himself stripped of his rights as an Indigenous person, yet denied the rights accorded non-Indigenous veterans. 
This presentation will take place on Zoom. All are welcome. Zoom registration link below.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

Héctor Fuentes

title: Oct 15 - AI, ML, and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Time, Place and Location**

Oct 15, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-october-15-2026)**

**Testing AI Systems in Production: Data Quality, Drift, and Model Evaluation**

AI systems can pass offline evaluation and still fail in production when real-world data changes, features become stale, labels or feedback signals are incomplete, or model behavior drifts away from expected outcomes. This talk shares practical patterns for testing and evaluating AI systems after deployment, including data quality checks, drift detection, online/offline metric comparison, model monitoring, and rollback analysis.

Using personalization and recommendation systems as examples, we will examine how teams can build evaluation workflows that catch quality issues before users do. Attendees will leave with a practical checklist for making AI-backed systems easier to evaluate, debug, and operate as data changes over time.

*About the Speaker*

[Jayakumar Ramalingam](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jayakumarramalingam) is a Staff Software Engineer and Cloud Architect at SiriusXM with over 16 years of experience building cloud-native platforms, real-time data pipelines, resilient APIs, and AI/ML-enabled applications at production scale.

**Where Should Your Model Live? A Framework for Tiering Computer Vision Deployments**

Where should a computer vision model actually run - on-device, near the edge, or in the cloud? It's a decision that looks simple until requirements like latency, cost, connectivity, and update cadence start pulling in different directions, often revealing themselves only after deployment.

Drawing on hands-on experience developing and deploying CV models across Hailo, Nvidia, Qualcomm and AWS platforms, this talk introduces a practical framework for tiering computer vision deployments based on real project requirements and constraints. Discussion will include what changes at each tier - from development to deployment to monitoring and update strategy - with relevant industry examples.

Attendees will leave with a set of questions or a framework they can use to place their own CV projects into the right tier.

*About the Speaker*

[Ajaykumaar Sivacoumare](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ajay-sa/) is an AI Software Engineer specializing in computer vision and edge AI, with production experience developing and deploying CV models across Nvidia, Hailo, Qualcomm and AWS-based platforms.

**From 2D Slices to 3D Tumors: Lightweight Volumetric Detection Without Heavy 3D Networks**

Slice-wise 2D detectors are fast and scalable, but they struggle to produce reliable 3D bounding boxes from volumetric medical data. This talk presents YOLO-PVC, a lightweight post-processing framework that consolidates slice-wise YOLO detections into coherent 3D bounding boxes using percentile-based geometric aggregation and a minimal MLP calibration module.

This talk demonstrates consistent improvements in volumetric IoU across three liver tumor categories i.e., HCC, CCA, and Mixed, without requiring dense 3D annotations or memory-intensive architectures. The talk covers the clinical motivation, the technical approach, and practical lessons from deploying computer vision on real hospital MRI data.

*About the Speaker*

[Talha Waqas](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mtalha-waqas-255557144/) is a second-year PhD student at ESME Research Lab, Paris and LISSI, Université Paris-Est, working on computer vision applied to medical imaging, with a focus on tumor classification, detection, and segmentation in multi-phase liver MRI.

**The Two-Loop Architecture for Voice AI**

Building responsive voice AI requires balancing latency with intelligence. This talk introduces a practical architecture that separates real-time conversation from asynchronous reasoning, enabling richer interactions without slowing the user experience. The session covers reusable design patterns drawn from production-inspired conversational AI systems.

*About the Speaker*

[Abhinav Tushar](https://lepisma.xyz/wiki/about/) is an ML engineer and researcher specializing in Conversational AI and Speech Technology.

About Aggie Armstrong
Aggie Armstrong is a Filipino-Canadian artist living and working in Ontario. Working primarily in painting while incorporating hand embroidery and textile elements, she creates layered work inspired by everyday experiences, personal history, and the ways we make sense of the world around us.
 
Her work has been exhibited across Canada, the United States, and France, and she has exhibited at The Artist Project in Toronto since 2022. In 2023, she was commissioned to create the official poster for the Royal Agricultural Winter Fair, and in 2022 she was an artist-in-residence at Château Orquevaux in France. Her work has also been featured in British Vogue, Art Seen Magazine, CTV News, CP24 Breakfast, the Create!, and Colour Me Happy podcasts.
 
Alongside her studio practice, Aggie teaches watercolour workshops throughout the GTA and Southwestern Ontario, creating welcoming, approachable experiences that help people build confidence and discover the joy of painting and creativity.

Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).

Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.

title: Open Studio: Esie Mensah’s ZAYO
location: West Wing, 65 Front Street West, Toronto, ON, M5R 1V9, Canada
description:
With Open Studio, Union and Fall for Dance North invite you into the daily life of a dancer. If you’re passing through Union Station’s West Wing, pause for a moment or stay for an hour and experience the artists at work. 
From 4–7 PM, experience Toronto-based dancer and choreographer Esie Mensah in process as she rehearses ZAYO with her company of dancers. 
ZAYO is an Afrofusion dance-theatre production shaped by Esie Mensah’s lived experiences. Conceived over eight years, the work explores the courage needed to follow one’s calling and ancestral purpose. The piece follows a young woman discovering her power as she exists between worlds, guided by her Ancestors toward her chosen destiny. 
Esie Mensah is an award-winning choreographer, director, dancer, educator, and TEDx speaker whose work spans dance, theatre, opera, and film/TV. She has worked with Rihanna, Drake, Nelly Furtado, Kenny Ortega, and clients including Canada’s Got Talent, Holt Renfrew, Deloitte, and the Toronto Raptors. 
Her work has toured nationally and internationally. Theatre credits include choreography for Soulpepper, Obsidian, Shaw Festival, and Stratford Festival, as well as directing Serving Elizabeth at Theatre Aquarius. She choreographed Scott Joplin’s opera Treemonisha: A Musical Reimagining and was an Artist in Residence at Fall for Dance North in October 2025. 
Co-presented by Union and Fall for Dance North.

title: How Do AIs "Think"? And Why They Get Things Wrong
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
How does a machine actually "think"? Explore the history and latest developments of machine learning.
In this class, we'll dig into what's really going on inside AI systems: how they decide what matters in your question, where their training data comes from (and who's missing from it), and how hidden instructions can sneak into content and hijack an AI. And we'll ask the question underneath it all: is there anyone home inside the machine?

title: San Francisco: An evening with U of T Professor Jacob Tsimerman, Fields Medal winner
location: CANOPY Jackson Square
description:
Join us for a special evening featuring Professor Jacob Tsimerman (HBSc 2006), one of Canada’s leading mathematicians and a 2026 Fields Medal recipient.  
Recognized for resolving the Griffiths conjecture, recently appointed scientific director of the new Mathematics and AI Safety Institute in the Bay Area, and set to join OpenAI’s safety division, Professor Tsimerman will explore the evolving landscape of AI and safety, and the opportunities and challenges shaping our future.  
A networking reception will immediately follow with Chris Yip, Dean of the Faculty of Applied Science & Engineering and Stephen Wright, Dean of the Faculty of Arts & Science.   
Open to all U of T alumni and friends.  
Register 
About the speaker
 
Professor Jacob Tsimerman
Jacob Tsimerman is a Canadian mathematician and a professor in the Department of Mathematics in the Faculty of Arts & Science at the University of Toronto. His research focuses on analytic number theory and arithmetic geometry, particularly the study of integer solutions to certain types of polynomial equations.  
Born in Russia, Tsimerman developed an interest in mathematical puzzles at the age of three. He won two gold medals as a high school student at the International Mathematical Olympiad, including a perfect score in 2004. He studied mathematics at the University of Toronto as an undergraduate student and received his PhD from Princeton University in 2011, under the supervision of Peter Sarnak.  
Tsimerman held a postdoctoral position at Harvard University as a Junior Fellow of the Harvard Society of Fellows. In July 2014, he was awarded a Sloan Research Fellowship from the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation and began his term as assistant professor at the University of Toronto, where he currently holds the position of full professor.  
Tsimerman is widely recognized for his contribution to proving the long-standing André-Oort conjecture in 2021, a milestone in modern mathematics that links special points with broader geometric structures, which has since unlocked new avenues of research inquiry. This included establishing key results in functional transcendence theory, most notably, the Ax-Schanuel theorem for Hodge structures. He is also recognized for resolving the Griffiths conjecture, developing an o-minimal version of the GAGA theorems. He was awarded a 2026 Fields Medal from the International Mathematical Union in recognition of these and other achievements.  
Tsimerman was the Distinguished Visiting Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study’s  School of Mathematics for its 2025-26 Special Year on Arithmetic Geometry, Hodge Theory, and o-minimality.  
He was elected a fellow of both the Royal Society and the Royal Society of Canada in 2025, and was awarded the 2024 John L. Synge Award, the 2023 Ostrowski Prize, the 2022 New Horizons in Mathematics Prize, the 2019 Coxeter-James Prize and the 2015 Sastra Ramanujan Prize.

title: Looking at Picture Books
description:
Join us for an online special career series with the
2026 Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence
, Elly MacKay! In this series, Elly will share insights into building a career in children’s book illustration, covering topics such as the journey to working as an illustrator, an overview of classic children’s books, portfolios, and colour. Details about each session follow:
Thursday, October 8, 7pm:
Becoming an Illustrator
Elly MacKay shares her early and current work, her career path, and her process for creating miniature 3D worlds. Her talk also covers developing your style, illustration trends, and how to stand out.
Thursday, October 15, 7pm: Looking at Picture Books
Elly MacKay gives an overview of famous picture books, the various styles, what works, and how they’ve changed over the years. She looks at cover design, structure, page turns, and how visual storytelling and words work together.
Thursday, October 22, 7pm: From Portfolio to Book
Elly MacKay discusses portfolios and what to include, as well as working with agents and publishers. She also looks at what goes into creating your first picture book.
Thursday, October 29, 7pm: Colour and Atmosphere
Elly MacKay considers colour in picture books—how it can be used to strengthen a message, or to alter the mood. She looks at how illustrators have used colour in unconventional ways in their books.
Workshops will be recorded and available for replay through Zoom until October 31, 2026.
About Elly MacKay
Elly MacKay is a children’s book author and illustrator and a paper artist. She studied printmaking and illustration at NSCAD University in Halifax and University of Canterbury in Christchurch. Elly creates miniature worlds with drawing, painting and cutting, and photographs them for illustrations in children’s books. She has more than 20 books published in Canada and the US, including The Enchanted Symphony by Julie Andrews and Emma Walton Hamilton, I Am a Meadow Mermaid and The Secret Fawn by Kallie George. Elly is both author and illustrator of Frostfire, In the Clouds and Red Sky at Night and others. She lives with her family in Owen Sound, Ontario.
About the Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence Program
The
Illustrator in Residence
program honours the memory of illustrator Joanne Fitzgerald (1956-2011), and is a joint program of IBBY Canada, Toronto Public Library, and the Young Family.

title: Marina Nemat: Mistress of the Persian Boarding House
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
TPL presents internationally bestselling author Marina Nemat in conversation with Farah Heron at the North York Central Library's Concourse Event Space.
In her debut work of historical fiction, Mistress of the Persian Boarding House, Nemat turns to the extraordinary life of her paternal grandmother, Zina, a Russian woman who fled the chaos of the 1917 Revolution and rebuilt her life in Iran. There, in a boarding house that becomes a refuge for other displaced women, Zina forms an unbreakable bond with fellow outsiders from Russia and Iran, women who support one another through childbirth, illness, poverty, political upheaval, and a pandemic. Amid this turmoil, Zina's path crosses with the ambitious Reza Khan, the future Shah of Iran, whose presence in her life becomes both an escape and a source of enduring hardship and sorrow.
Spanning decades and alternating between Zina's years in Russia and her later life in Iran, this sweeping novel asks: what does it mean to build a home and a family from nothing, in the wreckage of empire and revolution?
Drawing on her own family history and her lifelong engagement with themes of exile, resilience, and the search for home, first explored in her internationally bestselling memoir Prisoner of Tehran, Nemat brings the same unflinching honesty and tenderness to her grandmother's story that made her own so unforgettable.
Join Marina Nemat for an intimate conversation about inheritance, chosen family, and the quiet heroism of women who have had to build their lives twice.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Marina Nemat
Farah Heron

title: OTTAWA:  Culture in the Capital (9th trip)
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
Can you join us in **Ottawa**?

*For a cultural long weekend! **Our 9th Ottawa trip!***

This trip is in just 3 months. Cooler days!

Dates/details are now FIRM--early FALL. **After Thanksgiving.**

PLEASE read everything over before signing up--all the details are here.

We will continue to explore the culture scene in some of our favorite Cities. **A deep dive/below the surface.**

Each year we bounce back and forth between Montreal & Ottawa.

This year in Ottawa--we'll also spend some time again in **GATINEAU** (Hull) for the second time--we can ***WALK*** between downtown Ottawa and downtown Hull (it takes just 30 minutes!!)

This will be our 9th 'long weekend' Ottawa trip since 2015. (--not the sleepy city you think it is--)

**Very important, PLEASE read all the information over before you RSVP.**
**You must contact me first. There is a *Non-Refundable fee* to join us.**

**Emailed/payable when you are confirmed.**

**$100 per person**

**Our 2026 (FALL) Ottawa trip will be built around**--our favorite contemporary galleries, architecture, public art, The National Gallery, Canadian Museum of History+++ food/drink. National Arts Centre.

**Plus our other usual favorite stops,** and a Group dinner.

All in 2 1/2 days!!

We are on the go each day from 10:30am-9pm, and **walk** everywhere.

Ottawa is the least expensive of our trips--perhaps $1000 all in?

What else do we do? Some combo of:

-visit other private/public galleries
-architecture tour/talks/walks
-Indigenous exploration
-public outdoor art
-food/drink
-other things which we don't yet know about
-much of what we do is FREE

**Note:** there is so much going on in Ottawa with regards to ART and CULTURE--don't think otherwise! We are welcomed everywhere.

This is a 3-night trip. The dates of this trip are AFTER Thanksgiving weekend.

**How these trips work:**

**YOU look after** your travel and accommodations (everyone has own personal budgets), **I look after** everything else. I plan ALL our activities on the ground while we are together. From first night drink/gallery visit (Thursday), to last night's group dinner (Saturday). You leave as you like on Sunday.

1. 3 nights (Thursday, Friday, Saturday) We meet as a group on Thursday at 5pm SHARP.
2. VIA train is currently showing $150 round trip ticket. How will you get there, where will you stay? Drive, bus, train, fly? (Your Presto card works in Ottawa--on public transit!)
3. Will you drive your car? Use 'points' for accommodations? Airbnb, B&B, Hotel, other? Do you need any insurance? You should aim to stay within a 15 mins walk of downtown/Byward Market. We walk everywhere!
4. There is a **NON-refundable fee sent to me when you signup/RSVP--due within 2 days.** I organize everything on the ground, discounts, tours, reservations etc. **TRIP FEE for 2026 is $100 per person.**
5. We will start with 10 people..until we know more about group sizing. But no more than 12 people.
6. Build into your trip budget: $75 for tickets/tours/entry, and $125 for our famous last night **group dinner**--we always find someplace special/memorable. Excellent OTTAWA food scene.
7. And of course, with all our trips there are always special/vip type surprises.
8. Agenda/schedule/Details in due course. You want to be in Ottawa and able to MEET up by **5pm on Thursday October 15th**. At the National Gallery.

Please read everything over before signing up. I keep you in the loop as per our planning, with a final schedule sent to you a few weeks before.

Thank you for your interest!

You can connect with me (Greg) at
[torontoisculture@gmail.com](http://torontoisculture@gmail.com/)

title: The Grim History of the Death Penalty in Canada
location: Brentwood, Community Room, Ground Floor
description:
Death by hanging was a grim reality within the Canadian criminal justice system until its abolition in 1976. But what did capital punishment look like in Canada? Author Lorna Poplak will discuss the history of the death penalty in Canada, with a focus on topics such as the inconsistent application of the death sentence, the treatment of women, wrongful conviction, the difficult journey toward abolition, and the last two hangings at Toronto's notorious Don Jail.
Q&A to follow. Signed books available for purchase.
Drop in, no registration required.

title: Flashback (X Avant XXI: Memory Mannnnn, Night 2)
location: First Unitarian Church,473 Oakwood Ave, York, ON M6C 2R5, Canada
description:
Sonic Bikes improvises with the soundworld of bicycles, and Bilal Nasser’s a punk & post-rock infused set delves into resistance, commemoration, and lament.

In the first set, local artist Stephanie Orlando brings her Sonic Bikes to the stage. A bespoke ensemble of improvising percussionists will make use of reassembled and sonified bike parts to animate a familiar soundworld of gears, spokes, and pedals. The performance takes on added weight as each artist exerts and sustains a particular pedal-powered labour to realize the piece, which is found in their constantly negotiated collective space.

During each of the other nights of the festival, Stephanie’s sound sculptures will be set up in the venue for audiences to interact and improvise with.

During the second set, Bilal Nasser will perform delay- and reverb-drenched solo works for guitar and voice. He will also be joined by a chamber ensemble to present a genre-bending suite about genocidal crisis and diasporic despair. Bilal blends post-rock, post-classical, punk, electronic, and shoegaze in a musical statement of commemoration, resistance, healing and lament. This performance marks the Toronto launch of Bilal’s album, Every Martyr is a Universe, on Constellation Records.

All prices are inclusive of HST.

title: 2026 Annual Toronto Graduate Philosophy Conference
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 100 (Main Floor Lecture Hall), 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
Join us for the 25th Annual Toronto Graduate Philosophy Conference with keynote speakers Don Garrett (NYU) and Alva Noë (University of California, Berkeley). 
Don J. Garrett is Silver Professor of Philosophy at New York University. He specializes in early modern philosophy, with particular interests in the philosophy of David Hume, Baruch Spinoza, and Mary Shepherd, and in areas including epistemology, metaphysics, philosophy of mind, and ethics. He is the author of Cognition and Commitment in Hume’s Philosophy (1997), Hume (2015), and Nature and Necessity in Spinoza’s Philosophy (2018), and editor of The Cambridge Companion to Spinoza (1996), and has also published numerous articles on early modern philosophy and related topics in leading academic journals. 
Alva Noë is Professor of Philosophy and Chair of the Department of Philosophy at the University of California, Berkeley. His research focuses on consciousness, perception, the philosophy of mind, and the philosophy of art. He is the author of Action in Perception (2004), Out of Our Heads: Why You Are Not Your Brain and Other Lessons from the Biology of Consciousness (2009), Strange Tools: Art and Human Nature (2015), and The Entanglement: How Art and Philosophy Make Us What We Are (2023), among other books. He has published extensively in academic journals and also writes for a broader public, with essays appearing in venues including The New York Times and The Atlantic.

title: Dear Disabled Black Woman: Film Screening and Q&A
location: Fairview, Fairview Library Theatre
description:
Please join us for a special screening of Dear Disabled Black Woman, an independently produced film by Ingrid Palmer, who has partial vision and advocates with and for Black and blind communities. The film centres seven Black women with disabilities, across a range of ages, cultural backgrounds, classes, sexual orientations and disabilities, as they share their experiences and perspectives on working with a disability in Canada. Q&A to follow.
Registration recommended. Doors open at 10:30 am. Light refreshments provided on a first come, first served basis.
This program is presented in partnership with the City of Toronto's Confronting Anti-Black Racism Unit.

York University offers leading graduate programs in Disaster & Emergency Management. Its Masters degree (MDEM) is the only such program offered in Ontario, and one of just two in Canada. It’s newly established PhD in Disaster & Emergency Management is the first such program in the entire country. In this exciting and rapidly expanding field you will explore key concepts, methodologies and technologies used by emergency management professionals while honing your analytical, research and critical thinking skills. Both the Master’s and Doctoral program are offered on a full-time or part-time basis, and prepare you to synthesize large amounts of complex information and make sound decisions in challenging and often difficult circumstances.
