title: Co-op Information Session
description:
York University Co-op Information Session (live webinar)
Location: Online – Link:  https://yorku.zoom.us/my/askcoop
Date: October 16, 2026
Time: 2:00pm-3:30pm
The York University Co-op Program provides students with opportunities for paid, hands-on learning and valuable industry experience. We encourage you to visit the Co-operative Education website to review program details and confirm that you meet the academic requirements.
During this session, you will learn about:

The co-op advantage
Eligibility requirements
Program fees
The registration process
General Q&A with a Co-op Coordinator

Target Audience:
These sessions are for York University students intending to begin their first co-op work term in Summer 2027. Before registering, please self-assess your eligibility for the program ( https://www.yorku.ca/career-ready/work-opportunities/co-op/eligibility/ ).

Live Session vs. Self-Paced Modules: What’s the Difference?
Based on student feedback, we now offer flexible options to complete the required sessions. Each format has unique benefits:

Live sessions (in-person or webinar): Opportunity to ask questions and interact directly with a Co-op Coordinator.
Self-paced eClass modules: Complete the content at a time that is most convenient for you.


Important Reminders:

Required sessions must be completed for your application to be reviewed.
Already attended a mandatory session within the last 12 months? You do not need to attend again.
Already admitted to Co-op? You are not required to complete the mandatory sessions or re-apply.
If you have an eligible work term for Summer 2027: Log in to the co-op portal and accept the terms and conditions when prompted.

We look forward to your participation!
Having trouble logging in? 
Please make sure you’re using your PPY York U login. When you select SSO (Single Sign-On), you should be prompted to sign in with your PPY credentials. If you use a different login, you may not be able to access the system.

title: Google AI Essentials: In Person Learning Circle
location: Northern District
description:
Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization.
This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz.
By completing the specialization,
you will learn:
How AI works
How to write effective prompts
How to use generative AI tools responsibly
How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm
How to stay up to date with AI news
After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions.
No AI experience is required.
How to Join
a Learning Circle:

valid email address

title: The Annual Dante Lecture 'Between Ulysses and Saint Francis: Models of Leadership in Dante'
location: Alumni Hall 400
description:
Please join us on October 16th, 2026 for our Day of Dante! 



Marking the 800th anniversary of the death of Saint Francis, this year’s lecture – Between Ulysses and Saint Francis: Models of Leadership in Dante – traces how Dante’s Divine Comedy offers a powerful vision of charismatic leadership through the contrasting figures of Ulysses and Saint Francis of Assisi. This year’s Dante Lecture will be presented by Heather Webb, Professor of Italian Studies at Yale University. 



2026 Dante celebrations will begin with The Dante Garden Tour from 4:30 to 5:30 p.m., followed by the annual Dante Lecture from 6 to 7:30 p.m. and a Reception from 7:30 to 9 p.m. at the John M. Kelly Library featuring a new exhibit of the collection: Dante Sings the Praises of St. Francis. 



The Annual Dante Lecture is a cornerstone event celebrating the enduring importance of Dante’s work within literature, theology, philosophy, and cultural history. The lecture was established through the generosity of Alberto and Caroline Di Giovanni.

title: Ancient Circuitry (X Avant XXI: Memory Mannnnn, Night 3)
location: First Unitarian Church,473 Oakwood Ave, York, ON M6C 2R5, Canada
description:
Gathering two artist’s projects in concert form, Ancient Circuitry combines Mani Mazinani’s Solar Organ and Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong’s For The Youth: Reilluminated, connecting with ancestral knowledge today.

Solar Organ Ensemble moves between improvised and composed music using traditional and invented pentatonic scales covering a spectrum of approaches to pentatonic sound generation. Solar Organ https://manimazinani.net/project.html?project=Solar-Organ , an electronic pentatonic instrument created by Mani Mazinani, connects neurobiology with the geographic and historic ubiquity of pentatonic practice, a universal human phenomenon.

For The Youth: Reilluminated by Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong, is a re-creation of a light and sound installation https://www.instagram.com/alexisnanibush_pamaj/p/DQngD8REaYa/?img_index=2 with local Indigenous youth performances — to honour the life, kinship, and the spirit of generations past, present, and future.

Curated by Mani Mazinani

INSTALLATION
Outside of performances, attendees can interact with sound sculptures from Night 2 https://musicgallery.org/events/flashback/ artist Stephanie Orlando.

Inspired by everyday sounds from her time working as a bike mechanic, Stephanie Orlando’s Sonic Bikes installation invites attendees to interact with the spectrum of noises and musical textures of recycled bike parts.

All prices are inclusive of HST.

title: Ishq Ke Saat Muqaam
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Ishq Ke Saat Muqaam (The Seven Stages of Love) returns with a renewed artistic vision, bringing together poetry, music, dance, and storytelling to explore one of humanity’s oldest and most profound questions: what does it mean to love?

Written and directed by Nishar Mansuri, the production is inspired by the Sufi understanding of ishq as a path of transformation. Through seven interconnected stages, the work moves from human longing to self-discovery, devotion, and surrender, inviting audiences into a journey that is both deeply personal and universal.

Featuring the poetry of Rumi, Amir Khusrau, Kabir, Bulleh Shah, Hafez, Fariduddin Attar, Sultan Bahu, and other mystic voices, the production reimagines centuries of mystical thought through contemporary performance. Their words become the foundation for an experience that transcends borders, languages, and faith traditions, inviting audiences to reflect on love as a force that connects us all.

title: Wilder Series: The Wilder Loop
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/wilder-loop-fall-26)**

**The loop is back and more wild than ever!**

For those unfamiliar, The Wilder Loop is 16 km of remote, rugged terrain through one of Ontario’s most untouched landscapes. Right from the start, the trail throws you into the wild: the first 5 km have everything we love about backcountry hiking; twisting forest paths, sweeping granite ridges, narrow boardwalks, and multiple beaver dams to scramble across. No two kilometers are the same, and every twist in the trail feels like a secret waiting to be found.

Once we hit the loop section, things get much quieter. This part of the park sees very few visitors as human footprints give way to moose tracks, and the rustling in the brush might just be one of the many beavers that call this area home.

Though the total elevation gain is relatively modest (about 260 m over the whole route), the trail’s difficulty comes from its remoteness, terrain, and ever-changing conditions. That said, for those willing to take it on, the reward is huge: sweeping views, total solitude, an unfiltered experience of Ontario’s boreal beauty... and a well-earned sense of pride by the time we make it back to the trailhead.

***Secret Location***
This is one of Wilderness Union's 'secret' hikes. As a group, we visit some truly special spots that are undiscovered by the wider world. We like to keep them pristine and only share them among our members- we ask that you do the same! We reveal the location to registered members in the days before the trip.

**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com

**Highlights**
**Untouched Wilderness:** Step into a landscape that feels frozen in time; wild, windswept, and wonderfully remote. Just you, the forest, and the sound of your boots on the trail.
**Wildlife Spotting:** Bears, moose, beavers and loons are just some of the creatures that call this area home. You'll have a chance to spot some from a safe distance for a magical encounter.
**Beaver Dam Crossings:** The area we're visiting is shaped by beavers. Tiptoe across nature’s original bridges- muddy, meticulously built, and surprisingly sturdy

**Event cost: $60+HST. $50 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/wilder-loop-fall-26)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: SOLD OUT: Birding with Beni: Fall Birding
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fall birding nature walk!
Fall migration is well underway! Join TBG Horticulturist and avid birder Sasan Beni for an engaging walk through the gardens and Wilket Creek Ravine, as you seek out the wildlife that call this place home. Learn how to identify the many different species passing through and how you can help them in their journey.
 
Bring your binoculars for a better view (we will have extras on hand) and a mug/thermos for a warm beverage and post-birding chat.
 
As with any wildlife tour, the spotting of birds and other wildlife is not guaranteed and is not within the control of the tour guide. Please be patient and considerate. The tour will not be rescheduled due to a lack of bird sightings. The tour will only be rescheduled due to inclement weather.
 
Meet at the TBG main entrance, just outside the George and Kathy Dembroski Centre for Horticulture.
 
Saturday, October 17, 8 to 10 a.m.
Public $22, Members $20 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Sasan Beni
Sasan Beni is a writer turned horticulturist. He graduated with a diploma in Environmental Landscape Management from Seneca College in King City, worked for the Toronto Zoo as a seasonal gardener, and joined TBG in 2020 as a seasonal Horticulturalist. His home is a revolving door of tropical plants. Beni is also passionate about birdwatching and wildlife photography. In the last three years, he has led many guided birdwatching walks around Toronto and has written several articles for Trellis magazine illustrated with his nature photographs.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Accessibility
The walk will be at a leisurely pace throughout, following designated pathways and trails but sometimes covering uneven terrain and steep inclines. Dress appropriately for the weather and walk slowly. Wearing layers is recommended. Closed-toed shoes are required. We will begin promptly. 
NOTE: This program occurs rain or shine (save for cases of extreme weather); please dress appropriately for the weather.
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: Mold-Making 101 with Janet Macpherson | 2 Weekends
location: 300 Campbell Avenue, Unit 115, Toronto, ON
description: Dates : Saturday and Sunday October 17-18 & 24-25 2026 Times : 10:00am - 4:00pm Location : 300 Campbell Avenue, Unit 115 Instructor : Janet Macpherson Unlock new creative possibilities in ceramics with our comprehensive Mold-Making 101 course. This hands-on class will guide you through the process of designing and creating plaster molds for both slip casting and press molding techniques. You’ll learn how to craft one-part and two-part molds, make decorative sprig molds, and combine slip-cast pieces into finished ceramic forms. This course is best for those with some hand-building experience. Throughout the course, you'll explore: - The fundamentals of plaster and its use in mold-making. - Techniques for creating and using press molds and sprig molds. - How to design and construct two-part molds for more complex shapes. - The basics of slip casting and assembling multi-part pieces. - Finishing techniques to prepare your work for firing and glazing. What you'll take home: - Your Molds of course! - 1 - 3 Slip cast pieces of each mold you complete Please note: 1) Glazing is not part of this course. You can book a glazing session seperately ($50) by emailing the technician at our Dupont Location. Glazing sessions include the use of our studio glazes. Firing fee is included. 2) Due to the hands-on and cumulative nature of this course, it's important to attend each session as we may not be able to repeat material covered in a missed class in a thorough way although we will try to catch you up. 3) By the end of the course, you'll have developed a new set of skills, a collection of unique molds, and the confidence to continue exploring mold-making in your own creative practice. ALL WORKSHOPS ARE NON REFUNDABLE

Design and carve your own ceramic bird tile using sgraffito, a centuries-old technique where you scratch through a layer of underglaze or slip to reveal the clay beneath, creating crisp, hand-drawn lines in the clay. title: Hurricane Hazel 2026 (SPECIAL ANNIVERSARY EDITION)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

On October 15, 1954, Toronto was devastated by the deadliest Hurricane of the 1954 season. Hazel was the most intense hurricane to hit the continent of North America in 1954.

Prior to the disaster that struck Toronto, the storm killed 469 people in Haiti, and the Caribbean before striking the United States. It roared ashore as a Category 4 hurricane.

After causing 95 deaths in the US, Hazel struck Ontario, raising the death toll by 81, mostly in Toronto. As a result of the high death toll and the damage caused, its name was retired from use.

But Toronto gained so much from the 1954 disaster, and our ravines and parklands are our lungs of the city. Thanks to Hazel we have our green spaces for generations to come.

This walking tour is for all levels and walkers with a few small hills and some steps. The tour begins outside the Weston Branch of the Toronto Public Library at Weston Road and 2 King Street, and returns to the starting location at the end of the walk. TTC bus routes are adjacent.

This special yearly tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Shoe Design 101
description:
Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026
Time: 1:00 pm – 3:30 pm
Location: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St. W.
Tickets: $30 General
Age Restriction: 16+ 
Step into the world of footwear design with Shoe Design 101, a hands-on introductory course led by Toronto-based designer and shoemaker Jasmine Martins. In this workshop, participants will learn the foundations of shoe design from sketching silhouettes and choosing materials to understanding proportions and construction techniques. 
Guided by Jasmine, you’ll gain the skills and confidence to start sketching your own shoe collection. Perfect for beginners and fashion enthusiasts alike, this class offers a behind-the-scenes look at the creative process that brings footwear to life. Join us for this inspiring session and take your first step toward becoming a footwear designer. 
Recommended for participants 16+. Includes instruction, materials, and access to all current exhibitions.  
BUY YOUR TICKETS  
ABOUT JASMINE MARTINS: 
 
Jasmine Martins is a Toronto-based footwear designer known for her vibrant, made-to-order creations that celebrate individuality, colour, and craftsmanship. Trained at the University of the Arts London and Arsutoria in Milan, Jasmine blends traditional shoemaking techniques with modern design sensibilities. Since launching Jasmine Martins Footwear in 2020, she’s built a growing reputation for bespoke shoes, freelance design, and thoughtful collaborations that bring personal stories to life through design..

title: Wildlife-friendly Fall Gardens
location: Toronto Reference Library, Room B1 (located in the basement)
description:
At this time of year, many people admire the fall colours but also feel the need to rake and dispose of leaves, cut dead stems, and remove fallen branches. But what if this tidying up negatively affects our gardens and pollinators? While we may not see the bees and butterflies during the fall and winter, they are still around!
In this presentation, Dorte Windmuller, a Butterflyway Ranger of the David Suzuki Foundation, will discuss how to maintain and protect wildlife habitat even throughout the colder months, and how “leave the leaves” can help nature come back stronger the next season.

The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Saturday October 17th from 2:30pm - 4:30pm Bring your yarn over and pull through to our two hour granny square class! From blankets; to sweaters; to bags; and much more, these cozy squares can be used in a wide range of designs. They’re a joy to make, simple to reproduce and easy to customize to your own style and project needs. This class teaches how to make a basic granny square, how to change colours and, how to join squares together. We’ll discuss variations in construction and further possibilities. She is the owner of Kaotic Ekko's Curiosities (closed) and Fibremancy (current). At age 7, she learned to crochet doilies from her grandmother who's adage was "If you can crochet doilies, you can crochet anything!" She learned to knit about 11 years ago from a lovely group of friends she met on the TTC Knitalong. She's taught various classes over the years, including crochet and polymer clay. She loves to share her knowledge as well as learn from others. 【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

title: Meet New People, Great Conversations & 50+ Board Games | 25–45 | Fast Friends
description:
Toronto 20's to 50's Singles Social (4000+)
Ever wish there were an easier way to turn a room full of strangers into people you actually want to talk to?
*That’s what Fast Friends is designed for.*

Instead of arriving at a busy pub and wondering who to approach, our host guides you through short conversations and rotations, giving you the chance to meet a variety of people throughout the evening. You get a little structure to make connecting easier — without making the evening feel forced or formal.

And once the hosted rounds finish, you can keep the evening going. 🎲
We’re back at Stout Irish Pub in Cabbagetown — a relaxed Irish pub with food, drinks and 50+ board games, giving you plenty of ways to continue socialising with the people you’ve met.

🎟️ Book Early & Save: [https://toronto17thoct.eventbrite.co.uk](https://toronto17thoct.eventbrite.co.uk)
Early Bird: CAD $10
Regular: CAD $15
At the Door: CAD $20 cash — to host Faye
Booking ahead helps us plan the right group size and venue space, and your ticket confirms your place.

🤝 What to Expect
7:00 PM — Welcome & Drinks
Meet your host, Faye, grab a drink and settle in.
Coming alone? Completely fine. Many guests arrive solo, and we’ll help you get comfortable and connected from the start.
7:30 PM — Fast Friends
This is where the evening gets going.
You’ll move through a series of short, guided conversations, meeting different people along the way. Our host keeps the rotations moving, so you don’t have to worry about who to approach or what to do next.
Just show up, join the conversation and see who you click with.

✨ Themed Connection Rounds
Throughout the evening, we’ll mix in themed rounds and interactive prompts designed to make connecting easier.
They’ll help you discover shared interests, experiences and unexpected things you have in common — taking the conversation beyond the usual small talk.

🎲 8:30 PM onwards — Board Games & Socialising
Once the hosted rounds finish, the evening doesn’t have to.
Stout has 50+ board games available, making it easy to keep the conversations going. Pick a game with the people you’ve met, grab another drink, join a group or simply continue chatting.
You don’t have to be a serious gamer — the games are simply another easy way to socialise and get to know people.

🍻 Staying Later?
Stout’s current After Dark Special runs from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.

❤️ Why Come Along?
✔️ Meet 15–25 new people in one evening
✔️ Guided conversations make meeting people easier
✔️ Meet different people through rotating conversations
✔️ Interactive themed rounds to spark better conversations
✔️ 50+ board games available afterwards 🎲
✔️ Relaxed Irish pub atmosphere
✔️ Reserved space for our group
✔️ Most guests come solo
✔️ Plenty of time to keep socialising after the hosted rounds
✔️ Friendship-focused — not a dating event

👋 Who Is It For?
Ages 25–45
Whether you’ve just moved to Toronto, have lived here for years, or simply feel like your social circle could use some fresh faces, you’re welcome.
You don’t need to know anyone beforehand or arrive with a group.
Come by yourself, bring a friend, or simply come ready to have a few good conversations and see where the evening takes you.

🌍 About Fast Friends
For over 10 years, Fast Friends has been bringing people together through professionally hosted social events in 30+ cities worldwide.
Our goal is simple: make meeting new people easier, more relaxed and more enjoyable.
Come for the conversations. Stay for the games. Leave with new connections. ❤️

title: Ishq Ke Saat Muqaam
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Ishq Ke Saat Muqaam (The Seven Stages of Love) returns with a renewed artistic vision, bringing together poetry, music, dance, and storytelling to explore one of humanity’s oldest and most profound questions: what does it mean to love?

Written and directed by Nishar Mansuri, the production is inspired by the Sufi understanding of ishq as a path of transformation. Through seven interconnected stages, the work moves from human longing to self-discovery, devotion, and surrender, inviting audiences into a journey that is both deeply personal and universal.

Featuring the poetry of Rumi, Amir Khusrau, Kabir, Bulleh Shah, Hafez, Fariduddin Attar, Sultan Bahu, and other mystic voices, the production reimagines centuries of mystical thought through contemporary performance. Their words become the foundation for an experience that transcends borders, languages, and faith traditions, inviting audiences to reflect on love as a force that connects us all.

title: Cliffs & Fall Colours: A Bruce Peninsula Hike
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/bruce-peninsula-26)**

**The Bruce Peninsula does dramatic better than almost anywhere else in Ontario, and fall is when it really shows off.**

We'll be out for most of the day, covering 8.5km of moderate hiking through some of the best autumn scenery in the province, with the changing leaves against the escarpment's limestone making for a proper contrast.

We'll start in the forest before the trail opens onto the coastline, tracing the cliffs down to the Grotto. It's the most photographed spot on the peninsula for good reason: crystal clear water, a sea cave carved into the rock, and a natural window out to the bay. We'll take our time here, including a stop for lunch.

From the Grotto we'll keep following the shoreline out to Stormhaven, crossing pebble beaches with open views across Georgian Bay the whole way. We'll turn around there and retrace the coastline back, catching all the same cliffs and colour from the other direction with the light shifted by then.

**Two important things to note:**

1. **Self driving isn't possible for this trip. Parking passes at the trailhead sell out well in advance, so all members travel together on WU transport.**
2. **Bruce Peninsula National Park is stunning, but be aware that it is a long drive there and back. Full details are in the itinerary below.**

**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com

**Highlights**
**The Grotto:** The peninsula's most famous natural feature: a limestone sea cave with turquoise water and a rock window looking out over Georgian Bay.
**Stormhaven Coastline:** A stretch of cobble beach with wide open views across the bay, well past where most day hikers turn around.
**Fall Colour on the Escarpment:** Peak autumn colour against the Niagara Escarpment's pale limestone cliffs, a contrast you don't get anywhere else on the Bruce Trail\*\*.\*\*

**Event cost: $140+HST. Transportation is included in the cost of the adventure. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/bruce-peninsula-26)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: Paper Quilling: Fall Tree Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Celebrate the magic of autumn with a relaxing day of creativity at the beautiful Toronto Botanical Garden!
Join artist Deepa Krishnan for a fun, beginner-friendly paper quilling workshop. In this 4-hour session, you’ll learn a variety of quilling techniques while creating a stunning fall tree on an 8”x10” canvas. Inspired by the rich colours of the season, you’ll have the freedom to choose your own autumn palette, making your artwork truly one of a kind.
 
This workshop includes a 30-minute lunch break. We recommend bringing your own lunch to enjoy while taking in the beautiful surroundings of the garden.
 
Whether you’re trying paper quilling for the first time or looking to expand your skills, this workshop is a wonderful way to slow down, get creative, and celebrate the beauty of the season.
 
All supplies are included, and no prior experience needed. This workshop is suitable for adults and children ages 12 and above.
 
Sunday, October 18, 10:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.
Public $100, TBG Members $90 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Deepa Krishnan
Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling, which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling, that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level, and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: Impressionist Afternoon Tea + 3 Exhibits at the AGO
description:
Experience Toronto
On **Sunday, October 18th**, join me for an **Impressionist Afternoon Tea in the Norma Ridley Members’ Lounge to celebrate the connection between art, atmosphere and indulgence.** Inspired by the luminous colours and expressive brushstrokes of *[Impressionist Revolution: Monet to Matisse from the Dallas Museum of Art](https://ago.ca/exhibitions/impressionist-revolution-monet-matisse-dallas-museum-art)* we saw last month, this seasonal Afternoon Tea offers an elegant, leisurely escape into art, conversation and thoughtfully crafted flavours that reflect the beauty and softness of this exhibit. Delicate savoury selections and whimsical pastries are designed to evoke sunlit gardens, countryside picnics and the romance of Impressionism. Since Afternoon Tea includes free admission to the Gallery, we will see more Impressionism art that was not part of our August visit - **Reality & Reverie: Canadian and European Painting Beyond Impressionism**, **Steam: Impressionist Painting Across the Atlantic**, and a new exhibit that will open the day before - **In Plain Sight: Highlights from the AGO’s Collection of Historic Picture Frames**. **I** **have booked a table for Sunday October 18th at 2:30pm, and can add members to it.**

**COST**
Adult: $80 + taxes + gratuity = $104.80

Meetup Organizer Fee: $5

**SIGNING-UP**

* **RSVP Yes** **\- everyone goes on the waitlist until confirmed\.**
* **I will reach out to provide my email address for the etransfer of $109.80 and I will call in to add you to our table. Once I receive confirmation, I will inform you and move you to attending.**
* There are no refunds.

A reminder will be sent the day before with my cell and reminder details where to meet and when.

RSVPs close 3 days prior and the Waitlist will be removed at that time. Cancellations will result in a No Show and impact future attendance.

**MEETUP TIME**
**Meet me at: 1:45pm inside the entrance to the right side of the AGO at 317 Dundas St. W. We will then scan our tickets and head over to the exhibits, prior to Tea.**

**Note: We must enter the AGO together for our tea reservation.**

**EXHIBITS**
**Reality & Reverie: Canadian and European Painting Beyond Impressionism** (Level 1 Gallery 127)

**Steam: Impressionist Painting Across the Atlantic** (Level 1 Gallery 116)

**Highlights from the AGO’s Collection of Historic Picture Frames** (Level 1 Gallery 115)

**Meet me for Afternoon Tea: at 2:30pm in front of the** **Norma Ridley Members’ Lounge (Level 1)** (Please do not go to our table before I get there)

We will be covering chaining and single crochet, as well as double and half-double crochets. Don’t know what any of that means? Great, you’re in the right place! We’ll provide all the materials, including a simple pattern that teaches you common terms and instructions you’ll encounter in most crochet projects. We will also discuss how to choose the appropriate yarn and hook for a project as well as where you can take your crafting after you master these basic techniques. There’s a lot to learn, and we’re excited to accompany your beginning in the wonderful craft of crochet! Materials are included! - 50g ball of worsted weight cotton in your choice of colour - 6mm crochet hook Our class size is capped at 4 people, so everyone can receive the attention they need. Mike will share lots of tips and techniques to get you well on your way. About the instructor: Tired of disposing of clothes that were still perfectly wearable, Mike (he/him) started crafting mainly as a means of mending and repair. This led him to knitting (and later crochet), which pretty much immediately became one of his favourite tools of self-expression. Please note that classes will only proceed if we have a minimum of two attendees . If the minimum is not met, there will be the option for a refund or to reschedule. There will be a four person maximum for each class. Please pre-book your spot to let us know you are coming! Cancellation Policy Classes must be paid for at the time of registration to reserve your spot. - If cancelled 48 hrs or more prior to the start of the first class will be given a store credit. Classes cancelled less than 48 hrs prior to the start of the class will not be reimbursed.

Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
Join our **Spanish–English Language Exchange Meetup** and improve your conversation skills in a relaxed, social environment. This free event is perfect for anyone looking to practice Spanish or English while meeting new people in a cozy coffee shop setting.

### **🗣️ What You’ll Do**

* Practice Spanish and English through real conversations
* Join small groups and switch languages throughout the event
* Learn practical vocabulary and everyday expressions
* Build confidence speaking in a supportive environment

### **👥 Who Should Attend**

* Spanish learners (all levels)
* English learners (all levels)
* Native speakers who want to help others
* Anyone interested in language exchange and cultural connection

### **☕ Venue**

We meet at a local coffee shop—just grab a drink and enjoy the conversation!

### **💸 Cost**

**FREE event** (please support the venue by purchasing a drink)

### **🌟 Why Join?**

Language exchanges are one of the most effective ways to learn. You’ll improve faster by speaking with real people, hearing authentic accents, and using the language in everyday situations.
Whether you're a beginner or fluent speaker, you’ll find a welcoming community ready to practice and connect.

**👉 RSVP now and start speaking with confidence!**

Lectures & Snacks is your chance to mingle with fellow York grad and mature students over light refreshments while enjoying a short, engaging talk by a student, faculty or staff member. Think of it as a mini lecture with maximum curiosity…and snacks!

title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: A Good War
location: Toronto Reference Library, Lower Level, Room B1
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
October’s book is
A Good War: Mobilizing Canada for the Climate Emergency
by public policy advisor Seth Klein. Copies of the book are available in print, eBook & eAudiobook format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
"In A Good War, Seth Klein explores how we can align our politics and economy with what the science says we must do to address the climate crisis. But Klein brings an original and uniquely hopeful take to this challenge. The book is structured around lessons from the Second World War – the last time Canada faced an existential threat. Others have said we need a “wartime approach” to climate change, but this is the first book to delve into what that could actually look like. Canada’s wartime experience, Klein contends, provides an inspirational reminder that
we have done this before
. We have mobilized in common cause across class, race and gender, and entirely retooled our economy in the space of a few short years."
Drop in. No registration required.

title: Co-op Information Session: In Person
description:
York University Co-op Information Session 
Date: October 19, 2026
Time: 2:30pm-4:00pm
Location: Victor Phillip Dahdaleh Building, Room 1012
The York University Co-op Program provides students with opportunities for paid, hands-on learning and valuable industry experience. We encourage you to visit the Co-operative Education website to review program details and confirm that you meet the academic requirements.
During this session, you will learn about:

The co-op advantage
Eligibility requirements
Program fees
The registration process
General Q&A with a Co-op Coordinator

Who should attend? These sessions are for York University students intending to begin their first co-op work term in Summer 2027. Before registering, please self-assess your eligibility for the program ( https://www.yorku.ca/career-ready/work-opportunities/co-op/eligibility/ ).
Live Session vs. Self-Paced Modules: What’s the Difference?
Based on student feedback, we now offer flexible options to complete the required sessions. Each format has unique benefits:

Live sessions (in-person or webinar): Opportunity to ask questions and interact directly with a Co-op Coordinator.
Self-paced eClass modules: Complete the content at a time that is most convenient for you.

Important Reminders:

Required sessions must be completed for your application to be reviewed.
Already attended a mandatory session within the last 12 months? You do not need to attend again.
Already admitted to Co-op? You are not required to complete the mandatory sessions or re-apply.
If you have an eligible work term for Summer 2027: Log in to the co-op portal and accept the terms and conditions when prompted.

We look forward to your participation!

title: AI for Job Hunting: Build Your Own System
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
Job hunting is a job in itself: applications, deadlines, interviews, follow-ups. What if you could build your own AI-powered system to help you manage it?
In this hands-on class, you'll explore a job-hunting dashboard built with AI: how it tracks applications, sets automatic alerts for postings that match you, and practices interviews with you through role-play. “The truth is that we are one body moving through time together.” — Richard Wagamese 
How do we love and care for ourselves, one another, and our world? 
Embedded in the depth of our being we hold the truth of all creation. Clay grounds us and reconnects us to our shared humanity, the fertile Earth, and all life. Guided by a Zen practitioner and registered art therapist, engage in the simple physical practice of breath with clay. 
Working with clay, we acknowledge what has gone before us, care for the fruits of this moment, sync our energy through the rhythm of breath, nurture resonance, and remember and activate stewardship of future generations. 
At the end of the workshop we return the clay to its original form, letting go of what was created and ready to begin anew. 
This workshop welcomes everyone, whether you are new to or familiar with clay, breath, and presence.

                    Suzanne Thomson is ceramic artist, Zen Buddhist practitioner, and art therapist with over 30 years of experience integrating these practices to facilitate healing, community building, and social transformation work. As a practitioner of Zen Buddhism with training in contemplative arts, sensorimotor psychotherapy, narrative therapy and trauma-informed approaches, she offers psychotherapy, clinical supervision, and has taught at the Toronto Art Therapy Institute and the University of Toronto. Transformation by Fire: Women Overcoming Violence Through Clay, a 10-year retrospective at the Gardiner Museum facilitated by Suzanne, won the 2013 OMA Award of Excellence in Exhibitions. title: Taming the Tyrant: Democracy and Political Accountability in Athens and Today
location: Agincourt, Multipurpose Room, 1st floor
description:
How much power should a single individual have in a democracy? And how might ordinary citizens hold political elites to account? Dr. Ella Street (PhD, Political Theory, University of Toronto) takes us back to classical Athens to explore these enduring questions. Examining the remarkable institutions and cultural practices Athenians developed to keep their leaders in check, she considers what it really means for the demos—the people—to rule supreme.
Despite all that separates ancient and modern democracy, Athens offers surprising lessons for our own moment. As democracies today grapple with powerful individuals—from mayors and heads of state to corporate and technology elites—what might we learn from the Athenians about keeping power in the hands of the people? title: The Information Battle: Elections, Journalism and Misinformation
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall
description:
As elections take place in an increasingly complicated online world, voters are exposed to a huge mix of news, social media posts, AI-generated content, and false information spread by organized groups. New digital technologies have made it easier for people to learn about issues and take part in civic life, but they have also raised concerns about trust, fair elections, and respectful public discussion.
This panel brings together experts in misinformation, journalism, and election administration to explore the challenges and opportunities facing democracy today. How are AI and new technologies changing the way people get information? What do these changes mean for voters, journalists, and election officials? And what can be done to build public trust in elections while helping people stay informed and engaged in public life?

Nick Hune-Brown

title: David Treuer: The Savage Mind
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
New York Times bestselling author David Treuer shares his groundbreaking, intimate reckoning with the history of North America.
The Savage Mind is a seamless blend of memoir, history and reportage, in which Treuer leverages his unique dual perspective as the son of a Holocaust survivor and the first American Indigenous woman judge in the United States to offer an examination of the distinct nature of North American violence.
In contrast to the frontier thesis of American history, Treuer contends that frontier violence cannot be defined as an external force, but that it has actually entered the culture and taken root in our very selves.
By reckoning with these histories, the book confronts our complicity in either normalizing violence, or blaming it on outside sources, instead of seeing its recurring patterns and contending with its significance.
David Treuer speaks with journalist and author Tanya Talaga about The Savage Mind and shares why he chooses to embrace an ultimately hopefully view of the continent.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: The Certificate in Personal Wellness for Grad Students
location: Zoom Session
description:
The Certificate in Personal Wellness is a supportive and enriching experience designed to nurture personal well-being and promote balance in everyday life. Participants will explore practical, evidence-informed strategies for reducing stress, understanding and managing negative thought patterns, and building emotional resilience. Drawing from the field of positive psychology, the series introduces empowering practices such as mindfulness, gratitude, and self-compassion—skills that encourage greater self-awareness, inner calm, and a more compassionate relationship with oneself. Aspects of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy and Dialetical Behaviour Therapy will be included.



Dates: October 20, 27, November 3, 10 & 17​




Time: 10:30 A.M. – 12:00 P.M. (ET)
Open to: Graduate Students

title: How to Publish a Book with a University Press: A Scholarly Publishing Seminar
location: 242 York Lanes
description:
James MacNevin and Shalini Nanayakkara, editors at the University of British Columbia Press, are pleased to present a book publishing workshop on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, @ 11 a.m. at York Lanes room 242. The session will consist of a 45-minute presentation followed by a Q&A period. Graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, and faculty in the social sciences and humanities are welcome to attend.
The talk will focus on scholarly book publishing and will provide an opportunity to learn about the process of publishing with a university press in Canada. Topics of discussion include:

what distinguishes university presses from other publishers
how to locate the appropriate publisher for your work
how to prepare a compelling proposal
how to turn your thesis into a book
the peer review process
sources of funding for scholarly monographs
what to expect of your publisher and what your publisher will expect of you

Event Details

Location: 242 York Lanes

Students juggle a lot, from academics and work to family and friends. It can be hard to prioritize your own health and well-being at the same time.

Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.

Looking for some feedback on your work, career path, or life after OCAD U? title: Python Essentials 1 and 2 Learning Circle
location: York Woods
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Tuesday afternoons from September 22 to December 8, 2-3:30pm. description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)

[RESULTS of the poll for this event]

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"The Devotion of Suspect X was a hit with critics and readers alike. The first major English language publication from the most popular bestselling writer in Japan, it was acclaimed as "stunning," "brilliant," and "ingenious."
Now physics professor Manabu Yukawa—Detective Galileo—returns in a new case of impossible murder, where instincts clash with facts and theory with reality.
Yoshitaka, who was about to leave his marriage and his wife, is poisoned by arsenic-laced coffee and dies. His wife, Ayane, is the logical suspect—except that she was hundreds of miles away when he was murdered. The lead detective, Tokyo Police Detective Kusanagi, is immediately smitten with her and refuses to believe that she could have had anything to do with the crime. His assistant, Kaoru Utsumi, however, is convinced Ayane is guilty. While Utsumi's instincts tell her one thing, the facts of the case are another matter. So she does what her boss has done for years when stymied—she calls upon Professor Manabu Yukawa.
But even the brilliant mind of Dr. Yukawa has trouble with this one, and he must somehow find a way to solve an impossible murder and capture a very real, very deadly murderer.
Salvation of a Saint is Keigo Higashino at his mind-bending best, pitting emotion against fact in a beautifully plotted crime novel filled with twists and reverses that will astonish and surprise even the most attentive and jaded of readers." (from [Macmillan Publishers](https://us.macmillan.com/books/9781250036278/salvationofasaint/))

"When a man is discovered dead by poisoning in his empty home his beautiful wife, Ayane, immediately falls under suspicion. All clues point to Ayane being the logical suspect, but how could she have committed the crime when she was hundreds of miles away?
As Tokyo police detective Kusanagi tries to unpick a seemingly unrelated sequence of events he finds himself falling for Ayane. When his judgement becomes dangerously clouded his assistant must call on an old friend for help; it will take a genius to unravel the most spectacular web of deceit they have ever faced…
SALVATION OF A SAINT is a magnificently complex and page-turning thriller starring international crime fiction’s most enigmatic sleuth.This is essential reading for all fans of exceptional crime fiction." (from [Hachette UK](https://www.hachette.co.uk/titles/keigo-higashino/salvation-of-a-saint/9780349138817/))

title: Civic Meetup #565: Measuring Main Streets: Data Tools for Transit-Oriented Communities
location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom / Health Sciences Building
description:
Topic: Measuring Main Streets: Data Tools for Transit-Oriented Communities

Understanding what communities need from housing and transit, and deploying evidence-based responses to those needs is hard. Who's living in housing around transit infrastructure? What amenities are in their neighbourhood, and what's missing? What housing stock exists? How can it be developed further to serve the local community effectively? And of course, how does walkability fit into this whole picture?

To equip community leaders with tools to answer these questions and more, the Canadian Urban Institute (CUI) developed Measuring Main Streets. It's a digital platform bringing together unique neighbourhood-level data on demographics, housing development potential, and community amenities in and around transit station areas.

We'll demo the platform's tools and show how they go beyond traditional transit-oriented development, which tends to focus on density, to make the case for what we call transit-oriented complete communities: places where transit investment also delivers the amenities and housing mix people actually need.

Speakers: Greg Spencer (he/him), Luca Carnegie (he/him)

Greg has over 20 years of experience in urban and economic development policy making and research. He has worked in consulting and academia roles across Canada, the UK, and Ireland helping local communities reach their full potential. He has co-authored high profile reports with leading urban think tanks such as Brookings Metro, The Martin Prosperity Institute, and NESTA. He has also co-authored op-eds in the Globe and Mail, the Toronto Star, and The Guardian. He holds a Ph.D. in Economic Geography and a M.Sc. in Planning from the University of Toronto and a B.A. in Geography from Bishops University.

Luca is a Data Analyst on the Data Analytics Team at the Canadian Urban Institute. After graduating, he dove into urban data science at the CUI to drive evidenced-based, multidisciplinary solutions to urban challenges. He holds a Bachelor of Information in Information Systems from the University of Toronto. In his free time, he loves to watch and act in musical theatre, play music, and test new recipes in his kitchen. This is his second time presenting at Civic Tech and is SO excited to be back!!

Agenda:

7:00-7:20 Welcome and Introductions

7:20-7:50 Presentation and Q\&A/discussion

7:50-9:00 Breakout groups

‎

Code of Conduct: https://civictech.ca/about-us

‎

Check in with us on the Civic Tech Toronto Slack: https://link.civictech.ca/chat

‎

title: Jamaluddin Aram: The Blood of Things
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
TPL presents Afghan-Canadian writer Jamaluddin Aram in conversation with Dmitri Nasrallah at the North York Central Library's Concourse Event Space.
What does it mean to carry a homeland inside you after it has been lost, not once, but again and again? In his essay collection
The Blood of Things
, Aram turns his attention fully to Afghanistan, its beauty, its suffering, and its complexity. Spanning from the recent fall of Kabul to the early days of Islam, from the myth of the Order of Assassins to the persecution of the country's ethnic Hazara community, Aram weaves personal stories with sweeping historical and political inquiry.
Drawing on his own journey from Afghanistan to Toronto, and his work as associate producer of the Oscar-nominated film
Buzkashi Boys
, Aram brings a novelist's eye for character and an essayist's rigor to bear on questions of identity, belonging, and what remains possible even amid profound loss.
Join Jamaluddin Aram for an intimate evening of readings and conversation on exile, memory, and the enduring pull of home.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Jamaluddin Aram
Dimitri Nasrallah
Read more:
Blood of Things : A Love Letter to Afghanistan
Nothing Good Happens in Wazirabad on Wednesday

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions.
Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle.

n a Learning Circle:

title: Embodied Garden: 8-Week Art Therapy Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join Mahja Kabir, an artist and art therapy trainee, for an eight-week closed art therapy group for adults!
Embodied Garden invites participants to slow down, connect with nature, and explore their inner world through creative expression. Each session includes a brief embodiment meditation, gentle check-in, nature-inspired art-making, and optional sharing.
 
Across the eight weeks, the garden becomes both a setting and a metaphor for exploring themes of grounding, growth, movement, boundaries, protection, change, community, and belonging. Each session introduces a distinct theme while contributing to an overarching exploration of embodiment, connection, and our relationship with the natural world.
 
As a closed group, participants are invited to attend all eight sessions. The continuity of the series offers opportunities to build trust, develop connections, and reflect more deeply as the sessions unfold.
 
The group is facilitated by Mahja Kabir, an artist and art therapy trainee who creates gentle, creative spaces that support reflection, care, growth, and connection. Art therapy uses the creative process as a way to explore emotions, experiences, relationships, and self-awareness, with no emphasis on artistic skill or producing a finished artwork.
 
Wednesdays, October 21 through December 9, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. (eight sessions).
Public $160, TBG Members $120 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Résumé and Cover Letter for Industry
description:
About the facilitator 
 
Jessica Wurster, Career Exploration & Education, Graduate Career Educator  
Jessica (she/they) has been supporting students in their career journeys for over 15 years at universities in Quebec and Ontario. As Graduate Career Educator, Jess draws on their doctoral training in Communication Studies and professional experience to develop and deliver programming and resources targeted to professional and graduate students and recent alumni. She’s also a quilter, a frequenter of farmer’s markets in the east end and beyond, and a collector of cookbooks.    
Looking to tune up your résumé and cover letter for industry roles? Join us for a session with Career Exploration & Education to learn strategies, tips, and AI-assisted approaches to build and refresh your industry job application materials.  
We will discuss:  

Creating application materials targeted to industry roles  
How to analyze industry job descriptions so you can successfully tailor your résumé  
Strategies to create a more effective and captivating résumé including writing strong accomplishment statements and organizing résumé sections effectively 
How to use AI tools effectively and ethically to support résumé and cover letter development, including prompt-engineering techniques that help generate stronger content, identify skills alignment, and customize materials for specific roles 
Best practices for reviewing, refining, and personalizing AI-generated content to ensure authenticity and accuracy 

Bonus Activity: Participate in a résumé review for personalized feedback! You will need to bring a digital copy of your working résumé (it does not need to be finalized) and be ready to share it with your peers. You’ll also can practice AI prompting strategies to strengthen and tailor your application materials  
Register in Advance.

title: Recovery College: YU & Balance Week 1 | Self-care: Making time for your basic needs
location: Markham Campus (MK2050)
description:
This session will be offered in person at York University’s Markham Campus and is open to students from all York University campuses.
In this week’s session of YU & Balance, we will focus on building realistic self-care and time management habits that fit into student life.
Students will reflect on questions such as:

What motivates me to take care of myself?
What tends to get in the way of self-care?
How can I make time for myself when life gets busy?

Through discussion and reflection, students will explore ways to prioritize their well-being, build self-care into their routines and practice affirmations that support confidence and motivation.
This session is part of a 6-week Recovery College series. For each session attended, participants will receive $5 on their YU-card. To receive the gift card, you must attend the full session (approximately 45–60 minutes). Unfortunately, we’re not able to provide gift cards for partial attendance. Gift cards will be emailed after the session to the same email address used to register and join the session.
Space is limited, and registration is offered on a first-come, first-served basis. If the session is full and you’d like to be added to the waitlist, please email hstacey@yorku.ca. We’ll reach out if a spot becomes available. If you’re registered but can no longer attend, please let us know as soon as you can so we can offer your spot to another student.

title: Working With Your Go To Emotional State

It is the emotion that shows up automatically when we feel hurt or overwhelmed. That emotion can be
anger, anxiety, depression, guilt, shame, or even emotional numbness.
In this interactive presentation, we will explore how your go-to emotion developed, what purpose it serves, and offer techniques on how to respond from a more measured space.
Join Ann Schnurr, a Registered Psychotherapist with more than 25 years of experience, as she supports adults to understand their go-to emotion for greater emotional resilience, healthier relationships, and a deeper connection with self.
Registration is encouraged

Drop-ins welcome until capacity is reached.  For more information contact the Business Science & Technology desk at 416-395-5613

location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
The Friendship Test
Bring your best friend, your partner, or your whole crew and put your friendship to the test, Newlywed Game–style. Answer questions about each other's habits, histories and hot takes to see who really knows who, and who's got some catching up to do. It's playful proof that even our closest bonds have more to discover, echoing Berkowitz's case that friendship takes real, ongoing work.
This interactive pre-show is followed by
Friendships and other Complexities ft. Roger Berkowitz
, which starts at 7pm in the Appel Salon.
You can register for that event
here
, but please note if you wish to attend the pre-event activities you need to register separately
on this page
.

This evening’s
theme explores
the challenge of
staying in dialogue and connection across our
difference
s
through Hannah Arendt’s friendships
.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the
featured event
. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. Sign up for the workshop or try out one of the engagement activities available, including this event's Conversation Station: The Kitchen Table, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger to reflect on the rewards and challenges of friendship.
The Kitchen Table |
5:30 – 6:30 pm & 8:00 – 9:00 pm
Grab a seat and dig into the questions we rarely ask out loud: How has your definition of friendship changed? Can you stay close to someone you disagree with? What makes a friendship last? Inspired by Berkowitz's argument that friendship — not agreement — is the glue of a healthy society, this café is a space to reflect on your own circle with the strangers sitting next to you.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: Bridging Minds: Menopause, Metabolism and Heart Health: What Changes at Midlife
description:
What happens to your heart and metabolism as you move through menopause? As hormone levels change through the transition, so can the way your body manages cholesterol, blood sugar, fat and other factors that influence long-term heart health.
Join Dr. Iliana Lega for the next Bridging Minds: Health & Science Conversations webinar to understand these changes and what you can do to support your health. Building on last month’s conversation about menopause and brain health, this session broadens the picture to explore heart and metabolic health, practical strategies for prevention, and what current evidence tells us about the role of menopausal hormone therapy.
What to Expect
What changes during menopause:
Understand how the menopause transition can affect cardiovascular risk factors, metabolism, body composition and weight.
What you can do:
Explore practical lifestyle and preventive strategies to support heart and metabolic health during midlife.
The role of hormone therapy:
Learn what current evidence tells us about menopausal hormone therapy and cardiovascular and metabolic health.
About the Presenter
Dr. Iliana Lega is a staff endocrinologist at Women’s College Hospital, and a scientist at the Women’s College Hospital Research and Innovation Institute. Dr. Lega’s clinical interests lie in the area of diabetes, as well as reproductive endocrinology, including Premature Ovarian Insufficiency (POI), Turner syndrome, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), and Menopause.
About the Series
Bridging Minds: Health & Science Conversations is a partnership between the Toronto Public Library and Women’s College Hospital. Through monthly discussions led by experts from across different clinical areas and scientific disciplines, this series provides attendees with the opportunity to engage directly with our topics and speakers and empowers communities to navigate health and science topics confidently, inspiring a future of informed decision-making.
Learn more:
https://www.womenscollegehospital.ca/bridging-minds/

title: New Sounds, New Space Report Launch + Wavelength Documentary Premiere
location: St. Anne's Parish Hall,651 Dufferin St, Toronto, ON M6K 2B2, Canada
description:
Presented with Sonic Boom


October 21, 2026
Wavelength @ St. Anne’s

651 Dufferin St.

6PM

Free - RSVP at http://bit.ly/NSNSwl


You are invited to join Wavelength for an evening of original content! Local music lovers will enjoy this free presentation, panel, and screening plus a networking session soundtracked by DJ Uncle Chayne.


Be the first to view Wavelength: 25 Years of Music & Community, a short documentary written and directed by Ian Daffern (Idfactory) telling the story of Toronto’s unique artist-run concert series and non-profit organization. A who’s who of Canadian music, this project was scored and mixed by Justin Small (Do Make Say Think, BODY///GRAVE) and music supervised by Babs V. Westerholm (Cue Queens) and features interviews with Melissa Auf der Maur (Hole, Smashing Pumpkins), Emilie Hanskamp, pHoenix Pagliacci, Charles Spearin (Broken Social Scene, Do Make Say Think), and Wavelength’s Jonathan Bunce (AKA Jonny Dovercourt). Additional music by Burs, Luge, MOONBEAN, Orbital Ensemble, Paul Chin, Pony Da Look, Rich Aucoin, Sook-Yin Lee and more.


A follow up to 2023’s acclaimed Reimagining Music Venues Study, the launch of the “New Sounds, New Space” report explores different pathways for establishing community hubs for Toronto’s grassroots music community. With positive case studies on Hugh’s Room Live, It’s Ok* Studios, Small World Music and Primal Note Studios, the report shines light on Toronto’s post-COVID music venue landscape while pointing the way forward for imaginative new spaces. Funded by Canada Council for the Arts “Seed” grant!


Join in on the conversation that shapes Toronto’s music culture from the ground up.

title: Friendships and other Complexities ft. Roger Berkowitz
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
This evening’s theme explores the challenge of staying in dialogue and connection across our differences through Hannah Arendt’s friendships.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the featured event. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. Sign up for
The Friendship Test Workshop
(see registration below) or try out one of the engagement activities available, including tonight’s
Conversation Station: The Kitchen Table
, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger to reflect on the rewards and challenges of friendship.
*****
Join us at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon
for
Friendships and other Complexities
with political theorist Roger Berkowitz in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia.
This one is about the harder kind of connection: staying in relationships with people you disagree with. We'll consider friendship not as a private comfort but as political work; the daily, unglamorous business of talking with people whose views unsettle us and whose reasoning we may never fully understand. Expect to be asked what you're willing to hold open, and to talk it through with people who won't necessarily see it your way.
What can Hannah Arendt's friendships — including with people whose politics she found troubling — teach us about sustaining democracy today? If our current political crisis is, at its root, a crisis of friendship, what has eroded our capacity to stay in dialogue across difference? And in an age of mass loneliness and ideological certainty, what would it mean to treat friendship, rather than consensus or moral purity, as the foundation of democratic life?
Berkowitz is founder and academic director of the Hannah Arendt Center for Politics and Humanities at Bard College. In A World We Share: Hannah Arendt and the Power of Friendship in a Broken World, he rethinks politics through Arendt's own life — a Jewish woman who escaped Nazi Germany, lived as an exile in Paris and then New York, and became a bold critic of popular ideas after World War II. People who knew her said she had a special talent for making friends. Berkowitz argues that a politics built solely on being right becomes cruel, coercive and ultimately anti-political.
Come ready to disagree agreeably.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Roger Berkowitz
Sanjay Ruparelia
Read more:
World We Share : Hannah Arendt and the Power of Friendship in A Broken World
***
Sign up for The Friendship Test Workshop
|
5:30 - 6:30 pm
The Kitchen Table |
5:30–6:30 pm & 8:00 – 9:00 pm
Grab a seat and dig into the questions we rarely ask out loud: How has your definition of friendship changed? Can you stay close to someone you disagree with? What makes a friendship last? Inspired by Berkowitz's argument that friendship — not agreement — is the glue of a healthy society, this café is a space to reflect on your own circle with the strangers sitting next to you.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: Centre for Feminist Research Graduate Student Conference: “Assemblia”
location: 519 Kaneff Tower
description:
Date: October 22, 2026
Time: 10:00 AM–4:00 PM
Location: York University, Keele Campus
The Centre for Feminist Research is pleased to announce that we are accepting submissions for our upcoming conference, ASSEMBLIA, taking place on October 22, 2026.
This is the inaugural conference in what we hope will become an annual event organized by graduate students and members of the CFR. It provides an interdisciplinary forum for emerging and independent artists and scholars by bringing together studio practice, criticism and theory, gender studies, and art history.
We welcome academic articles, poetry, short fiction, artworks, and essays. Any questions can be directed towards the Assemblia Graduate Student Leadership Team (Julia and Ame) at CFRfeministfestival@gmail.com
The conference is free and open to graduate students, independent scholars, artists, and interdisciplinary practitioners. Any questions can be directed towards the Assemblia Graduate Student Leadership Team (Julia and Ame) at CFRfeministfestival@gmail.com
Our Objective
Assemblia is organized through a collaborative, non-hierarchical structure grounded in accessibility, shared decision-making, and collective accountability.
Assemblia approaches feminism as a lived practice—often present even when it is not named. Across cultures and histories, feminist resistance has been misrecognized as hysteria, sanctity, deviance, or danger. Assemblia brings together people interested in attending to the language of feminism as acts of care, survival, and uprising.
 
Click HERE  ( https://www.yorku.ca/cfr/cfr-feminist-festival-call-for-volunteers/ )to apply to be a volunteer.
Click HERE  ( https://www.yorku.ca/cfr/assemblia2026-information-submission-guidelines/ )to access the Call for Papers

title: In-Depth Intro to Woodworking Oct 22 [Thursdays - 6 week Intensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
Woodworking at TTLMakerspace

 
 Suitable for beginners, this woodworking course is designed to teach you all that you need to get started in woodworking by learning both traditional, and modern techniques.

 Students will learn valuable hands-on skills working on instructor-lead projects using both hand and power tools.

 Projects are chosen to provide skills development in a natural progression from familiarity with the unique characteristics of wood, to basic essential techniques, to some more advanced topics.

 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course. 

 

 Schedule : 

 Six three-hour weekly classes, Thursdays 10am to 1pm. 

 Outcomes : 

 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 

 
- A complete understanding of the nature and properties of wood 

- Proficiency with traditional woodworking techniques

- Comfort working with chisels, planes, saws

- Proficiency with wood milling techniques

- Comfort with safe operation of power tools

- Familiarity with power planing, joiner, drill press, router and table saw 

- Dressing and laminating wood 

- Experience following project plans 

- Familiarity with joinery 

- Wood finishing, various treatments 

 
  Following this course, you'll be certified to use the woodshop. And you'll be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing knowledge on our Discord community.

 Certifications for all courses are valid for one year from the time that they are issued, and can be renewed at no cost with your active monthly membership within 3 months of their expiry. Certification renewal requires booking with an instructor, is conducted at the makerspace, and helps you keep your skills current. 

Useful for: furniture, cabinets, organisers, cutting-boards
