title: Colour & Atmosphere
description:
Join us for an online special career series with the
2026 Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence
, Elly MacKay! In this series, Elly will share insights into building a career in children’s book illustration, covering topics such as the journey to working as an illustrator, an overview of classic children’s books, portfolios, and colour. Details about each session follow:
Thursday, October 8, 7pm:
Becoming an Illustrator
Elly MacKay shares her early and current work, her career path, and her process for creating miniature 3D worlds. Her talk also covers developing your style, illustration trends, and how to stand out.
Thursday, October 15, 7pm: Looking at Picture Books
Elly MacKay gives an overview of famous picture books, the various styles, what works, and how they’ve changed over the years. She looks at cover design, structure, page turns, and how visual storytelling and words work together.
Thursday, October 22, 7pm: From Portfolio to Book
Elly MacKay discusses portfolios and what to include, as well as working with agents and publishers. She also looks at what goes into creating your first picture book.
Thursday, October 29, 7pm: Colour and Atmosphere
Elly MacKay considers colour in picture books—how it can be used to strengthen a message, or to alter the mood. She looks at how illustrators have used colour in unconventional ways in their books.
Workshops will be recorded and available for replay through Zoom until October 31, 2026.
About Elly MacKay
Elly MacKay is a children’s book author and illustrator and a paper artist. She studied printmaking and illustration at NSCAD University in Halifax and University of Canterbury in Christchurch. Elly creates miniature worlds with drawing, painting and cutting, and photographs them for illustrations in children’s books. She has more than 20 books published in Canada and the US, including The Enchanted Symphony by Julie Andrews and Emma Walton Hamilton, I Am a Meadow Mermaid and The Secret Fawn by Kallie George. Elly is both author and illustrator of Frostfire, In the Clouds and Red Sky at Night and others. She lives with her family in Owen Sound, Ontario.
About the Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence Program
The
Illustrator in Residence
program honours the memory of illustrator Joanne Fitzgerald (1956-2011), and is a joint program of IBBY Canada, Toronto Public Library, and the Young Family.

title: Jesse Wente: Tough Lies
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space
description:
Award-winning author Jesse Wente shares his highly-anticipated new book exploring how we can heal from colonialism.
In Tough Lies, Wente explores his own healing path and how it informs what he sees as necessary for reconciliation between Nations, asking us to consider several pressing questions.
What does healing from colonialism look like for First Nations? What about non-Indigenous people? What are the barriers to this healing, and what can we do to move past them?
Through a lens of healing and anti-colonial thought, Wente examines his reaction to incidents that have hit close to home, chronicling his personal journey and what it has taught him about the present and future of reconciliation in Canada.
Jesse Wente speaks with professor Kim Anderson about Tough Lies and the path for healing between Nations.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Magnifica Humanitas: Choosing Humanity in the AI Revolution
description:
— A Symposium on Putting Pope Leo’s “AI Encyclical” into Practice 







October 30-31, 2026 (Fri/Sat), 10:30am – 5:00pm 



Father Madden Hall (in Carr Hall, 100 St. Joseph St) 



Free admission / Lunch included: Register now 



How do we maintain our humanity and agency in a world that increasingly revolves around AI? 



From workplaces to social media feeds, from breakthroughs in healthcare research to that question you Googled last night, AI seems to be permeating every aspect of our lives. But as the ways we think, work, live, and act are being rapidly transformed, how do we protect and nurture those parts of our humanity that matter most—our dignity, our agency, our creativity and moral commitments? 



Join us as we discern our stakes in the current AI revolution through the lens of Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo’s “AI encyclical.” Through two days of panels, discussions, and workshops, we will explore how the Pope uses Catholic social teaching to engage with the structural realities of AI, and consider our own practical responses to his call to prioritise human dignity over unrestricted AI development. 



By asking practical questions about AI in light of Magnifica Humanitas, this symposium will help us engage critically and faithfully with changing technologies in our own lives, work, and service to the world. Whether you are new to the conversation and wanting to learn more or are already confronting pressing issues around AI, we welcome you to join us in this timely dialogue on navigating the emerging AI frontier. 



__________ 



Magnifica Humanitas Online Reading Group 



Monday evenings (7-8pm) from Sep. 14-Oct. 19 



UPDATE: sign-ups for the reading group have now closed. 



Are you interested in Pope Leo’s “AI encyclical,” but daunted by the thought of reading it alone? Have you been tempted to ask ChatGPT for a summary? Join us instead for this virtual reading group and explore the encyclical in conversation with others. Over 6 weekly sessions, Dr. Ren Ito will facilitate discussions of each chapter of Magnifica Humanitas. Participants will build an understanding of the encyclical’s key arguments, and will learn to engage with current issues of new technology through the lens of Catholic social teaching. 



Participants will also have the opportunity to present reflections on and takeaways from the encyclical during a session of our October 30-31 Magnifica Humanitas symposium.

title: Indigenous Medicine Workshop: Cedar Salve

description:

Tanya Gluvakov is a mixed Mohawk woman from Toronto with family and "roots" from Six Nations of the Grand River in Oshweken, Ontario. The founder of Roots and Raven, Tanya is a herbalist, a mom, a teacher, and auntie, who teaches several workshops about medicines from the land and how connecting with them helps us find our way. She also leads several projects that bring the resurgence of medicines and accessibility to urban communities

title: Internet Horror Classics on Film: Demonlover
description:
In this second instalment of Toronto Public Library's virtual series Internet Horror Classics on Film, critic Saffron Maeve and director Pascal Plante discuss Demonlover, the 2002 French neo-noir thriller film directed by Olivier Assayas. Exploring the damaging effects of media and modern desensitization to violence, the film has gained a cult-following in recent years.
About this event's guests:
Saffron Maeve
is a Toronto-based critic, film curator, and researcher. A regular contributor to The Globe and Mail, her writing has also appeared in numerous publications.
Pascal Plante
is a Canadian film director and screenwriter from Quebec, whose debut feature film, Fake Tattoos, premiered in 2017. His second film, Nadia, Butterfly, premiered in 2020 in the official selection of the Cannes Film Festival. His third feature film, Red Rooms, garnered widespread critical acclaim.
Adam Nayman
is a critic, teacher, and author, whose books include critical surveys of the Coen Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and most recently, in Mind Games, the filmmaker David Fincher. He is a regular contributor to The Ringer, a lecturer at the University of Toronto's Cinema Studies Institute, and he has written on film for The New Yorker and The New York Times.

title: Native Plant Series: Collecting Native Seed
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for an engaging workshop where you’ll learn about biodiversity, native plants and how to enhance your garden!
Nature needs your help and it’s as simple as using native plants in your garden! Biodiversity, the variety of all living things necessary to sustain life, is declining because of climate change, habitat loss from increasing urbanization and agricultural practices. Come understand the importance of native plants, how to grow them to welcome pollinators and enhance the beauty of your garden.
 
Session 1: Collecting Native Seed
Discover a simple and rewarding way to grow your garden while supporting plant diversity! Join us for an engaging workshop on ethical seed collecting, where you’ll learn best practices for gathering and caring for seeds. We’ll head out into the Toronto Botanical Garden for a guided session collecting a limited amount of seed, then return indoors to explore seed cleaning and storage techniques. You will keep the seed you collect. To help you get started, the Toronto Master Gardeners will also share a limited selection of seeds collected earlier in the year.
 
Saturday, October 31, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m.
Registration: Public $20, TBG Members $15 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Tina Cesaroni and Pat Concessi
Toronto Master Gardeners Tina and Pat are transitioning their home gardens to more natural environments, which includes adding native plants, shrubs and trees. They collect seed each fall and grow native plants from seed for their own gardens and to share with their communities.
 
About Toronto Master Gardeners
Toronto Master Gardeners (TMG) is a volunteer not-for-profit organization that shares current, science-based horticultural information with the gardening public through various channels, including in person, in print, through the media, and online. Our committed volunteers support and inspire the community, and continually update the sound knowledge required to help them. Learn more and ask your questions Toronto Master Gardeners – Helping Gardeners.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Botanical Drypoint Printmaking
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled afternoon of drypoint printmaking!
In this hands-on workshop, you’ll be creating an edition of 5 original prints using a printmaking technique called drypoint. This medium is similar to etching, but it’s far safer because no dangerous acids are involved. Rembrandt is a well known Old Master who excelled at both drypoint and etching.
 
For botanical subject matter, please bring sketches and line drawings for inspiration and reference. The image needs to measure 4×6 inches; you’ll learn how to incise the image onto a printing plate using a drypoint needle. If you’re stuck for ideas on what to create, there will be pressed leaves available which make lovely subjects. You’ll also learn how to ink the plate and work with an old-fashioned mechanical printing press.
 
Drypoint gets messy, so please wear old clothes or bring an apron. Also, please bring a pair of dishwashing gloves.
 
Saturday, October 31, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $75, TBG Members $65 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature-focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.

title: Real Ghosts: A Hallowe'en Exclusive
location: Mimico Centennial, Auditorium
description:
Putting the ‘boo’ in ‘book’, author Peter Roe (
Haunted Town Halls
,
The Complete Paranormal  Investigation Handbook
) will manifest at the Mimico Centennial Library, for an exclusive Hallowe’en visit Saturday, October 31st, at 2:30 pm sharing
The Searcher Group’
s true-life discoveries from the field of ghost investigation.
Over 30 years before reality TV inspired thousands of thrill-seeking groups worldwide,
The Searcher Group
– Canada’s oldest, most reputable and accomplished paranormal research team – celebrates its 47
th
Anniversary in 2026!
Mixing chills, a deep appreciation of Ontario’s vanishing heritage and thought-provoking discussion with a dash of humour, this popular presentation returns discussing tools-of-the-trade, original theory on life-after-life phenomena and rarely-seen ghost photos!
Skeptics and the curious alike are all welcome to attend this judgment-free Hallowe’en event. Bring your own inquiries and experiences to a Q&A following the hour-long talk!
For early attendees eager to secure a seat, a Pre-Show video will start at 2:00 pm, to set the mood.
Copies of
Haunted Town Halls
($20) and/or
The Complete Paranormal Investigation Handbook
($30) will be available for sale and signing with no obligation to purchase. Cash only, please.
*Please Note: Video recordings of this presentation are not permitted, thank you.
About the Presenter
As Assistant Director of The Searcher Group (TSG), Peter Roe also serves as Director of TSG subdivision, Mortal Coil Paranormal (MCP), serving the Greater Toronto Area and southwestern Ontario.
When he is not spearheading investigations and conducting research, he is actively promoting TSG’s pro bono services, publicly presenting field discoveries and advocating against Ontario’s rapidly vanishing heritage.
Peter has appeared in a testimonial capacity over two seasons of the Travel Channel’s Fear the Woods (aka Evil Encounters on T+E Channel), been interviewed by CBC Radio and the Paranormal UK Network, and has earned worldwide notoriety with the release of his first nonfiction publication, Haunted Town Halls (Quagmire Press), in 2018.
Peter is co-author of
The Complete Paranormal Investigation Handbook
with Searcher Group founder Richard Palmisano – released August 18, 2025 through Llewellyn Worldwide.
About The Searcher Group
Founded in 1979 by Richard Palmisano, The Searcher Group (TSG) is Canada’s leading team of investigators, researchers and theorists. The Searcher Group’s mission includes investigating alleged paranormal activity, developing and conducting experiments for the advancement of parapsychology, and researching and developing new technologies and theoretic models.
Boasting an ironclad reputation for safety, confidentiality and credibility over the course of 47 years, TSG has had the privilege of working with government officials and operators of recognized, historic public sites alike, in its ongoing quest to discover and contribute answers to humankind’s most enduring questions pertaining to life-after-life and ghost phenomena.
Applying his 37-year career in law enforcement, security and surveillance in the field, Richard is also the author of five nonfiction publications documenting the team’s most harrowing and informative cases, including
Overshadows
(2003),
Journeys into the Unknown
(2006),
Ghosts
(2009),
Ghosts of the Canadian National Exhibition
(2011) and
Meeting Place of the Dead
(2014), all available through Dundurn Press. He has co-authored an advanced paranormal investigation manual with TSG Assistant Director Peter Roe, titled The Complete Paranormal Investigation Handbook released August 18, 2025 through Llewellyn Worldwide.
Richard and his books have been featured on television, radio and internet podcasts worldwide, including A Haunting (Season 1, Discovery Channel), Northern Mysteries, Portal into the Unknown, CBC Radio, Breakfast Television, Darkness Radio, and Crash Course in Awesome, among many others.
The Searcher Group featured as the cover story of the United Church Observer (now
Broadview
) in October 2016* and soon after appeared in Reader’s Digest (April 2017)

title: 🇨🇦Japanese and English Language Exchange  (Page for everyone)
description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は5頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

***Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events***

*Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate*

RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List:
Members can join the waiting-list even if an event is full. When a spot becomes available, we will move you to the going-list.

Going List:

title: 🎃 Halloween Special: Meet New People | + 50+ Board Games | 21–45
description:
Toronto 20's to 50's Singles Social (4000+)
🎃 Looking for a fun way to meet new people in Toronto this Halloween?

You could walk into a room full of strangers and hope a conversation happens… or you could let us make the first step easy.

Join us for a Halloween Special at Stout Irish Pub, where Fast Friends takes the guesswork out of making new connections.

Through relaxed, professionally hosted conversations, rotations and Halloween-themed connection rounds, you'll meet 20+ people, discover common interests and have plenty of reasons to laugh and chat along the way.

🎃 Costumes are welcome but completely optional — come dressed up, add a little Halloween flair, or simply come as you are.

And the best part? The evening doesn't stop when the hosted rounds do.
Afterwards, stick around at Stout for 50+ board games, drinks and more time to socialise with the people you've just met. 🎲🍻

Book Early & Save: [https://toronto31stoct.eventbrite.co.uk](https://toronto31stoct.eventbrite.co.uk)
Early Bird: CAD $10 \| Regular: CAD $15 \| Door: CAD $20 cash

Advance tickets help us plan the right space and group size and ensure a well-organised experience for everyone.

🤝 What to Expect
7:00 PM — Welcome & Drinks
Meet your host, Kruttika, grab a drink and settle in.
Coming alone? You're in good company. Many of our guests arrive solo, and our host will help you get comfortable, make introductions and get the evening started.

7:30–8:30 PM — Hosted Fast Friends
This is where the evening really gets going.
You'll have a series of short, guided conversations, moving around the group so you get the chance to meet a variety of people rather than spending the whole evening talking to just one person.
No need to walk up to strangers and figure out what to say — we've created the structure for you.

🎃 Halloween-Themed Connection Rounds
Alongside the regular Fast Friends conversations, we'll add some Halloween-inspired themed rounds with fun prompts and challenges designed to get people laughing, talking and discovering what they have in common.
Expect a few seasonal twists — nothing complicated, just an easy way to make the conversations even more fun.

🎲 8:30 PM onwards — 50+ Board Games & Socialising
Don't feel like heading home after the hosted rounds?
Stay and keep the evening going at Stout.
With 50+ board games available, you can join a game with people you've met, grab another drink, continue a conversation or simply mingle and see where the evening takes you.
You don't need to be a serious gamer — the games are simply another easy way to keep people interacting.

🍻 And if you're staying later, Stout's After Dark Special runs from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.

❤️ Why This Event?
✔️ Halloween Special 🎃
✔️ Meet 25+ new people in one evening
✔️ Professionally hosted conversations and rotations
✔️ Halloween-themed connection rounds
✔️ Costumes welcome — but completely optional
✔️ 50+ board games at Stout 🎲
✔️ Reserved area for our group
✔️ Easy-to-reach Toronto location
✔️ Relaxed Irish-pub atmosphere
✔️ Most guests attend solo
✔️ Meet members from across our Toronto social communities
✔️ Ages 25–45
✔️ Friendship-focused — not a dating event

👥 Who Should Come?
Whether you've recently moved to Toronto, have lived here for years, work from home and want a bigger social circle, or simply feel like meeting some different people — you're welcome.
You don't need to know anyone beforehand.
Come by yourself, bring a friend, wear a costume or don't — the evening is designed to make it easy to get involved and start connecting.

💳 Why Book in Advance?
Your ticket helps us plan the right space, manage the group size and create a comfortable experience for everyone.
Online tickets are also cheaper than paying at the door.

🌍 About Fast Friends
For over 10 years, Fast Friends has been helping people make genuine connections through professionally hosted social events in 30+ cities around the world.
Our goal is simple: make meeting new people easier, more relaxed and more enjoyable.
Come solo. We’ll guide the experience. You make the connections. ❤️

title: AI for Small Business and Entrepreneurs
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
You've got the business idea. Now come the thousand questions: who's my customer, what's the market, how do I pitch this?
In this class, you'll use AI as a research and planning partner for small business. We'll practice together on a sample business, turning rough ideas into business plans, digging into markets, drafting customer-discovery questions, and building useful low-maintenance automation. The most valuable thing you'll get is usually a better question to be tested in the real world. Whether you're starting or growing, you'll leave with an experiment you can run on your own business this week.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

title: Python Essentials 1
location: Brookbanks, Lower Level Auditorium
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact
networkingacademy@tpl.ca

title: Botanical Leaf Painting Workshop: 4-sessions
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a four-week introduction course and learn the basics of botanical leaf painting!
Learn how to paint a realistic oak leaf using watercolour paint and colour pencil. Participants will learn how to mix and layer colour washes in order to create an image that has depth and feels true to life. Our instructor will guide each stage of the process through group demonstrations and provide individual attention. Attendees will observe and paint from actual pressed oak leaves (we will not be copying photos).
 
Beginners welcome. All art materials will be provided.
 
Tuesdays, November 3 through 24, 1 to 3 p.m. (four sessions)
Public $125, TBG Members $110 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine-inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing, and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Let's Make a Graphic Novel! Workshop with Tory Woollcott
location: High Park, Program Room
description:
Led by the professional cartoonist, Tory Woollcott, this workshop teaches the fundamentals of story outlining and narrative structure as it applies to comics & graphic novels, prose, or even video games! Drop in, limited spots.
Tory Woollcott is a Toronto-based author, illustrator, designer, and educator whose work spans graphic novels, science comics, audio dramas, podcasts, and kids' books. She is the author of Science Comics: The Brain: The Ultimate Thinking Machine (First Second Books), a vibrant and accessible exploration of neuroscience, illustrated by Alex Graudins. Her debut graphic novel, Mirror Mind, is a celebrated autobiography that recounts her experiences growing up with dyslexia. Other notable works include the audio drama Awake with Sparklermonthly, the travel diary Toronto to Tuscany (created in collaboration with Kean Soo), and two successful Kickstarter campaigns: the Tessera Oracle and its follow-up, the Trine Oracle.

title: Jennifer Botterill & Cassie Campbell-Pascall: Game Changers
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Trailblazing hockey players Jennifer Botterill and Cassie Campbell-Pascall share their new memoirs.
Botterill broke barriers as the youngest player on Team Canada at the first Olympics for women’s ice hockey, while Campbell-Pascall set records as the longest-serving captain in Canadian hockey history—and the first of any gender to lead the country to two Olympic gold medals.
Since their Hall of Fame playing careers, both have remained at the very top their game as sought-after broadcasters and advocates for athletes. Now, in their memoirs Why Not You and Just a Girl, these two titans of hockey invite us into their worlds like never before.
Jennifer Botterill and Cassie Campbell-Pascall speak with sportscaster Ailish Forfar about their new memoirs, taking a look back on their decorated hockey careers and toward a brighter future for all who play the game.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Recovery College: YU & Balance Week 3 | Making meaningful connections: Staying present in conversations
location: Markham Campus (MK2050)
description:
This session will be offered in person at York University’s Markham Campus and is open to students from all York University campuses.
Building connections can sometimes feel exciting, awkward or even a little intimidating.
In this week’s session of YU & Balance, we will focus on helping students feel more comfortable meeting new people, strengthening the relationships they already have and recognizing what makes a connection healthy and supportive.
Students will explore ways to:

Manage social anxiety
Build confidence in social settings
Think intentionally about who they can turn to for support.

This session is part of a 6-week Recovery College series. For each session attended, participants will receive $5 on their YU-card. To receive the gift card, you must attend the full session (approximately 45–60 minutes). Unfortunately, we’re not able to provide gift cards for partial attendance. Gift cards will be emailed after the session to the same email address used to register and join the session.
Space is limited, and registration is offered on a first-come, first-served basis. If the session is full and you’d like to be added to the waitlist, please email hstacey@yorku.ca ( mailto:hstacey@yorku.ca ). We’ll reach out if a spot becomes available. If you’re registered but can no longer attend, please let us know as soon as you can so we can offer your spot to another student.
Register for Making meaningful connections: Staying present in conversations ( https://forms.students.yorku.ca/view.php?id=499412 )
ics_categories: Faculty of Liberal Arts & Professional Studies

Why Toronto plans for nuclear emergencies
What nuclear emergency planning zones mean
How emergency alerts and official information would be shared

title: Bring Your Problem: Can AI Help?

description:
Do you have a recurring problem you think AI might help with? A thing you keep doing by hand that feels like it should be easier? Bring it. If you don't have one, come help your neighbours with theirs.
In this interactive class, you'll learn a simple seven-step way to think about problems: what's annoying you, what you've tried, what AI could actually do, and where it would fail. We'll gather real problems from the room, sort them into groups, and map out what's worth solving with AI, and what's better solved without it. We'll also talk honestly about what an AI fix costs: your money, your time, and sometimes your private information. The problems AI could help with most are often the most personal, and the most personal ones are worth the most care.

description:
Learn how to create stunning arrangements using natural materials!
Each week a different natural material – wood, branches, foliage, and fruit and vegetables – will take centre stage. We will study their forms and shapes, textures, sizes, colouring and characteristics to discover the new and exciting ways they can be used. Join us on this journey of discovery.

About Margaret Taylor
For more than 15 years, Margaret’s passion for flowers has led her to exhibit, judge, demonstrate and teach floral design in Canada and abroad. A recipient of many awards, Margaret’s accolades include two Canada Blooms’ Founder’s Gold Cups for Best in Show. Margaret has also won Best in Show on three occasions at the provincial triennial show and as a result, has been chosen to represent Canada in two world shows. It was her greatest honour to exhibit for Canada both in Boston and in India.
 
Margaret is currently a floral design judge accredited by the Garden Clubs of Ontario, a horticultural judge accredited by the Royal Botanical Gardens and a rose judge accredited by the Canadian Rose Society. Margaret is also a Sogetsu Ikebana teacher and exhibitor. Much lauded for her design acumen by the horticultural community, she is a past president of the Garden Club of Toronto and is a coordinator of floral design studies at Toronto Botanical Garden.

title: A Matter of Feeling: Chinese Ceramics Through the Senses
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
A Matter of Feeling: Chinese Ceramics Through the Senses            
                                    
                                
                        
                                                
                                                        Get Tickets                        
                                            
                
                    
    



	

    
         
    




	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Thursday November 5, 2026
12:00 pm – 1:00 pm ET
Online via Zoom 
Part of the Gardiner Signature Lecture Series
The Ann Walker Bell Lecture 
Speaker: Dr. Laura Vigo, Curator of Asian Art and Archaeology, Montreal Museum of Fine Arts 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    The Duran Duran song “A Matter of Feeling” seemed to define an era. Strangely enough, it offers an unexpectedly bittersweet point of departure for a talk that, in its own way, circles back in time. In this online lecture, Dr. Laura Vigo will turn to the origins of the Chinese ceramic collection at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts (MMFA) and the enduring feelings these objects have inspired in those who handled them—potters, users, collectors, and curators alike. She will also consider how attending to these sensory encounters might shift the way we engage with them today. The objects’ appeal has never been simply about beauty or romance. Rather, there is a profound sensuality to ceramics: the sensation of touch, the scent of fired clay, the sound of porcelain when gently struck, and, above all, the pleasure of looking closely. 
These perceptual connotations shaped the collecting practices of figures such as Sir William Van Horne and the museum’s remarkably charismatic first volunteer curator, Cleveland Morgan. Their tales, and the objects they left behind, remind us that collecting ceramics has always been about more than acquiring beautiful commodities. It was, and still is, about cultivating the senses and the imagination, and about bridging past and present through the intimate experience of handling and looking.

                    About the Speaker
                    
                
                
                    Laura Vigo
                    
                
                
                    Laura Vigo is Curator of Asian Art and Archaeology at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts (MMFA) and an invited curator at the Museum of Asian Art in Turin (MAO), where she co-curated several recent exhibitions and is currently preparing the new galleries dedicated to Chinese material culture. 
At the MMFA, she has developed major exhibitions and collection displays, including the N. Kapany Gallery for Sikh Art, the Asian collections in the Arts of One World wing, and the recent exhibition Tōkaidō: Dreamscapes by Andō Hiroshige. Her previous projects include Egyptian Mummies, Pompeii, and The Warrior Emperor and China’s Terracotta Army, as well as exhibitions exploring Japanese ceramics, artistic diversity, and the museum’s collections. 
Vigo holds a PhD in Chinese Archaeology from SOAS, University of London, and has worked across museums, galleries, and auction houses in Italy, the UK, and Canada. Her interests span from the histories of collecting, the Western construction of Asian art, transcultural narratives, to sensory studies, and digital mediation. She also teaches at the Université de Montréal. 
Her work often brings together museum collections, contemporary artistic practices, and questions about how we encounter objects—and how museums can create new ways of seeing, sensing, and understanding them.

title: Nov 5 - Visual AI Agriculture Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics at the intersection of agriculture and AI.

**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 05, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/visual-ai-agriculture-meetup-november-5-2026)**

Talks will include:

**U-Net Framework for Micro-Scale Surface Damage Segmentation in High-Resolution Soybean Seed Imagery**

Accurate detection of surface-level seed damage is critical for soybean seed quality assurance, yet automated micro-scale damage detection in high-resolution imagery remains an open challenge due to extreme spatial variability in damage scale, severe class imbalance across damage types, and the computational demands of processing ultra-high resolution agricultural imagery at scale. This research addresses the semantic segmentation of fine-grained soybean seed surface defects, such as wrinkles, dark spots, and general surface damage, in 6048 × 4024 pixel images where target damages can be as small as 18 × 18 pixels, using an augmented dataset of 77,000 individual seed images.

To overcome the difficulties of micro-scale detection, spatial sparsity, and class confusion, we propose a two-stage training and dual model inference framework built on an optimized U-Net architecture with a ResNet34 encoder. In the first stage, a damage specialist model is trained using weighted loss functions and a class-balanced approach that prioritizes damage classes.

In the second stage, transfer learning is applied to initialize a healthy seed specialist model from Stage 1 weights, with rebalanced class weights and tile probabilities that identify healthy seeds. During inference, a confidence-gated damage filter suppresses low-confidence predictions, and healthy seed labels are assigned only when the specialist model's confidence exceeds that of the damage model.

The two specialist models achieve validation accuracies of 94% and 98.53%, respectively, and the combined inference system successfully detects and localizes all three damage categories across unseen test images under conditions of extreme spatial variability and class imbalance. Qualitative evaluation confirms close alignment of predicted boundaries with ground truth annotations across all damage types, including dark spots.

These results demonstrate that confidence-gated dual model inference can reduce class confusion in imbalanced micro-scale segmentation, advancing the feasibility of fine-grained automated seed quality inspection at the scale.

*About the Speaker*

[Saurav Upadhyaya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sauravupadhyaya/) is an AI/ML researcher with a Master's degree in Computer Science, whose work spans agricultural AI, conversational systems, and public health, consistently translating advanced technology into tangible real-world impact.

**From camera to drone: wildfire detection and integration at the edge**

Wildfires are getting larger and more expensive every year. But caught early, a fire is a small job for a small team; caught late, nothing stops it. The cameras to catch them are already installed, so the work is not necessary more sensors but making the ones we have act.

This talk walks the whole chain: a small vision model running on the camera that flags smoke, an integration layer that scores the alert against terrain, weather and history to decide whether it matters, and a drone dispatched to confirm before anyone commits a crew. We will cover what has to run at the edge and why, how small the model can get before it stops seeing smoke, and what it takes to trust a detection nobody has looked at yet.

*About the Speaker*

[Maxime Carriere](https://voxel51.com/events/www.linkedin.com/in/maxime-carriere-871756161) is co-founder of Kernwerk in Berlin, where he works on compressing AI models to run on cheap embedded hardware.

**5,000 Flights to Answer One Question: Can a Drone Sample as Well as a Human?**

Environmental testing still begins with a person walking onto a site with a shovel. We built a system that turns a plain-language brief into a sampling campaign, flies it, and returns soil, water and vegetation samples with GPS, timestamps and chain of custody intact: 5,000 flights, roughly 9,000 miles and 570 flight hours over a 185-acre site in Roatan, much of it under canopy where GPS degrades and clearances are tight.

I will walk through the vision and planning stack, including multispectral and thermal canopy sensing, terrain and land-cover mapping, and the constraint solver that clears a route against airspace and battery budget before anything leaves the ground. Then the harder problem: evidentiary comparability.

A drone-collected result means nothing to a regulator unless it agrees with a hand-collected split under the same method, so I will show the dual-collection protocol we designed to test exactly that. I will close on why calibrated uncertainty and knowing when a model should refuse to answer matter more than raw accuracy once the output lands in a regulatory filing.

*About the Speaker*

[Rohan Talwadia](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rohantalwadia/) is co-founder and CTO of LabGPT, which automates environmental field sampling using drones and edge analysis, with results returned through ISO/IEC 17025-accredited partner laboratories.

title: Continental Philosophy Research Group (Thimo Heisenberg, Rice University)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Continental Philosophy Research Interest Group welcomes guest speaker Thimo Heisenberg, an associate professor in the Department of Philosophy at Rice University. 
Professor Heisenberg is a specialist in 19th and 20th century German Philosophy. Having earned his PhD from Columbia in 2019, his work has appeared in journals such as the British Journal of the History of Philosophy, the European Journal of Philosophy, Inquiry, and the Journal of the American Philosophical Association, as well as in many edited collections and anthologies. He was a Fulbright Scholar, and has received fellowships from the Alexander-von-Humboldt Foundation, the German National Academic Foundation, the Max Weber Program and from Columbia University. His book, The Economy in German Idealism, is under contract with Oxford University Press. 
Talk Title
The Dream Allegory in Schelling’s Denkmal 
Talk Abstract
The final section of Schelling’s 1812 Denkmal is its most unusual. While the rest of the text had presented a philosophical critique of Jacobi and Jacobianism, this third part offers a satirical Dream Allegory showing a fictional Jacobi on an absurd journey. Because of this unconventional form, commentators have largely avoided this part of the text or dismissed it as unserious. Yet, even though this is rarely noted, Schelling himself insists on the allegory’s importance: telling us that it is only here that his critique of Jacobi finds “proper completion” (AA I 18, 188) and even that it does the “best work” (AA I 18, 144). In this regard, unless we want to dismiss these remarks too, we need to attend to the allegory and its role in Schelling’s argument. This is what I will do in this talk. I will argue that, rightly interpreted, the allegory does indeed bring Schelling’s critique of Jacobi to completion and culmination:  rounding out Schelling’s well-known critique of Jacobi’s principles with a much less well-known (but motivationally even more powerful) critique of the life those principles lead us to live, if we adopt them as our own.

description:
Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space!

title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Forest Bathing at the Garden
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Connect with nature and join us for a guided forest therapy walk!
Rekindle your relationship with nature this fall through a guided outdoor forest bathing walk with certified forest therapy guide Laura Bincik. At a slow pace and in community with other participants and the environment, you will be guided by a series of invitations throughout the experience to awaken your senses and intentionally connect with nature in the present moment.
 
We will gather briefly indoors to prepare for the walk and consider the origin of forest bathing, as well as some of the benefits of the practice. When we venture into the Toronto Botanical Gardens and surrounding ravine, we will cover a loop of approximately 1.5 km on paved pathways, lawns and bare ground, at times encountering uneven terrain, inclines and declines. We will be strolling, standing and sitting (if you wish to). Your comfort and safety are most important!
 
As this program occurs rain or shine, please dress for the weather and wear sturdy, closed-toed footwear. Long pants and shirt sleeves will help to protect against insect bites. You may wish to bring a water bottle, sunhat/glasses, walking poles and/or a folding stool or sitting/kneeling pad.
 
As the walk ends, we will gather and partake in a seasonal tea, snacks and taste honey harvested at Toronto Botanical Garden.
 
In the event of severe weather or environmental conditions, TBG staff will make alternative arrangements to the program.
 
Washrooms are available onsite.
 
The program is suited for adults 18+. All participants must sign a liability waiver at the start of the program.
 
Service pets welcome but we ask that you leave your pets at home during this program.
 
Friday, November 6, 1 to 3 p.m.
Public $35, TBG Members $30 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Laura Bincik
Laura Bincik is a certified forest therapy guide with the Association of Nature and Forest Therapy. Following a career that straddled health care and education, Laura discovered that her lifelong sense of awe for the natural world could be enriched and shared with others to enhance wellbeing. Laura feels a connection to the land and the wonder of being in nature from countless hours spent exploring Toronto ravines in all seasons. An active member of Nature and Forest Therapy Canada, Laura follows the growing research on the mental and physical health benefits of forest bathing and is expanding her practice by connecting with local, national and international leaders in the field.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.

Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. Paul Bloom (Psychology, University of Toronto)

title: Learn to Spin Your Own Yarn- November
location: Bistitchual, 266 Jane St, Toronto, ON M6S 3Z2
description: This listing is for a three session Beginner Spinning Course. The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Saturday November 7th, 14, 21st from 12:30pm - 2:00pm Learn how to transform fibre into yarn with our drop spindle class! In this class you will learn how to use a drop spindle to spin starting with woolly fibre and ending with a completed, ready to use yarn. You will learn how to spin a single ply yarn, how to spin a 2-ply yarn using the Andean Plying method, and how to chain ply for a 3-ply yarn over three classes. Drop spindles must be brought by students or purchased in store. 50g of fibre provided in two different colours. Please note that classes will only proceed if we have a minimum of two attendees . location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:

Imagine: There is a slight nip in the air, the snow-covered landscape, the crunching of snow beneath your feet. Millean Kung will guide participants through making a 6” by 6” glass plate. You will learn how to cut glass and how to piece them together to create your winter scene. Participants will also learn about the types of glass, the tools involved, and techniques used.
 
All materials will be provided. This course welcomes beginners.

About Millean Kung
Born and raised in Toronto, Millean discovered pottery and glass art more than 10 years ago. Currently, she is a member of the of the Potter’s Studios in Scarborough and is involved in the Small Business Arts Mentorship Program at Glasstronomy Studios in Markham. Since retiring from education, Millean has devoted her time to her pottery and glass art. She is the sole proprietor of her business, “1 in a Millean,” and participates in a number of arts and crafts shows.
 
Millean also loves to garden and is a member and a volunteer at the Toronto Botanical Garden. To keep her schedule busy she enjoys cooking and baking.

title: Laser for Artists - Nov 7 [Saturdays 6 week comprehensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
In this course at TTLMakerspace, you will go from beginner to practical working knowledge of designing and modelling in 2D and 3D, and the operation of a laser for etching and cutting a variety of materials. 

 Starting with desktop versions of lasers you’ll work your way through lessons and projects up to the industrial ThunderLaser cutter. 

 Outcomes: 

 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 

 
- A complete understanding of the steps needed to go from concept to completed project 

- Familiarity with the properties of a variety of materials - woods, plastics, textiles 

- Experience and comprehension of the most important principles of CAD modelling for constructing with laser cut parts 

- Setting speeds and power levels 

- Creating a design environment and workflow 

- Full understanding of the most common etching and cutting operations 

- Experience creating tool paths with Lightburn software 

- Setting up materials and performing operations 

- Machine maintenance and Safety 

 
 Schedule: 6 lessons, Saturdays, 2pm-5pm 

 Following this course, you’ll be certified to use desktop lasers, and book time with the industrial laser at TTLMakerspace (with your membership). You will also be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing Laser knowledge on our Discord community. 

 Useful for : signs, gifts, personalising anything, stamp-making, organiser, decorative items, lanterns 

 Want to get notified next time classes are posted? 

 Join our mailing list!

title: Cable Class - November
location: Bistitchual, 266 Jane St, Toronto, ON M6S 3Z2
description: This listing is for a one session Cable Class. The class will be held in person at Bistitchual on Saturday November 7 from 2:30pm-4:30pm Have you been fantasizing about the cable sweater of your dreams? Take a step towards making that dream a reality with our Cables Class and learn the secrets of the deceptively simple yet hugely impactful cable knitting technique. In this class you will learn cable basics which will allow you to tackle any cable project. Students will work through a small pattern that exemplifies cable techniques. title: 🇨🇦Japanese and English Language Exchange  (Page for everyone)
description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は5頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

***Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events***

*Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate*

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List:
Members can join the waiting-list even if an event is full. When a spot becomes available, we will move you to the going-list.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

Group Instagram -
@tjex.ca

Feel free to follow us!

title: Fall Hiking Glen Major Forest/Brock Tract 13 km 9 AM START
description: Glen Major Forest/Brock Tract Loop The Glen Major Forest is more than 3700 acres of land located on the Oak Ridges Moraine in the headwaters of the Duffins Creek Watershed. This area consists of mixed coniferous/ deciduous forests and a gravel pit once operated in the Glen Major site and is currently being restored. The remainder of the property complex was previously used for agriculture and contains a variety of habitat including forest, meadows and wetlands. Old farm roads and farm building foundations are still visible. This hike has lots of elevation changes and I think that most hikers will find the forest quite beautiful but strenuous. It is a hike worth doing. Distance: 13 km Route:...

title: Immersion Festival
location: Betty Oliphant Theatre, 404 Jarvis St, Toronto, ON
description: Join us for a celebration of Canadian cultural life for audiences and a sought-after performance and networking opportunity for renowned and aspiring artists, with three distinct stage performances, twelve workshops, a dance education roundtable, and community gatherings. Performances and workshops are open to all! Enjoy The Vanguard Presentation includes commissioned works by Katlyn Addison and Tanya Charles, Travis Knights and Divine Brown, and Nubian Néné. The National Presentation features Ebnflōh Dance Company, Lua Shayenne Dance Company, and N.A.P.P.Y. Dance, while the Next Gen showcase highlights emerging Black youth artists. Our workshops for youth, beginners, and professionals are led by Kwasi Obeng-Adjei, Reequal Smith, Natasha Powell, and Isaac Gasangwa, exploring diverse Black and diasporic movement practices. Three gathering events bring together presenters, artists, and academics to connect, exchange ideas, and celebrate Black dance across Canada.

Practice data entry and formatting
Manipulate rows and columns

title: The Theatre Centre:  Far-Flung Peoples  ($20-$30)
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
The phone is ringing.

The roof is banging.

French downstairs.

English upstairs.

Caught in the middle: five people, one couch, and a landlord calling it an open-concept bedroom.

**Welcome to Far-Flung Peoples**, an award-winning, fast-paced, multilingual dark comedy set inside a crooked house in downtown Toronto, where its residents are squeezed into a living arrangement that would raise questions at City Hall, if City Hall were paying attention.

*Ticket link is below ($20-$30)*

The winner of the Norma Epstein Foundation Award and the Hamilton Fringe Best New Canadian Play Contest, *Far-Flung Peoples*, is funny until it is not.

We'll join our friends at ***Minor Punctuations Theatre*** for this!

https://minorpunctuationstheatre.com/our-team/

**TICKET link is here: (you're purchasing for Sunday November 8th @ 2pm)**

https://theatrecentre.org/event/far-flung-peoples/

Small venue space--just 50 seats!! General admission,

We'll meet in the CAFE before the performance.

title: Wychwood Clarinet Choir Performance
location: Forest Hill, Program Room
description:
Join us this fall for a beautiful performance from the Wychwood Clarinet Choir, Toronto's premier clarinet ensemble!
From their
website
: "Founded in 2009, the Wychwood Clarinet Choir is directed by conductor and clarinetist Michele Jacot. The members of the choir include skilled clarinetists of all ages who share a love of music making, friendship and fun. The choir’s instrumentation extends from the contrabass clarinet to the E flat sopranino, and they regularly perform new compositions and arrangements for the ensemble, many written by their own Composers’ Collective. They embrace the ideal of “music for life” and are committed to sharing our musical experience in educational settings and in the wider community."

Join us on the following Monday afternoons to discuss books in a friendly and social atmosphere: September 14th, October 19th, November 9th, and December 14th.

Martyr!
by Kaveh Akbar.
Martyr!
is the 2024 debut novel by Iranian-American poet Kaveh Akbar. It is a
New York Times
bestseller and the paper's 2024 "Best Books of the Year So Far." It was a finalist for the 2024
Waterstones Debut Fiction Prize
and shortlisted for the
National Book Award for
Fiction.
The novel follows Cyrus Shams, a newly sober, queer, Iranian-American who becomes consumed with the idea of martyrdom. With the musculature of poetry and incandescent ideas, images, and humour, the novel is an inedible and haunted searching. Guided by the voices of lost artists, poets, and kings, Cyrus embarks on a search that leads him to a terminally ill painter living out her final days in the Brooklyn Museum.
Participants can borrow a copy of the book from the Woodside Square branch upon registration.

Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.

title: Changing the Narrative: Toronto’s Indigenous – Settler History
location: Toronto Reference Library, 1st Floor, Beeton Hall
description:
Learn more about Toronto's multifaceted Indigenous history, which has often been ignored or minimized due to the telling of the region's history only from settler perspectives. Join us for a panel discussion about a public history project that worked with five local First Nations to create a more accurate and inclusive story of the region's past, and is transforming the way settlement of 19th century Ontario is represented at The Village at Black Creek (formerly Black Creek Pioneer Village).
Changing the Narrative: Reconnecting Settler and Indigenous Histories at Black Creek Pioneer Village was a collaborative project of York University historians, The Village at Black Creek, Jumblies Theatre, and the Mississaugas of the Credit, Chippewas of Rama, Six Nations of the Grand River, Chippewas of Georgina Island, and Mississaugas of Scugog Island First Nations.
This panel discussion will share research highlights, reflect on the process of collaboration, and explore how the project is expanding and enriching storytelling at one of the region’s prime living history museums.
The project’s findings have also been published in
Where Histories Meet: Indigenous and Settler Encounters in the Toronto Area
, by Victoria Freeman. The book explores this history from multiple perspectives in an accessible and richly illustrated format and includes excerpts from interviews with twenty Indigenous elders and knowledge keepers. It has been nominated for a
2026 City of Toronto Book Award
.
Panel members include:
Victoria      Freeman
, historical researcher and author of
Where Histories Meet:      Indigenous and Settler Encounters in the Toronto Area
.
Jennifer      Bonnell
, professor in the Department of History at York University and the      lead of the Changing the Narrative Project.
Allison      White
, curator at The Village at Black Creek (Toronto and Region      Conservation Authority).
Darin      Wybenga
, heritage interpreter for the Mississaugas of the Credit First      Nation, and member of the Research Committee for the Changing the      Narrative project.
Lauri      Hoeg
, Anishinaabe artist and cultural advisor from the Chippewas of      Georgina Island First Nation, and member of the Research Committee for the      Changing the Narrative project.
The panel discussion will last approximately 60 minutes, followed by a Q&A with audience members. No registration required.

title: Hank Idsinga: The High Road
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
TPL presents retired homicide detective and author Hank Idsinga in conversation with Wendy Gillis at the North York Central Library's Concourse Event Space.
In his bestselling memoir
The High Road: Confessions of a Homicide Cop
, Idsinga takes readers behind the crime scene tape and into the mean streets of Toronto's most notorious murders. Teaming up with partners including future police chief Mark Saunders, Idsinga built a reputation for excellent recall and sharp instinct, finding motive and method faster than most. As the public face of that investigation, Idsinga remained strong and compassionate before the cameras, even as the police force faced fierce criticism over its handling of the case.
How do homicide detectives carry the weight of the cases they never solve? What does real accountability within policing actually look like, and why does it matter? And what can three decades on the front lines of Toronto's worst crimes teach us about justice, institutional trust, and the human cost of violence?
Join veteran crime reporter Wendy Gillis in conversation with Hank Idsinga for a gripping, candid evening inside the world of Canada's most storied homicide unit.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

description:
Sometimes, a single grade can get inside your head and make you question your ability to succeed in your program. The pressure to earn high marks, often called “academic perfectionism”, is something many post-secondary students experience.
In this week’s session of YU & Balance, participants will explore how stress affects academic performance and learn practical strategies to manage it as you prepare for exam season. By the end of the session, participants will have tools to recognize stress, respond to it effectively, and protect your confidence during exams.
This session is part of a 6-week Recovery College series. For each session attended, participants will receive $5 on their YU-card. To receive the gift card, you must attend the full session (approximately 45–60 minutes). Unfortunately, we’re not able to provide gift cards for partial attendance. Gift cards will be emailed after the session to the same email address used to register and join the session.
Space is limited, and registration is offered on a first-come, first-served basis. title: ABCD Reads Body Language by Meg Howrey
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***[Body Language](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4801989)*** by Meg Howrey.
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/6325601387675648) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"Sloane, a former actress now working as a therapist, is determined to find a meaningful way through menopause, away from marketing schemes, possibly with the aid of psychedelics. Her sister Laurel is managing her own growing rage and restlessness while engaging in work at an environmental non-profit and raising teenagers. Nanette, the youngest, has answered a long-delayed religious calling and is living as a Novice in a convent. All three lives will be further disrupted when Sloane receives a call summoning her to their mother’s house, Laurel discovers possible evidence of her husband’s infidelity, and Nanette finds herself in the middle of a media frenzy after a spontaneous act of public prayer.
Soon, all three are reunited under their mother’s roof, and no one can seem to agree about anything beyond the Barbara has dementia, as did her mother and sister before her. Will it be an opportunity for the closed door of their very private mother’s inner life to crack open? A lesson in care; a shared responsibility that will be the making of this family, divided by large age gaps, parental divorce, and temperament? Or will a stunning revelation upend not only their mother’s remaining time, but divide the sisters permanently?
With razor-sharp prose and undeniable humor, acclaimed author Meg Howrey brings an American family in the midst of a painful crisis to unforgettable life, interrogating memory and emotional inheritance, the right of a woman’s autonomy, and the indelible bonds even the most disparate of sisters can share." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/244709885-body-language))

"Howrey is a reliably beautiful stylist, and her slyly funny prose and blade-sharp insights into human behavior really should put her in the same conversation as writers like Ann Patchett and Barbara Kingsolver. Though this novel hits some familiar beats, Howrey manages to haul in plenty of shimmering pearls on the perils and joys of womanhood—whatever that means.
A comfort meal of a novel: poignant and prismatic." (from [Kirkus](https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/meg-howrey/body-language-4/))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Hot Docs & Soulpepper Present: Everybody to Kenmure Street
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
When the government came for their neighbours, an entire community stood in the way.

A new monthly series in partnership with Hot Docs, bringing visionary documentary filmmaking from around the world to Toronto’s East End.

From executive producer Emma Thompson comes an inspiring and profoundly moving portrait of what everyday citizens are capable of in the face of injustice. In May 2021, a U.K. Home Office dawn raid triggered one of the most spontaneous and successful acts of civil resistance in recent memory. In Scotland’s most diverse neighbourhood, hundreds of residents rush to the streets to stop the deportation of their neighbours. The morning in Glasgow, the first day of Eid, started as any other. But when neighbors heard through community message networks that two local men were snatched up for deportation, hundreds of people left their daily lives to rush down to Kenmure Street and put their bodies on the line. Though mostly strangers and with almost no planning, this extremely diverse group organized themselves, taking on essential roles to allow the collective to achieve their goal: protecting their own from government forces going after the most vulnerable among them. Everybody to Kenmure Street reminds us of the power that is always inherent in the people.

More information and registration can be found here: https://soulpepper.ca/everybody-to-kenmure-street/ https://soulpepper.ca/everybody-to-kenmure-street/ .
