title: Nov 11 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Time, Date and Location**

Nov 11, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-november-11-2026)**

**Agentic RAG: Beyond Retrieve-and-Generate**

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the default pattern for grounding large language models in external knowledge, but most implementations still follow a rigid retrieve-once, generate-once pipeline — one that struggles with multi-hop questions, ambiguous queries, and knowing when its own retrieved context is insufficient. This talk introduces Agentic RAG, where retrieval is treated as an action within an agent's reasoning loop rather than a fixed upstream step.

We'll examine query decomposition and routing for breaking complex questions into targeted sub-queries, self-reflective and corrective retrieval loops that let an agent judge and re-query its own results, and tool-orchestration patterns (via MCP) that let retrieval sit alongside other agent actions like database lookups and API calls. Using a live architecture — evolving a standard RAG chatbot into an agentic, MCP-connected system — we'll walk through what changes in design, and where these systems introduce new failure modes: grounding drift, latency and cost from repeated retrieval loops, and cases where a simpler RAG pipeline still wins.

Attendees will leave with a practical framework for deciding when the added complexity of agentic RAG is worth it, and a set of design patterns for building it correctly.

*About the Speaker*

[Balaji Venkatasubramaniyar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/balaji-venkatasubramaniyar/) is a Technical Lead at Wisdom Infotech, leading a 15+ person engineering team delivering enterprise solutions. With 13+ years of experience in enterprise software and insurance technology, he specializes in agentic AI systems, RAG architectures, and vector databases.

**GeoAI for the Physical World: Earth Observation, Foundation Models, and Urban Digital Twins**

Earth observation provides a unique form of computer vision for understanding the physical world at city to continental scales. In this talk, I will show how satellite imagery, geospatial data, machine learning, and foundation-model representations can be combined to characterize urban environments and environmental conditions.

I will present UrbanScope Open, an open GeoAI digital-twin prototype integrating Earth observation with 3D buildings, vegetation, land-surface temperature, air quality, noise, population, and other urban data. I will also share lessons from my research using geospatial foundation-model embeddings for environmental prediction across Europe.

The talk will discuss how these approaches can contribute to increasingly multimodal AI systems capable of reasoning about real-world environments.

*About the Speaker*

[Cesar Alvarez](https://voxel51.com/events/cesar.alvarez@uni-a.de) is a researcher at the University of Augsburg working at the intersection of GeoAI, Earth observation, remote sensing, and environmental intelligence. His research applies machine learning, computer vision, and geospatial foundation models to problems including urban environments, climate risk, air quality, and agriculture.

**Can agents get curious?**

Most AI agents are good at answering a question once we tell them exactly what to look for. The harder problem is building agents that can explore a complex dataset autonomously: generating hypotheses, deciding which analyses are worth running, allocating additional compute when evidence is ambiguous, and knowing when they have enough evidence to stop.

In this talk, I’ll show an architecture for autonomous research agents that combines structured knowledge, iterative tool use, and explicit evidence tracking to turn open-ended questions into a sequence of testable investigations. I’ll discuss practical lessons from building and evaluating these systems, including why more test-time compute does not automatically produce better research and how provenance and evaluation can make long-running agents more reliable.

I’ll close with a live example of an agent exploring a dataset, revising its hypotheses, and choosing what to investigate next.

*About the Speaker*

[Srivatsa P](https://www.linkedin.com/in/srivatsa-p) is a member of technical staff at Sigma Computing, where he works on AI agents that reason over complex enterprise data. Previously, he worked on machine learning at Apple and conducted research at the MIT Media Lab; outside of traditional ML, he has also worked on mapping coral reefs through underwater imaging, which sparked an enduring interest in how intelligent systems make sense of messy real-world data.

title: Nov 11 - Toronto Physical AI Workshop and Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join us at the University of Toronto on November 11 for the Toronto Physical AI Workshop and Meetup, co-presented by Nebius and Voxel51.

Seats are limited, **[Pre-registration is mandatory.](https://voxel51.com/events/toronto-physical-ai-workshop-and-meetup-november-11-2026)**

**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 11, 2026
5:30 PM - 8:30 PM
The Conference Centre at U of T
Giovanni Room (2nd Floor)
89 Chestnut St.
Toronto, ON M5G 1R1

**Meetup Agenda**
*5:30–6:30 PM*

* Networking, food, drinks, and lightning talks

**Workshop Agenda**
This hands-on session uses DROID, a real-world robotics dataset loaded into FiftyOne as a native multimodal MCAP recording, and YOLO11n, fine-tuned live during the session.

*6:30–7:30 PM*

* Welcome + framing: from raw robot logs to a trained detector
* Explore a real DROID robotics recording in FiftyOne's native multimodal MCAP viewer: camera, proprioception, and language on one synced timeline, no ROS install required
* Curate: extract and browse frames from the recording, filter and deduplicate
* Compute embeddings on the curated frames; explore via similarity search and embeddings visualization (via Nebius Serverless AI Jobs)

*7:30–8:00 PM*

* Auto-label: open-vocabulary detection to generate bounding boxes for the robot gripper and target objects
* Train: fine-tune a YOLO11n detector on the auto-labeled frames (via Nebius Serverless AI Jobs)
* Evaluate results and close the loop: view predictions back on the original MCAP timeline

*8:00–8:30 PM*

* What else Nebius offers: Token Factory walkthrough — chat/vision models, fine-tuning, credits

title: The Writings of David Thompson on His Travels in North America
location: North York Central Library, Room 1, 2nd floor
description:
This presentation examines the historical Writings of David Thompson. Between 1784 and 1812, David Thompson (1770-1857) explored and traded over a vast expanse of western North America. Later in life, the surveyor and fur trader wrote what he called his
Travels
, a spectacular geographical and spirited intellectual journey of the Canadian experience. His story tells of a remarkable life in the fur trade but it also captures hid reflections on the land and the indigenous peoples of western North America.
Presented by Bill Moreau, editor of the three-volume work,
The Writings of David Thompson
.
Registration is encouraged but not necessary.

title: Common Hour: Celebrating the Canadian League of Composers: John Burge, Piano
location: Tribute Communities Recital Hall, 112 Accolade East Building, York University
description:
In celebration of the Canadian League of Composers 75th Anniversary in 2026, composer and pianist, John Burge presents a solo piano recital of music composed by many of the CLC past presidents. Starting with music by founding President, John Weinzweig, the program proceeds chronologically to current president, Tyler Versluis. The concert opens with a musical land acknowledgement, “Trillium,” composed by Indigenous-Canadian composer and CLC member, Beverley McKiver, and concludes with a rousing collective singing of O Canada. This all-Canadian concert promises to be an event of historical, cultural and artistic significance.
Thursday, November 12, 2026
12:30 – 1:30 p.m. 
Tribute Communities Recital Hall
FREE
Composer and pianist, John Burge ( https://sdm.queensu.ca/people/burge-john ), taught at Queen’s University, Kingston, Ontario, for 38 years before retiring as a Professor Emeritus in 2025. Many of Burge’s orchestral works, such as Snowdrift, The Canadian Shield and Rocky Mountain Overture, have been performed by orchestras across Canada and internationally. His string orchestra work, Flanders Fields Reflections, as recorded by Sinfonia Toronto, received the 2009 Juno Award for the Best Canadian Classical Composition. In 2014 he was inducted into the Royal Society of Canada for his achievements as a composer and support of the Arts in Canada. Having completed his Associate Diploma from the Royal Conservatory of Toronto in Piano Performance while still in high school, John Burge has continued to perform throughout his career, usually in presentations of his own music. Over the years, his piano music has been included in a number of conservatory music syllabi and he is in high demand as a music festival adjudicator. A passionate advocate for Canadian music, he served on the executive committee of the Canadian League of Composers from 1993-2007 (including eight years as President) and on the SOCAN Foundation board of directors from 2009-2025, as well as on the boards of several arts organizations in the Kingston area.

title: Imagining a Turtle Named Franklin by Brenda Clark
location: Lillian H. Smith, Lower Level- Auditorium
description:
Photo credit: Lee Higginson.
Join the Osborne Collection of Early Children's Books for our 19th Annual Sybille Pantazzi Memorial Lecture: Imagining a Turtle Named Franklin by Brenda Clark.
Award winning picture book illustrator, Brenda Clark is the original illustrator of the beloved Franklin the Turtle book series, by author Paulette Bourgeois. In this lecture, she will share how she became an artist and how Franklin was created. Brenda’s illustrations have played a key role in Franklin’s worldwide popularity, leading to the inspiration of the animated TV series, merchandise, spin-off books, a children’s garden on Toronto Island and a Canadian postage stamp. She will walk us through the process of designing and painting the art and explain how it takes some amazing teamwork to meet the challenges of Franklin’s success.
For the past 40 years, Brenda Clark has delighted children as the illustrator of the hugely successful Franklin the Turtle children’s book series. Over 70 million Franklin books have been sold in more than 30 languages worldwide, making it the single most successful picture book series in the history of Canadian publishing. In 2011, the archives of Brenda Clark were donated to the Osborne Collection of Early Children’s Books, and recognized by the Canadian Cultural Property Export Review Board as cultural property for its “Outstanding Significance and National Importance”. In 2014, Brenda was named a Member of the Order of Canada. She lives in Port Hope, Ontario.
Book signings will take place before the lecture from 5:00-6:00 pm on the 4th floor in the Osborne Collection.

title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Ghost Stories of Toronto: Séances & The World Wars
description:
Séances were all the rage a century ago. Having begun to fall out of fashion in the early 1900s, they experienced a resurgence after the deadly years of the First World War and the Spanish Flu as people held out hope they could still communicate with their lost loved ones. In the third lecture of this series by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore the history of séances during those turbulent times, from those who truly believed in their power, to the fraudsters who preyed on a grieving city, to the prime minister who took advice from the spirits of the dead.
About this event's guest:
Adam Bunch
Read More:
The Toronto Book of Love
The Toronto Book of the Dead
About this series:
You can learn a lot about Toronto through its ghost stories. Whether you believe in the supernatural or not, the tales we tell about spirits and spectres illuminate the true history of the city. They're often tied to dramatic stories of death and disaster, to fascinating historic sites, and to pivotal moments that helped shape our communities. In this series of talks by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore Toronto's past through tales of ghosts, séances and hauntings. Whether it's phantom horses from the War of 1812, the strange prime minister who believed in the occult, or the ghost who was arrested by the Toronto Police Morality Squad, these supernatural stories have a lot to teach us about the history of the place we call home.

description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
**The banjo visionary leads an all‑star ensemble through some new music and classic tunes, blending bluegrass roots with jazz and classical influences.**

We have a 15% off promo code--*at the TICKET link below. Join us at Koerner Hall in mid-November!*

YouTube teaser (with his All-Star band)\*\* The Flecktones.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6wQ3dAg_cpQ&t=17s

Over the last four decades, Béla Fleck has made a point of boldly going where no banjo player has gone before, a musical journey that has earned him 19 Grammys in nine different fields, including country, pop, jazz, instrumental, classical, and global music.

But his roots are in bluegrass, and that is where he returns with his band of all-star players, My Bluegrass Heart.

https://www.belafleck.com/

Taking its namesake from Fleck's 2021 Grammy Award-winning album, *My Bluegrass Heart*, the album was the third chapter of a trilogy which began with the 1988 album, *Drive*, and continued in 1991 with The Bluegrass Sessions. Fleck’s band spotlights a multi-generational gamut of the best of bluegrass players, all sporting a myriad of Grammy nominations, as well as gigantic piles of IBMA awards for their instruments: fiddler Michael Cleveland, mandolinist Dominick Leslie, Jeff Partin on dobro, bassist/multi-instrumentalist Mark Schatz, and Jake Stargel on guitar.

Participants who register for an experienced slot but are not actually experienced crocheters may not receive the help they require during the class, so please ensure you are registered under the correct ticket. Tickets JCCC Members: $30 Non-members: $40 Workshop 1 1:00 - 3:00 PM Buy Tickets Workshop 2 3:30 - 5:30 PM Buy Tickets *Tickets on sale October 2 @ 10AM Artist Bio Angela is a Therapeutic Recreation Specialist who teaches Inclusive Art and Crochet to kids and adults in the KW Region. On the side she runs her small business "So Craftful" where she sells cute crochet creations she makes in her free time at local fairs, markets and cons. title: Aki no Tabi | 秋の旅
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
Aki no Tabi — Autumn at the JCCC This fall, join us at the JCCC for a new seasonal experience celebrating Japanese and Japanese Canadian culture through creativity, connection, and hands-on activities. About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature-focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.

location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
Celebrate the beauty of autumn through clay in this hands-on ceramic workshop. Participants will learn to create small mamezara (豆皿) — Japanese bean dishes — inspired by the natural shapes, textures, and colours of the season. You'll have the opportunity to make 2–3 small dishes, choosing from autumn-inspired designs such as leaves and tree bark. These versatile pieces are perfect for pickles and side dishes, or as charming trinket trays for small treasures. Once your pieces are complete, you'll select your preferred glaze colour, and the studio will glaze and fire your work. Finished mamezara will be ready for pickup in approximately 4–6 weeks . Tickets JCCC Members: $75 Non-members: $85 Workshop 1 1:30 - 3:00 PM Buy Tickets Workshop 2 4:00 - 5:30 PM Buy Tickets *Tickets on sale October 2 @ 10 PM Artist Bio Helen Kong is the owner of Secret Teatime , a ceramic studio in Scarborough where she creates pottery and teaches intimate clay workshops and courses. A practitioner of Chado (the Japanese Way of Tea) as well as Chinese tea, Helen’s love of tea deeply informs her creative practice. She specializes in ceramic wares for Japanese and Chinese tea rituals, everyday living, and multisensory food experiences in restaurants and cafés. Through her work, Helen hopes to bring people together through tea and handmade culture, creating memories, stories, and vessels that can be cherished and passed down for generations.

title: Aki no Tabi Workshop: Crafting Our Narratives with Erica H. Isomura and Nico Koyanagi
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
Led by artist Erica H. Isomura and peer support worker Nico Koyanagi, this interactive workshop invites community members to reflect on their personal stories through writing prompts, dialogue, and a hands-on paper craft activity. Through group sharing, we hope to surface both shared and divergent community narratives — building deeper understanding and compassion for ourselves and one another. Participants will create a handmade "pocket altar" to take home: a small talisman to carry forward, encouraging continued reflection and intention-setting through the changing season ahead. Tickets Workshop from 1:30 PM to 4:00 PM JCCC Members: $10 Non-members: $20 Buy Tickets *Tickets on sale October 2 @ 10 AM Artist Bios Erica H. Isomura is an artist, writer, and educator whose work is rooted in community. She was raised by a Chinese Canadian mom and sansei dad on the west coast beside the Sto:lo (Fraser River). Erica's inter- and multi-disciplinary practice combines storytelling, book arts, printmaking, collage and mixed-media art with land-based and critical diasporic knowledge. Erica has taught community art, bookmaking, and creative writing workshops across Canada. She holds an MFA in Creative Writing from the University of Guelph. Nico Koyanagi is a mixed-race yonsei, registered social worker, community organizer, educator, and mediator who prioritizes connection and healing in all aspects of her work. She grew up as a settler in Nogojiwanong on Michi Saagiig Nishnaabeg territory (Peterborough, ON). Through her community work with the BIPOC Growing Collective, Mata Ashita, and Tsuru for Solidarity, Nico is interested in how we can live with more compassion, kindness, and care towards ourselves, each other, and the earth alongside challenging oppression in all forms. Images 1: Photo by Kayla Isomura 2: Erica H. Isomura (left) and Nico Koyanagi (right)

About Deepa Krishnan
Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling, that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.

title: Série Portraits et autoportraits: Du Symbolisme à l’Expressionnisme : le moi en question.
description:
En un temps où l’industrialisation est triomphante, certains peintres et écrivains sont, en cette fin du XIXe siècle, en proie à une inattendue inquiétude existentielle : le rationalisme explique-t-il à lui-seul le sens de la vie et de l’histoire ? Ces interrogations seront parfaitement résumées par le titre du tableau que Paul Gauguin exécute en 1898 :
D’où venons-nous ? Que sommes-nous ? Où allons-nous ?
De Van Gogh à George Grosz en passant par Edvard Munch, les peintres explorent alors dans leurs autoportraits ces champs d’inquiétude qui étreignent les consciences, en de fascinants tableaux hallucinés.
Cette conférence vous est proposée par Gilles Genty, historien de l’art, en partenariat avec l’
Alliance française de Toronto
.

title: Toronto's Ravines: Nature and History at Your Doorstep
location: Richview, Room A, 2nd Floor
description:
Toronto's ravine landscapes are not just a sanctuary for wildlife; they also protect the city against flooding and allow us to enjoy nature at our doorsteps. This presentation by the Toronto Field Naturalists shares how the ravines are changing over time; how they are responding to numerous pressures and how you can explore and help protect them.
Presenter Bio:
Ellen Schwartzel is a former president of the Toronto Field Naturalists, and she enjoys leading walks through Toronto's ravines.  Ellen's career in environmental policy included 23 years with the Environmental Commissioner of Ontario. She was Ontario's Deputy Environmental Commissioner for four years, until retiring in 2018.  Ellen’s academic training was in Botany, and she received her BSc and MSc at the University of Toronto.
This program is part of TPL's
Our Fragile Planet
program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​

title: In-Depth Intro to Woodworking Nov 15 [Sundays - 6 week Intensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
Description: 

 
 Suitable for beginners, this woodworking course is designed to teach you all that you need to get started in woodworking by learning both traditional, and modern techniques.

 Students will learn valuable hands-on skills working on instructor-lead projects using both hand and power tools.

 Projects are chosen to provide skills development in a natural progression from familiarity with the unique characteristics of wood, to basic essential techniques, to some more advanced topics.

 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course.

 

 Schedule : 

 Six three-hour weekly classes, Sundays 10am to 1pm. 

 Outcomes : 

 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 

 
- A complete understanding of the nature and properties of wood 

- Proficiency with traditional woodworking techniques

- Comfort working with chisels, planes, saws

- Proficiency with wood milling techniques

- Comfort with safe operation of power tools

- Familiarity with power planing, joiner, drill press, router and table saw 

- Dressing and laminating wood 

- Experience following project plans 

- Familiarity with joinery 

- Wood finishing, various treatments 

 
  Following this course, you'll be certified to use the woodshop. And you'll be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing knowledge on our Discord community.

 Certifications for all courses are valid for one year from the time that they are issued, and can be renewed at no cost with your active monthly membership within 3 months of their expiry. Certification renewal requires booking with an instructor, is conducted at the makerspace, and helps you keep your skills current. 

Useful for: furniture, cabinets, organisers, cutting-boards 
 
 
 
 Want to get notified next time classes are posted? 

 Join our mailing list!

title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: AI Snake Oil
location: Toronto Reference Library, Lower Level, Room B1
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
November’s book is
AI Snake Oil: What Artificial Intelligence Can Do, What It Can't, and How to Tell the Difference
by computer scientists Arvind Narayanan & Sayash Kapoor. Copies of the book are available in print,
eBook
&
eAudiobook
format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
"Confused about AI and worried about what it means for your future and the future of the world? You're not alone. AI is everywhere—and few things are surrounded by so much hype, misinformation, and misunderstanding. In AI Snake Oil, computer scientists Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor cut through the confusion to give you an essential understanding of how AI works, why it often doesn't, where it might be useful or harmful, and when you should suspect that companies are using AI hype to sell AI snake oil—products that don't work, and probably never will. While acknowledging the potential of some AI, such as ChatGPT, AI Snake Oil uncovers rampant misleading claims about the capabilities of AI and describes the serious harms AI is already causing in how it's being built, marketed, and used in areas such as education, medicine, hiring, banking, insurance, and criminal justice. The book explains the crucial differences between types of AI, why organizations are falling for AI snake oil, why AI can't fix social media, why AI isn't an existential risk, and why we should be far more worried about what people will do with AI than about anything AI will do on its own. The book also warns of the dangers of a world where AI continues to be controlled by largely unaccountable big tech companies. By revealing AI's limits and real risks, AI Snake Oil will help you make better decisions about whether and how to use AI at work and home."
In addition, we will be discussing Chapter 1 of
Atlas of AI: Power, Politics, and the Planetary Costs of Artificial Intelligence
by artificial intelligence and media researcher Kate Crawford.
Drop in. No registration required.

title: Python Essentials 1
location: Brookbanks, Lower Level Auditorium
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).

title: Practical 3D Print Nov 16 [Mondays - 6 Week Comprehensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
In this course at TTLMakerspace, you will go beyond basic 3D printing knowledge and be able to create custom designs. Learn to use CAD modelling to upgrade or build your own models, optimized for 3D print.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Starting with manual printer control, you will progress to custom modelling and even advanced techniques such as 3D scanning and reverse engineering.

 Schedule: 

 
 Six three-hour weekly classes, Mondays 6:00pm to 9:00pm.

 
 
 
 
 
 Outcomes: 
 
 
 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 
 
 
 
- A complete understanding of the steps needed to go from concept to completed part

- Experience and comprehension of parametric 3D modelling

- Knowledge of 3D printing best practices 

- Familiarity with scanning for 3D print 

- Principles of reverse engineering and part repair

- Understanding of the properties of different 3D printing filaments

- Use cases for SLA (resin) printing vs. FDM printing 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Following this hands-on course, you’ll be certified to use 3D printers and book time with the machines at the TTLMakerspace (with your membership). You will also be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing 3D printing & 3D modelling knowledge on our Discord community.

 Useful for: design prototyping, custom organizational tools, repairs, prop-making, decorations, fabrication tools

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 Want to get notified next time classes are posted? 

 Join our mailing list!

title: Tutankhamun: The Sensational Discovery
location: S. Walter Stewart, Meeting Room
description:
This year marks an important anniversary in the history of Egyptology .  On November 4th, 2026, it would be 104 years since Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon discovered the intact tomb of King Tutankhamun in 1922 - a discovery that continues to capture the public imagination.
Nearly a year after the complete collection went on display at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Cairo on November 1, 2025, Egyptology Specialist Sherine ElSebaie will take audiences back to the moment of its discovery.  Following the footsteps of the excavators, she will recount the story leading to the discovery of the tomb and explore the remarkable objects found in its two chambers during the initial excavation.

description:
Cliffcrest invites all to our Seniors Club! Hang out and enjoy games, engaging presentations and workshops on a variety of topics.
This Month: Birds in Winter
Winter is a harsh season, yet many birds stay in Toronto and survive. Why don’t they all fly south? How do they stay warm and find food and shelter? Which birds stay and which ones migrate? Learn about migrant birds and their incredible journeys, visiting birds who come to the city from their boreal and Arctic homes, and our resident birds who spend the long, cold winter months here.
Join Monika Croydon, avid local birder and member of the Toronto Ornithological Club, to find out how we can all help birds in winter, from providing feeders and creating bird-friendly gardens and homes, to supporting conservation and research as Citizen Scientists.

Presenter Bio:
Ellen Schwartzel is a former president of the Toronto Field Naturalists, and she enjoys leading walks through Toronto's ravines.  Ellen's career in environmental policy included 23 years with the Environmental Commissioner of Ontario. She was Ontario's Deputy Environmental Commissioner for four years, until retiring in 2018.  Ellen’s academic training was in Botany, and she received her BSc and MSc at the University of Toronto.

Job hunting is a job in itself: applications, deadlines, interviews, follow-ups. What if you could build your own AI-powered system to help you manage it?
In this hands-on class, you'll explore a job-hunting dashboard built with AI: how it tracks applications, sets automatic alerts for postings that match you, and practices interviews with you through role-play. You'll leave with the templates to build your own. We'll also talk about how employers screen applications, and how it can make things unfair. Come explore a tool that works for you, not the other way around.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.

description:
This special series of masterclasses offers dancers a rare opportunity to learn with three extraordinary flamenco artists, Óscar de los Reyes, Carmen Talegona, and El Yiyo.

Each workshop offers participants a deeper understanding of the art form’s power, precision, musicality, and emotional truth. The three artists brings a distinct voice, lineage, and approach, guiding dancers toward greater technical clarity, expressive range, and connection to rhythm, structure, and cante. Together, these masterclasses create a rich encounter with flamenco as a living, evolving art form — one that honours tradition while continuing to move boldly into the future.

Open to intermediate, advanced, and professional-level dancers, the workshops offer an inspiring environment for growth, exchange, and artistic discovery.

This year’s lineup spans both traditional flamenco from Andalusia and innovative collaborations at the crossroads of qawwali and Persian muqam, tracing the art form’s evolution from its regional roots to a global practice.

title: Entrepreneurship 101
location: Live on Zoom @ Zoom
description:
Join us for an introductory workshop on entrepreneurship designed specifically for graduate students and postdoctoral fellows. This session will introduce practical frameworks for translating research, technical expertise, and emerging ideas into potential innovations for real-world solutions.
Participants will learn about the entrepreneurial journey, explore the steps involved in moving from research to application, and discover resources available to support them along the way. No prior business experience or fully developed idea is required.
By the end of the workshop, participants will be able to:

Understand the foundational concepts of innovation and entrepreneurship and how they apply within a research context.
Identify opportunities to translate research findings, specialized knowledge, or technical expertise into practical solutions.
Apply introductory frameworks to assess a problem, explore potential users, and develop an early-stage idea.
Understand the key stages involved in moving from research or academic study toward innovation, commercialization, or venture creation.
Develop a more entrepreneurial mindset by approaching uncertainty through experimentation, iteration, and continuous learning.
Build confidence in communicating ideas, testing assumptions, and taking the first steps toward launching an initiative.
Identify relevant programs, tools, mentors, funding opportunities, and institutional resources that can support their journey.

title: Hope in Action: Building Hope: Reimagining Institutions for Human Flourishing (Continuing Education Free Webinar)
description:
In a time of precarity, fragmentation, burnout, and democratic uncertainty, what would be possible if we stepped outside of the constrictions of scarcity and austerity and oriented toward abundance to reimagine how our public-serving higher education institutions can be places where hope can become a force for collective renewal? 



In this webinar, Dr. Jessica Riddell (professor of Early Modern Literature at Bishop’s University and founder of the Hope Circuits Institute) will join Dr. David Sylvester (President and Vice-Chancellor of the University of St. Michael’s College) to discuss the transformative role that hope plays in building vibrant institutions.  



Drawing on her work with the Hope Circuits Institute and her forthcoming book, Hope Circuits Illuminated: Conversations with Luminaries Amid Collapse, Dr. Riddell will share practical tools, reflections and insights from engaging in thousands of hours of conversations with scholars, students, presidents, staff, artists, and public thinkers to explore how public educational institutions can reclaim their civic purpose and embrace the complexity of our world to imagine new futures. 



Part of the Hope in Action speaker series from USMC CE



Join Continuing Education at the University of St. Michael’s College for a free speaker series exploring how hope becomes action in sustainability, leadership, social impact, spirituality, education, technology, and the arts. 



Hope is not wishful thinking. It is the decision to engage with our world’s most urgent challenges and work toward meaningful change , from climate and culture to how we live our values in our workplaces and communities. 



Hope in Action brings together innovators, faculty, alumni, and leaders who are meeting urgent challenges with clarity, courage, and purpose. 



Come to be inspired. Leave ready to act.

Get a realistic overview of their financial responsibilities

title: Tutankhamun: The Sensational Discovery - Part 2
location: North York Central Library, Room 1 (2nd floor)
description:
This year marks an important anniversary in the history of Egyptology. On November 4th, 2026, it will be 104 years since Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon discovered the intact tomb of King Tutankhamun in 1922 - a discovery that continues to capture the public imagination.
Nearly a year after the complete collection went on display at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Cairo on November 1, 2025, Egyptologist Sherine ElSebaie will take audiences back to the time of its discovery. Following the footsteps of the excavators, she will conclude the story of the discovery and explore the remarkable objects found in the burial chamber and the treasury during the excavation of 1923.
Registration is encouraged but not required.

description:

While other sessions in the Native Plant Series explore how to grow native plants from seed, this session focuses on choosing the right plants for your garden and finding the best place to plant them. The right plant in the right place is key to growing a successful garden. Whether your space is sunny or shady, dry or exposed to road salt, there are native plants suited to every condition.
 
We’ll also share local sources for native plants, shrubs and trees. Fall is the perfect time to plan additions to your garden for next year, so come learn how to make the best choices for your space!
 
Wednesday, November 18, 6:30 to 8 p.m.
Registration: Public $20, TBG Members $15 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Toronto Master Gardeners
Toronto Master Gardeners (TMG) is a volunteer not-for-profit organization that shares current, science-based horticultural information with the gardening public through various channels, including in person, in print, through the media, and online. Our committed volunteers support and inspire the community, and continually update the sound knowledge required to help them. Learn more and ask your questions Toronto Master Gardeners – Helping Gardeners.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Rachel Cusk: Life of M
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Critically acclaimed author Rachel Cusk shares her irresistible new novel.
Life of M introduces us to movie star M, one of the most recognizable faces of our time, whose image has been ubiquitous since she was a child.
With such fame, her life has the appearance of freedom: people are instantly obliging, spaces are altered to accommodate her, time can be rearranged. M may live in the same places as real people. She may meet her friends or collect her children from school or walk her dogs as they do. But it seems the rules of reality have melted away.
Now, a writer has decided to pay close attention to M’s life in the hope of understanding who she really is. It is hard not to feel ugly next to M, hard not to feel insignificant. But what truths―about the very experience of living―might this proximity allow the writer to briefly capture?
Rachel Cusk speaks with Sheila Heti about Life of M, an astonishing new novel about fame, power, beauty, and truth
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

Part of the Aga Khan Museum’s 12th annual Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World, join us for a film screening that celebrates the legacy of Farruquito, one of the greatest flamenco dancers of this century.

Farruquito is celebrated as the finest flamenco dancer of his generation. He belongs to a legendary dynasty of bailaores (dancers). At only 20, he was already at the height of his success, captivating audiences around the globe from New York to Tokyo – with his extraordinary talent, yet the shadows of his family’s tumultuous history loomed large.

The film follows Farruquito’s journey through triumph and tragedy, focusing on a pivotal moment that changes everything — a tragic accident that leads to the death of a pedestrian and lands him in prison. This harrowing experience forces him to confront the demons of his past and the heavy burden of his family’s legacy.

description:
Join us for an introduction to Sleep Qigong & Self-Acupressure!
Sleep issues can occur at different times during our lives in a variety of ways and for different reasons. You might have trouble falling asleep; perhaps you can fall asleep easily but wake up several times throughout the night; you might fall asleep but wake up too early feeling you haven’t slept quite enough; or you suffer from insomnia. Stress, anxiety, depression, age, worry, and other factors can all contribute to sleep complications.
 
In this session, I will demonstrate and guide you through some holistic and non-invasive ways to deal with sleep issues. They will include simple self-acupressure, gentle qigong, helpful tips, and calming breathing exercises.
 
Whether you experience occasional or chronic sleep problems, this session can provide you with some alternative ways to deal with it.
Thursday, November 19, 10 to 11:30 a.m.
Registration: Public $25, TBG Member $20 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About David Leopold
Sifu David Leopold has been practicing, studying, researching and teaching martial and healing arts since 1994.
 
In 1999, Sifu David achieved his black belt in Shaolin Kung Fu. Since 1999, Sifu David has received numerous certifications in Tachi and weapon forms, and seven Qigong routines. In 2009, Sifu David received his Usui Reiki master certification from the Naturopathic School of Medicine in Toronto.
 
In 2012, Sifu David travelled to China to compete in the International Wushi Competition in Shanghai. He brought home 2 gold and a bronze medal.
 
By combining all these modalities and experiences, Sifu David brings a unique style of teaching that includes technique, philosophy, and practicality. Sify David’s approach to teaching is relaxed and he believes Taichi and Qigong practice should be useful in everyday life and enjoyable to do.
 
Sifu David has a passion for martial and healing arts. His holistic approach to wellness includes physical, emotional, spiritual and nutritional well-being. Sifu David continues to improve his skills as a practitioner, teacher/ mentor, and hopes to teach for the rest of his life.
 
Sifu David’s words of wisdom:
 
“To be a master of what you do, you must first be a master unto yourself.”

title: Nov 19 - Visualizing and Debugging Hugging Face's LeRobot Data
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
This workshop is a hands-on tour of what actually breaks when you load real LeRobot datasets, and how Voxel51's native LeRobot support in FiftyOne catches it.

**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 19, 2026
9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/lerobot-workshop-november-19-2026)**

Robot learning data doesn't look like the data that trains most vision-language models. It's temporal, low-dimensional in the parts that matter most, embodiment-specific, and expensive to collect, and increasingly, it's shipped in Hugging Face's LeRobot format. But packaging robot data consistently isn't the same as being able to see it: episodes hide broken metadata, silently dropped sensor modalities, and mismatched schemas between robots that look identical on paper.

Starting from the core differences that make robot data hard (temporal structure, proprioception, action grounding, embodiment heterogeneity, data scarcity), we'll move into live debugging: a metadata bug that broke multiple dataset imports, sensor streams that vanish without an error, and two robots running an identical benchmark whose data is structurally incompatible. By the end, you'll know what to check before you trust a LeRobot dataset, and how to actually look inside one.

description:
Always wanted to learn to cook, draw, knit, fix a bike, or speak another language, but have trouble sticking to it? What if you had a personal AI tutor?
In this class, learn how AI can become your personal tutor for something you love, or something new you want to fall in love with. title: The Ishizue Award Dinner 2026
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
The JCCC Board of Directors is pleased to announce that the 8th Ishizue Award and accompanying dinner will be held on Thursday November 19, 2026. The Ishizue Award acknowledges and expresses our appreciation and respect to members or friends who have made exceptional contributions to the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. The name Ishizue, meaning cornerstone or foundation, pays tribute to the 75 families who, at significant personal financial risk, guaranteed the original mortgage on the JCCC at 123 Wynford Drive in the early 1960’s. These families provided the foundation upon which the JCCC was built, and their support for the JCCC will forever be recognized as the cornerstone for who we are as a community. The recipients of this annual award are a very distinguished group of people who have each made significant life contributions to the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. They are: Ken Fukushima Harry Kawabe Akiko Maruoka David Ohashi (Post humous) Connie Sugiyama David Tsubouchi We cordially invite you to honour these distinguished award recipients at an intimate and elegant dinner on Thursday November 19th at 6:30pm at the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. Black tie optional. Tickets are $180 each (plus HST) . Maximum of 10 guests per table. To purchase tickets please order through the button below or in person at the JCCC, starting September 21, 2026, and ending November 9, 2026. Please contact Sharon Marubashi for any further information by email or phone (647-291-4751). On behalf of all of the directors of the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre, we look forward to spending a special evening of recognition and celebration together. Purchase Ticket

title: Qawwali Flamenco
location: Massey Hall, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
From Pakistan to Andalusia, musical traditions have crossed paths, met, nourished one another, and blended so thoroughly that between the volcanic power and virtuosity of qawwali singing and the hypnotic lyricism of flamenco, distances fade and similarities naturally emerge.

Qawwali Flamenco marks the long-awaited return of the celebrated collaboration between Pakistani qawwali master Faiz Ali Faiz and flamenco guitar virtuoso Juan Gómez “Chicuelo.”

Following their acclaimed first collaboration a decade ago, Faiz and Gómez reunite to deepen a remarkable artistic dialogue. The first chapter of their Qawwali Flamenco journey explored the relationship between human beings and their beloved; this new creation turns toward the connection between humanity and the divine.

title: Adaptive Ceramic Histories
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
Adaptive Ceramic Histories                                                                          
        
    




	

	

	


			
Events
	









	

    
        
             
                
                    

November 20, 2026 – March 29, 2027
The Hilary and Galen Weston Foundation Hall. Ground Floor
Included with admission. Free for Gardiner Members.



                
                    
    



    
         
    




	


  Get Tickets



  Become a Member






    
         
    




	



    
        
             
                
                    Curated by Alexandra Box, Gardiner Museum Curatorial Resident 
Engage in an exploration of materially mediated dynamics of care and adaption. Adaptive Ceramic Histories presents an expansive way of looking at histories of medical and adaptive ceramics created for sick or disabled users. The exhibition invites you to delve into the design of care from the vantage point of users, departing from traditional histories of medicine centering on medical professionals. Instead, it considers the possibilities of pleasure and metaphor to build a more fulsome knowledge of patient care to craft the future. 
Adaptive Ceramic Histories features objects from the Gardiner Museum’s permanent collection alongside loans to highlight the importance of ceramic materials at different moments in the history of Western medicine from the 17th century to the present day. 
The Gardiner Museum Curatorial Residency is made possible through the generous support of the Rebanks Family. 

                
                    
    





    
         
    




    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    About the Curator
                    
                
                
                    Alexandra Box
                    
                
                
                    Alexandra Box is an arts professional and artist. She has been awarded fellowships and artist residencies through Medalta Potteries, Salt Spring Arts Council, and Point Gallery. Alexandra is a curatorial participant in the Knowledge Incubator & Mentorship Initiative through Redefine Arts. Her writing has been published by Hearth, Peripheral Review, and The Capilano Review. Alexandra serves on the Board at Forest City Gallery and is a contributor to the Media Collaboratory. She holds a BFA (2020) in ceramics and curatorial practices from Emily Carr University and an MA (2024) in Art History from the University of Toronto.

title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

Her seminar series, web site and print/electronic tools are recognized as key long term care educational resources for Canadian families.
Karen is a Certified Professional Consultant on Aging (CPCA).

title: Orhan Pamuk's The Museum of Innocence: Novel and Museum
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Nobel Prize-winner Orhan Pamuk speaks about the creation of Istanbul's Museum of Innocence.
Renowned Turkish novelist and Nobel Prize-winner Orhan Pamuk joins celebrated museum and cultural planning leader, Gail Lord, for an extraordinary conversation about one of the most singular acts of imagination in contemporary literature and museology: the creation of Istanbul's Museum of Innocence.
Conceived in tandem with his acclaimed novel of the same name, Pamuk's museum houses the fictional world of his characters Kemal and Füsun in a real, physical space — a small house in Istanbul filled with everyday objects, each one tied to a moment in the novel. The result is a haunting blur between fiction and reality, where a love story lives on not only on the page, but in glass display cases, drawers, and rooms visitors can walk through.
How does one curate a museum for people who never existed? What does it mean to give physical form to memory, longing, and melancholy — the very textures of a novel? And what challenges arise when an author becomes a museum-maker, translating narrative into space, object, and atmosphere?
Orhan Pamuk sits down with Gail Lord, co-founder of Lord Cultural Resources and one of the world's leading museum planners, to discuss the twin creation of the novel and the museum, the ethereal act of turning fiction into physical experience, and what he hoped visitors would feel wandering through the rooms of a story. The conversation will also turn to Pamuk's evolving philosophy of museums — the ideas first laid out in his "Modest Manifesto for Museums" — exploring his belief in small, intimate institutions that honor individual and everyday stories over the grand, monumental narratives so often privileged by national museums.
The discussion will also look ahead to Pamuk's second museum project, currently in development, in which he continues to explore the relationship between storytelling, memory, and collected objects. Building on the foundations laid by the Museum of Innocence, this new endeavor promises to further test the boundaries between literature and lived space, offering fresh insight into how narrative can be translated into an immersive, tangible experience.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Blackbird: In the Footsteps of Ziryab
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Blackbird: In the Footsteps of Ziryab makes its world premiere as a bold new multidisciplinary performance celebrating the enduring connections between cultures through oral and artistic traditions. Led by Artistic Director Amir Amiri, the Amir Amiri Ensemble, featuring Óscar de los Reyes and Esperanza Soria, the performance brings together Canadian and Spanish Andalusian artists in a powerful artistic dialogue. Connected through centuries of migration, poetry, rhythm, and memory, the performance explores a shared cultural legacy while embracing new creative expression. The essentials of flamenco are all present: voice, complex rhythm, and dance.

This presentation ultimately asks how music travels through history, how cultures reshape one another, and how artists continue to carry ancient knowledge into contemporary life. The project seeks to illuminate the enduring connections between Persian and Andalusian artistic worlds, while creating a contemporary performance grounded in research, artistic integrity, and shared humanity.

title: Who Should Own AI? Building Public AI

description:
If AI becomes as important as roads, electricity, or libraries, who should own it? Who decides what it's used for? Who gets access and to say no?
This panel discussion will include speakers building public-interest AI, working in civic tech, and organizing communities affected by AI decisions. We'll explore what's already being built, from open models and public compute to community-owned data, and what's being privatized. You'll get to draft your own "public AI requirements" and see what others think should be guaranteed to everyone. The future of AI is being decided now; this is a chance to have a say in it.
Featuring:
Alex Olson
, Director of University of Toronto’s Centre for Analytics & AI Engineering
Khasir Hean
, Founder of Technologists for Democracy, Machine Learning engineer
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

title: Theatre at York presents Casimir and Caroline
description:
Casimir and Caroline by Ödon von Horváth ( https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%96d%C3%B6n_von_Horv%C3%A1th ) – Adapted by Paolo Santalucia, Holgar Syme with The Howland Co. From an original translation by Holgar Syme
Casimir and Caroline is a play about love in the cold atmosphere of modern capitalism. We follow these ultra star-crossed lovers, as they navigate clingy co-workers, sketchy best friends, questionable HR representatives, the playboy boss, that powerhouse from the Montreal office and those beautiful few who might actually possess an ounce of wisdom. They all desperately long for something more. None of them can say what that might be. But at least their lives look good on Instagram.

title: Flamenco: Made in Canada presents Duende Al Nur
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Duende al Nur , meaning “Duende toward the light,” is an immersive flamenco work where light, shadow and fire transform the dancing body.

Performed on a luminous plexiglass platform, the piece explores light as a sacred, living force rising from beneath the dancer. From darkness, the body is awakened by illumination. Breath becomes pulse, pulse becomes rhythm, and rhythm becomes flamenco. Through footwork, castanets, zills, breath and silence, Carmen Romero moves through a ritual journey of awakening and renewal. Rooted in the emotional power of duende and the Arabic resonance of nur, the work becomes a passage through memory, prayer, rhythm and transformation.

The work draws from flamenco’s emotional intensity, rhythmic complexity and theatrical power while opening the performance space to Arabic resonance, sacred illumination and immersive sound. Rather than presenting cultural influence literally, Duende al Nur approaches these elements as echoes, atmospheres and poetic points of connection.

description: FALL/WINTER HIKING The Forks of the Credit is a part of the Bruce Trail and also the Niagara Escarpment Biosphere. There had been a mill in the Cataract area since 1820 and in 1885 John Deagle bought the mill and converted it into a hydro generating station which was later purchased by Ontario Hydro and eventually shut down in 1947. title: Look to Windward - Ian M. Banks
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi all,

So glad to have our Iain M. Banks selection finalized for November. As we’ve discussed previously, the books in the Culture series are connected, but don’t necessarily need to be read in order. The Club really enjoyed Book 2, *The Player of Games*, and I’m curious to see where in the universe we land with Book 7, 2000’s *Look to Windward*.

[sophyanempire](https://sophyanempire.wordpress.com/2012/03/08/look-to-windward-iain-m-banks-orbit-2000/) has a solid review of this entry in the Culture series, calling *Look to Windward* “exciting, tense, sad and heroic.” She notes that from there, “the book grows in scope, showing multiple perspectives, almost all of them from a non-human alien point of view.”

[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/books/2000/sep/02/sciencefictionfantasyandhorror.iainbanks) also has a great review from when the book was first published. Phil Daoust writes that “Banks has tremendous fun with his giant canvas” in *Windward*.

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/B9NMnC2F). Join us and keep the conversation going.

A reminder that Book Club takes a break each October, so while Look to Windward has a fairly large page count, we’ll essentially have two months to read our pick.

Cheers,

Jon

title: Sound and Sense: Jewish Music @York presents Pursue Peace
location: Tribute Communities Recital Hall @ Accolade East Building 83 York Boulevard, Toronto
description:
Contemporary Chamber Music by Canadian Jewish Composers
Album Release Celebration Concert
York University’s Koschitzky Centre for Jewish Studies ( https://www.yorku.ca/cjs/ ) and the Department of Music ( https://ampd.yorku.ca/department-of-music/ ) in the School of the Arts, Media, Performance and Design ( https://ampd.yorku.ca/ ) invite you to the opening of the fifth season of Sound and Sense: Jewish Music at York, with a special release concert celebrating Pursue Peace, the initiative’s debut album. The program brings together the work of three distinguished Canadian composers and leading performers in an evening of music shaped by memory, identity, history, and the many ways music gives voice to human experience.
Released by New Focus Recordings, the New York-based independent label devoted to contemporary and creative music, Pursue Peace features composers Noam Lemish ( https://www.noamlemish.com/bio ) (ON), Sid Robinovitch ( https://www.sidrobinovitch.ca/ ) (AB), and James Rolfe ( https://www.jamesrolfe.ca/bio/ ) (ON), whose music spans intimate works for violin and piano, string quartet and clarinet, and a larger work for choir, soprano and ensemble.
More than three years in the making, the album is the culmination of an ongoing artistic collaboration at York, bringing the work of Sound and Sense: Jewish Music at York to a wider audience. We invite you to join the ongoing conversation through music and celebrate this milestone with us.
Sunday, November 22, 2026
Tribute Communities Recital Hall 
3:00 p.m.
FREE

title: Los Magníficos
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
“Los Magníficos” is a once-in-a-lifetime encounter with the greatness of contemporary flamenco. Five outstanding artists come together in a unique performance where singing, dance, guitar, and piano reach their highest expression.

Sandra Carrasco, one of the most important voices of the moment, takes us to the very heart of flamenco. David de Arahal captivates audiences with his mastery of the guitar, while Andrés Barrios transforms the piano into pure emotion. Dancer “El Yiyo” embodies the power and intensity of flamenco, joined by Carmen “La Talegona,” whose artistry and magnetic stage presence bring elegance, strength, and depth to this extraordinary encounter.

Prepare for an intense and magnetic journey, where energy and sensitivity intertwine in an explosion of talent. “ Los Magníficos” is not just a performance; it’s a unique opportunity to witness the union of some of the finest artists of our time in a moment destined to remain forever in the memory of flamenco art.

title: Get Things Done with AI: Build Your Own Productivity System
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if your to-do list could check in on you, notice what's been stuck for weeks, and offer to help instead of just sitting there?
In this class, you'll explore a personal productivity system built around an AI agent and a weekly-review practice. See how the agent loads goals, counts what actually got done, flags the items that keep slipping, and drafts next week's plan. It can support without cheerleading, asking "Why has this been stuck for three weeks? Here are your options." You'll try it yourself with a practice set of goals, and leave with the plain-text templates and a clearer map of how an AI might support you, ready to build your own system at home.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.

title: Python Essentials 1
location: Brookbanks, Lower Level Auditorium
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.

In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. title: Bee-ing a Pollinator Protector: Plan Now for a Buzzing Spring Garden
location: Riverdale
description:
Saving the bees is an environmental cause that resonates deeply with Canadians.  While most of us might not be thinking about bees this time of year, our actions during the colder months can still support these pollinators, particularly native bees, which are crucial and threatened by climate change, habitat loss, and other pressures.
In honour of the late bee scientist Sheila Colla, this presentation will offer practical tips on planting and maintaining gardens that provide beautifully blooming habitat for pollinators, with a particular focus on how native plants support wild bees.
Presented by
Lorraine Johnson
, who co-authored
A Garden for the Rusty-Patched Bumblebee
with Sheila Colla, as part of TPL's environmental program series,
Our Fragile Planet
, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​
Free. Register for a reminder.

title: ABCD Reads Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***Yesteryear*** by Caro Claire Burke.
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/4849281772290048) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"A traditional American woman, a beautiful wife and mother who sells her pioneer lifestyle of raw milk and farm-fresh eggs to her millions of social media followers, suddenly awakens cold, filthy, and terrified in the brutal reality of 1855—where she must unravel whether this living nightmare is an elaborate hoax, a twisted reality show, or something far more sinister." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/yesteryear/))

"The chasm between social media and reality runs deep and dark in Caro Claire Burke’s debut novel, “Yesteryear,” which crawls into the psyche of a tradwife influencer so maddening and mesmerizing that Anne Hathaway has already signed on to play her in the movie adaptation.
“Sometimes it actually made me sick,” Natalie Heller Mills narrates, “how perfect my life was, and how good I was at living it.” Note her use of the past tense." (from [New York Times Book Review](https://archive.ph/WHSQ6#selection-753.0-764.0))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Jeff Chang: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents award-winning author Jeff Chang in conversation with [HOST TBC] at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon, celebrating what would have been Bruce Lee's birthday.
More than half a century after his death, Bruce Lee remains as towering a figure as ever, the man who popularized martial arts in the West, became a bridge between Eastern and Western culture, and was poised to conquer Hollywood when he died suddenly at age thirty-two. But in the decades since, his legend has eclipsed the man. Forgotten is the immigrant, the fighter, the seeker, the teacher, the father grappling with exile and belonging in a country that questioned his right to simply exist.
In his epic new cultural biography
Water Mirror Echo: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
, acclaimed author Jeff Chang recovers the man behind the icon. Drawing on in-depth interviews with Lee's closest intimates, thousands of newly available personal documents, and dozens of rare photographs from the family archive, Chang traces Lee's remarkable journey: a charismatic child star turned delinquent teen fighter in Hong Kong, exiled alone to America, who transformed personal struggle into a philosophy of movement and being. Chang reveals how Lee's rise didn't just create a Hollywood legend, it helped birth something even more enduring: the very concept of Asian America.
Join Jeff Chang for a special evening honoring Bruce Lee's birthday, offering a stirringly human portrait of the icon, the immigrant, and the movement he unknowingly ignited.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

Jeff Chang

title: Wednesday Afternoon @ the Movies: One False Move
location: Weston, Program Room. Lower Level.
description:
Join us on Wednesday afternoon at the library for a screening of One False Move movie.
A small-town police chief conceals an explosive secret. A pair of ruthless drug dealers leave a bloody trail in their wake as they make their way from Los Angeles to Arkansas. And an enigmatic woman is caught in the middle. The way these desperate lives converge becomes a masterclass in slow-burn tension thanks to the nuanced direction of Carl Franklin, whose haunting debut feature travels a crooked road across America’s most fraught divisions—urban and rural, Black and white—while imbuing noir conventions with a wrenching emotional depth.

title: Vibe Coding: Make Your Own Interactive Story with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if you could write a story where the reader chooses what happens, like a branching adventure, a mystery, or a game, and have AI build it with you?
In this class, you'll learn "vibe-coding": using an AI coding assistant to build your own interactive story or simple game. You'll design the branches, describe the rules in plain language, test for the tricky edge cases (what if the player picks the weird option?), and end up with a single file you can share with anyone. Just a story you want to tell. This is the playful sibling of the practical vibe-coding workshop.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.
About the AI Tools Used in This Program
This program includes activities that use agentic AI tools (listed below) on library laptops.
You do not need to create your own account for this program.
Participants are encouraged to follow the Resident’s guidance throughout sessions, which include best practices on using AI.

The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Recovery College- Balance & Build Week 6: Managing Academic Stress & Exam Anxiety
description:
All it takes is one below average or even just average mark to get inside your head and begin doubting yourself and your ability to succeed in your program. The pressure to get high marks, or academic perfectionism, is commonly experienced by students in university. This week, students will explore the effects of stress on academic performance, learn strategies for managing and coping with stress to tackle exam season.
